docs.title: TestFlow Backend Docs
docs.text:
TestFlow is an online assessment platform. People and organizations use it to create tests (often with AI), invite participants, run timed attempts, and score the answers automatically. It also builds AI learning roadmaps and offers an AI assistant that can answer questions about your tests and results.

The backend is one NestJS application (a "modular monolith"). It uses PostgreSQL for data, Redis for caching and rate limiting, RabbitMQ for background jobs, Socket.IO for realtime messages, and LangChain/LangGraph to talk to LLM providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google).

New to the team?

Read these four pages in order: Overview, Getting Started, Architecture, then the ERD. After that, jump to the feature page you are working on.

docs.title: Start here

docs.title: Feature design (HLD)
docs.text:
"HLD" means high-level design. Each page explains one feature: the flow, the states, and the main files.

Page What you will learn Authentication & Users Signup, login, Google sign-in, JWT access/refresh tokens, email verification, password reset. RBAC Roles and permissions, for the platform and inside organizations. Organizations Creating organizations, members, org roles, invitations, and bulk CSV invites. Assessments The assessment lifecycle (draft, ready, published), participants, invitations, templates, and prompts. Questions & Tags Question types (MCQ, coding, descriptive), the question bank, and tags. AI Assessment Generation How a prompt becomes a full assessment through background section jobs. Attempts Starting, answering, submitting, and reviewing an attempt; leaderboard and analytics. Evaluation How submitted attempts are scored per question type, in the background. Code Execution How candidate code runs on Piston or OnlineCompiler.io and is judged against test cases. AI Layer The chat model factory, the model registry, LangGraph graphs, prompts, structured output, and LLM audit. AI Assistant & Tools The conversational assistant and the read-only tools it can call. Commerce, Payments & Webhooks Plans, subscriptions, usage quotas, Razorpay checkout, and webhooks. Learning Roadmaps AI-built learning graphs, progress tracking, and roadmap assessments. Realtime Events The Socket.IO gateway: auth, rooms, events, and live code runs. Jobs & Schedulers The jobs table, job status, retries, and cron tasks. Notifications Transactional email over SMTP and the email templates. Platform Services Rate limiting, feature flags, health checks, stats, newsletters, support tickets, and file storage.

docs.title: Glossary
docs.text: Term Meaning Assessment A test. It has a title, a time window, a duration, a marking scheme, sections, and questions. Its status moves draft → ready → published. Section A part of an assessment that holds questions of one type (for example, 10 MCQs). AI generation creates one background job per section. Question One item to answer. The types are mcq (multiple choice), coding (write code that passes test cases), and descriptive (free text, graded by an LLM). Question bank The shared questions table. Questions are copied ("snapshotted") into an assessment, so later edits do not change old tests. Participant A user linked to an assessment. Status is invited, active, or revoked. The creator is also a participant but does not use a seat. Invitation A request to join something. Assessment invitations add participants. Organization invitations add members, one by one or from a CSV file. Attempt One sitting of an assessment by a participant. Status moves in_progress → submitted → evaluating → evaluated. A reviewer can mark it rejected. Response A participant's answer to one question inside an attempt. Evaluation Scoring a submitted attempt. It runs in the background and is split by question type. Template A ready-made starting point. Assessment templates define sections and question counts. Roadmap templates give a starting point for a learning roadmap. Assessment prompt A saved, reusable prompt for AI generation. It can be public or private and can carry tags. Tag A label (for example, "javascript") used to group and search content. Learning roadmap An AI-generated graph of topics (nodes and edges) that a learner works through, with progress tracking and practice assessments per node. Organization (org) A team account. Members have an org role: org_owner, org_admin, or org_member. Many routes can act "inside an org" through the x-organization-id header or an :orgUid path segment. Platform role A role that applies across the whole platform, such as super_admin. It is separate from org roles. Permission A named right such as questions:create. Roles hold permissions. Routes ask for them with @Permissions() or @OrgPermissions(). Plan A product tier. Each plan has versions, and each version lists features with limits (for example, how many AI assessments you can generate). Subscription A user's link to a plan version. Status is PENDING, ACTIVE, PAST_DUE, or CANCELLED. Usage / quota How much of a plan feature a user has used. AI generation spends quota and gives it back if the generation fails. Order / Payment An order is what the user is buying. A payment is the Razorpay charge for it. Razorpay webhooks confirm payments. Job A row in the jobs table that tracks one background task (generate a section, evaluate an attempt, import invitations). Clients poll GET /v1/jobs/:id to see progress. Consumer A class that listens to a RabbitMQ queue and runs the jobs that arrive there. AI model A row in the ai_models table. It names a provider and a model, plus the env vars that hold its API key and base URL. The user's plan decides which model they get. LLM audit A row in llm_audit that records one LLM call (model, tokens, timing) for cost tracking and debugging. AI assistant / conversation A chat with an LLM that can call tools to read your assessments, attempts, and roadmaps. Messages travel over the WebSocket. Feature flag A switch that turns a feature on for some roles (for example, beta_tester). Envelope The standard JSON shape of every response: { success, message, data, meta? }.

docs.title: API Design — Scenario Index (Superseded)
docs.text:
This page previously mapped business scenarios to a planned tests/submissions-based API (referencing a api-design/v2.md that was never created). The backend that was actually built uses a different domain model (assessments/attempts/questions, plus commerce/payments/webhooks) — see:

  • API Design v1 — the full, current endpoint reference
  • Data Access Patterns — scenario → query mapping for the current schema
  • Architecture — module map and request pipeline
  • ERD — current schema

This page is not linked from the site navigation and is kept only so old links don't 404.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
TestFlow's backend is a modular monolith: one NestJS app, one deployable, split into feature modules under src/. All modules share one PostgreSQL database. Slow work (LLM calls, grading, CSV imports) runs in the background through RabbitMQ, in the same codebase.

Why a monolith? The team is small, features touch each other a lot (assessments, attempts, AI, plans), and one deploy is simple. Module boundaries keep the code organized, and RabbitMQ lets slow work scale separately (see CONSUMER below) without splitting into microservices.

flowchart LR
    client["Web client"] -->|"HTTPS REST /v1"| api["NestJS app"]
    client -->|"Socket.IO"| api
    api --> pg[("PostgreSQL")]
    api --> redis[("Redis")]
    api -->|"publish and consume"| mq[["RabbitMQ"]]
    api --> llm["LLM providers"]
    api --> runner["Code runner"]
    api --> smtp["SMTP"]
    api --> s3["S3"]
    rzp["Razorpay"] -->|"webhook"| api
    api --> rzp

docs.title: 2. Request pipeline
docs.text:
Every HTTP request passes the same steps. Guards are registered with APP_GUARD in src/app.module.ts. The pipe and the filter are registered in src/main.ts.

flowchart TB
    req["HTTP request"] --> g1["1. JwtAuthGuard"]
    g1 --> g2["2. RateLimitGuard"]
    g2 --> g3["3. RolesGuard"]
    g3 --> g4["4. OrgContextGuard"]
    g4 --> g5["5. PermissionGuard"]
    g5 --> pipe["ValidationPipe - DTO checks"]
    pipe --> ctrl["Controller"]
    ctrl --> svc["Service and domain rules"]
    svc --> ser["Serializer - entity to DTO"]
    ser --> ok["new ApiResponse - success envelope"]
    g1 -. "throws" .-> filter["HttpExceptionFilter"]
    g5 -. "throws" .-> filter
    pipe -. "throws" .-> filter
    svc -. "throws" .-> filter
    filter --> err["Error envelope"]

Order

In NestJS, guards run before pipes. So a request is authenticated and authorized first, and only then is its body validated.

docs.title: 2.1 Global guards, in order
docs.text:
# Guard File What it does Controlled by 1 JwtAuthGuard src/identity/auth/guards/jwt-auth.guard.ts Requires Authorization: Bearer <access token>. Verifies it with JWT_ACCESS_SECRET. Then loads the account and rejects it (401) if it was deleted, deactivated, or is unverified. Sets request.user = { sub, email, username }. @Public() (src/common/decorators/public.decorator.ts) skips it. 2 RateLimitGuard src/rate-limiter/rate-limit.guard.ts Token bucket in Redis. Sets X-RateLimit-Limit and X-RateLimit-Remaining; on deny returns 429 with Retry-After. Skips non-HTTP contexts. Fails open if Redis is down. @RateLimit(policy, { scope?, cost? }). Policies: CLASS_A 10 per 5 min by IP (auth), CLASS_B 30 per min by user (writes), CLASS_C 120 per min by user (reads). No decorator means no limit. 3 RolesGuard src/identity/rbac/guards/roles.guard.ts Checks the user has one of the listed platform roles. @Roles(...). No decorator means pass. 4 OrgContextGuard src/organizations/guards/org-context.guard.ts Finds the organization the request acts in and checks the user is an active member. Sets request.org (org id and the member's role). A non-member gets 404, so the org's existence is not leaked. @OrgScoped() reads :orgUid from the path. @OrgHeaderScoped() reads the optional x-organization-id header; without it the request is "personal". 5 PermissionGuard src/identity/rbac/guards/permission.guard.ts Checks permissions. Inside an org, it checks the member's org role. Outside, it checks the user's platform roles. @Permissions(...) (always) and @OrgPermissions(...) (only when request.org is set).

Handy parameter decorators: @CurrentUser() (the JWT payload), @CurrentOrg() (org context, only on @OrgScoped routes), and @OptionalOrg() (org context or null).

RabbitMQ consumers also pass through guards

@golevelup/nestjs-rabbitmq calls @RabbitSubscribe handlers through Nest's normal pipeline, so the global guards run for them too. That is why every consumer class is marked @Public(). Without it, JwtAuthGuard would look for an HTTP header that does not exist.

See Auth, RBAC, Organizations, and Platform Services for details.

docs.title: 2.2 Validation
docs.text:
src/main.ts sets a global ValidationPipe with:

  • whitelist: true: unknown fields are removed.
  • forbidNonWhitelisted: true: unknown fields cause a 400 instead of being silently dropped.
  • transform: true: query and path values are converted to the DTO types (for example, "5" to 5).

DTOs use class-validator decorators. WebSocket messages use their own pipe (src/events/pipes/ws-validation.pipe.ts).

docs.title: 2.3 Responses: envelope and serializers
docs.text:
There is no global interceptor. Each controller builds its own response:

  1. The service returns entities (or plain query rows).
  2. The controller passes them through the module's serializer, for example src/assessments/serializers/assessments.serializer.ts. Each serializer extends Serializer<TSource, TResponse> from src/common/serializers/serializer.ts and copies only the fields the response DTO documents. This stops password hashes, joined relations, or soft-delete columns from leaking.
  3. The controller returns new ApiResponse(data, message, meta?) from src/common/api-response.ts.
{ "success": true, "message": "Assessment fetched", "data": { }, "meta": { } }

meta is optional (for example, paging info). data is never missing; undefined becomes null.

docs.title: 2.4 Errors
docs.text:
HttpExceptionFilter (src/common/filters/http-exception.filter.ts) is registered with @Catch(), so it catches everything:

  • An HttpException keeps its status. Its message is used (arrays of validation messages are joined with ,). Any extra fields on the exception body are spread into the response.
  • A DomainError (see section 6) is mapped to HTTP first by src/common/filters/domain-error.mapper.ts: invalid_transition and conflict → 409, rule_violation → 400, forbidden → 403.
  • Anything else becomes a 500 with Internal server error, and the stack is logged.
{ "success": false, "message": "Missing permission: questions:create" }

There is no error key. Extra fields sit at the top level.

docs.title: 3.2 Redis
docs.text:
Redis has two separate jobs, on two separate connections and logical DBs. Both fail open: if Redis is slow or down, the app keeps working.

Use Client DB What happens when Redis fails Rate limiting REDIS_CLIENT in src/rate-limiter/redis.provider.ts REDIS_DB (0) Requests are allowed. Timeout is 200 ms by default. Read cache CACHE_REDIS_CLIENT in src/config/redis/redis.provider.ts, used through RedisHelper (src/common/helpers/redis.helper.ts) REDIS_CACHE_DB (1) A read becomes a cache miss and goes to Postgres. Timeout is 500 ms by default.

What is cached (keys are prefixed cache:v1, TTLs in src/config/redis/cache-ttl.constants.ts):

Data TTL Why it is safe Results and analytics of an evaluated attempt 1 hour An evaluated attempt never changes again. Question content during an attempt 1 hour Assessment questions are append-only. AI assistant lists and details (assessments, attempts) 60 seconds Short TTL instead of explicit invalidation.

The health check (GET /health) pings the rate-limit Redis client. Redis is not used for sessions, refresh tokens (those are in Postgres), or Socket.IO.

docs.title: 3.3 RabbitMQ
docs.text:
MessagingModule (src/config/rabbitmq/rabbitmq.module.ts) connects with RABBITMQ_URL and declares 4 topic exchanges and 12 queues. Names live in src/config/rabbitmq/rabbitmq.constants.ts. The CONSUMER env var decides whether this instance also runs the consumers (registerHandlers).

Every producer first saves a row in the jobs table, then publishes { jobId, ...payload }. Because of this, JobsService can rebuild and republish any message on retry using the route table in src/jobs/job-routes.ts.

(src/assessments/generation/generation-orchestrator.service.ts) McqSectionConsumer (src/assessments/generation/consumers/mcq-section.consumer.ts) question.generation question.section.coding (src/assessments/evaluation/consumers/) attempt attempt.evaluate.mcq attempt-evaluation-mcq-queue EvaluationOrchestratorService (src/assessments/evaluation/evaluation-orchestrator.service.ts) attempt-evaluation-descriptive-queue EvaluationOrchestratorService DescriptiveEvaluationConsumer roadmap roadmap.analyze roadmap-analysis-queue LearningRoadmapsService (src/learning-roadmaps/learning-roadmaps.service.ts) RoadmapAnalysisConsumer (src/learning-roadmaps/consumers/) roadmap roadmap.generate roadmap-generation-queue LearningRoadmapsService RoadmapGenerationConsumer roadmap roadmap.modify roadmap-modification-queue LearningRoadmapsService RoadmapModificationConsumer organization organization.invitations.import organization-invitation-import-queue OrganizationInvitationImportService (src/organizations/services/organization-invitation-import.service.ts) OrganizationInvitationImportConsumer (src/organizations/consumers/)

JobsService.retry (src/jobs/jobs.service.ts, behind POST /v1/jobs/:id/retry) can republish any of these.

Why one queue per question type? Coding work (writing test cases, running code) is much slower than MCQ work. Separate queues mean a slow coding section never blocks MCQs.

Why save the job row first? If publishing fails, the code marks the job FAILED right away and returns 503, so nothing is left "stuck" in a running state. The client can always read progress from GET /v1/jobs/:id.

docs.title: 3.4 Socket.IO gateway
docs.text:
EventsGateway (src/events/events.gateway.ts) listens on path /socket.io.

Part Behavior Connect The token comes from handshake.auth.token, the token query param, or an Authorization: Bearer header. It is verified with JWT_ACCESS_SECRET. A bad token gets an exception event and is disconnected. A good one joins the room for that user. ai.conversation.message Client → server chat message. The AI assistant answers and the reply returns on the same event. code.run Client → server "run my code" during an attempt. Results stream back to that socket only: code.run.started, code.run.case (per visible test case), then code.run.completed or code.run.failed. Server push emitToUser(userId, event, data) sends to every socket of the user. Today it is used for org.invitations.import.settled when a CSV import finishes. Errors WsExceptionFilter sends an exception frame and keeps the socket open.

Connections are tracked in an in-memory map (src/events/connection-manager.service.ts). There is no Redis adapter, so a push only reaches sockets connected to the same instance. See Realtime Events.

docs.title: 3.5 External services
docs.text:
Service Used for Code Config OpenAI, Anthropic, Google GenAI Question generation, descriptive grading, roadmaps, AI assistant src/ai/llm/chat-model.factory.ts, src/ai/ai-model-registry.service.ts ai_models rows point at env vars such as OPENAI_API_KEY Razorpay Orders and payment webhooks src/commerce/payments/razorpay/razorpay.service.ts, src/webhooks/ RAZORPAY_* Piston (self-hosted) or OnlineCompiler.io Running candidate code src/code-execution/runners/ chosen by src/code-execution/code-execution.module.ts CODE_RUNNER_PROVIDER, PISTON_*, ONLINE_COMPILER_* SMTP (Nodemailer) Transactional email and newsletters src/notifications/email/email.service.ts SMTP_*, EMAIL_FROM AWS S3 (or MinIO / LocalStack) Uploaded invitation CSVs src/storage/storage.service.ts AWS_* Google OAuth Verifying Google ID tokens src/identity/auth/google/google-oauth.service.ts GOOGLE_OAUTH2_CLIENT_ID

All LLM calls are recorded in the llm_audit table (src/ai/llm-audit.service.ts). See AI Layer and Code Execution.

docs.title: 4. Sync vs async work
docs.text: Rule of thumb: if a task calls an LLM, runs code, or loops over many rows, it goes to RabbitMQ. The HTTP request saves a jobs row, publishes a message, and returns fast. Everything else runs inside the request.

docs.title: 4.1 A typical sync request: save an answer
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor C as Client
    participant G as Global guards
    participant P as ValidationPipe
    participant Ctl as AttemptsController
    participant S as AttemptsService
    participant DB as PostgreSQL

    C->>G: PUT /v1/attempts/:attemptUid/responses/:questionId
    G->>G: JWT check, rate limit, roles, org, permissions
    G->>P: allowed
    P->>Ctl: validated DTO
    Ctl->>S: save response for current user
    S->>DB: load attempt and assessment
    S->>S: domain rules - attempt answerable, assessment window open
    S->>DB: upsert response row
    S-->>Ctl: saved entity
    Ctl-->>C: 200 ApiResponse with serialized data

docs.title: 4.2 A typical async job: AI assessment generation
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor C as Client
    participant Ctl as AssessmentsController
    participant O as GenerationOrchestrator
    participant DB as PostgreSQL
    participant MQ as RabbitMQ
    participant W as Section consumer
    participant LLM as LLM provider
    participant A as GenerationAggregator

    C->>Ctl: POST /v1/assessments/generate
    Ctl->>O: start request
    O->>DB: check plan, spend quota
    O->>DB: one transaction - assessment, sections, parent job, one job per section
    O->>MQ: publish each section job to its type queue
    Ctl-->>C: 200 with assessmentId and jobId
    MQ->>W: section message
    W->>LLM: LangGraph plan, generate, review
    LLM-->>W: questions
    W->>DB: save questions, mark section job done
    W->>A: section settled
    A->>DB: lock parent job, update progress
    A->>DB: all done - assessment ready, parent job completed
    loop until done
        C->>Ctl: GET /v1/jobs/:jobId
    end

If any section fails, the aggregator fails the parent job and refunds the quota once. POST /v1/assessments/:id/generation/retry re-runs only the failed sections. Clients learn about progress by polling GET /v1/jobs/:id; there is no WebSocket push for generation today. See AI Assessment Generation.

docs.title: 4.3 Async job with a WebSocket push: CSV invitation import
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor C as Org admin
    participant Ctl as OrgInvitationsController
    participant I as InvitationImportService
    participant S3 as S3
    participant MQ as RabbitMQ
    participant W as InvitationImportConsumer
    participant WS as EventsGateway

    C->>Ctl: POST /v1/orgs/:orgUid/invitations/import with CSV
    Ctl->>I: start import
    I->>S3: store CSV
    I->>I: save jobs row
    I->>MQ: publish job
    Ctl-->>C: 200 with jobId
    MQ->>W: import message
    W->>S3: read CSV
    W->>W: parse rows, invite in chunks, send emails
    W->>W: mark job completed or failed
    W->>WS: emitToUser org.invitations.import.settled
    WS-->>C: push event

Whether the import succeeds or fails, the user gets the org.invitations.import.settled event with the job id and a summary (or the failure reason).

Other async flows follow the same shape: attempt evaluation (see Evaluation) and the three roadmap stages (see Learning Roadmaps).

docs.title: 4.4 Scheduled work
docs.text: SchedulersModule (src/schedulers/) is the only place for @Cron handlers. Today there is one: newsletter-dispatch, every minute, turned off with NEWSLETTER_SCHEDULER_ENABLED=false. See Jobs & Schedulers.

docs.title: 5. Folder structure
docs.text:
Each feature module follows the same shape. The nestjs-folder-structure skill has the full rules.

src/<module>/
  <module>.module.ts
  <module>.controller.ts      # thin: validate, call service, serialize, wrap in ApiResponse
  <module>.service.ts         # business logic and DB access
  admin.controller.ts         # /v1/admin/... routes for platform admins (many modules)
  dto/                        # request and response DTOs (class-validator + Swagger)
  serializers/                # <module>.serializer.ts extends common Serializer
  domain/                     # pure rules and state transitions (where needed)
  consumers/                  # RabbitMQ consumers (where needed)
  interfaces/                 # TypeScript interfaces
Folder What lives there src/common/entities/ All TypeORM entities, exported from index.ts. Entities do not extend a base class; each declares id, createdAt, updatedAt, and usually deletedAt inline. src/common/decorators/ @Public(). src/common/filters/ HttpExceptionFilter and the DomainError → HTTP mapper. src/common/domain/ DomainError and transition-table helpers. src/common/dto/ PaginationDto and PaginatedResponseDto. src/common/enums/ Shared enums by area (assessments, commerce, identity, jobs, roadmaps, and more). src/common/helpers/ RedisHelper, LIKE-escaping, question content helpers. src/common/serializers/ The base Serializer class. src/common/ (root files) api-response.ts, db-errors.ts (for example, unique-violation checks), nano-id.ts and prefixed-id.ts (public ids), slugify.ts. src/config/ Database, RabbitMQ, and Redis setup. src/migrations/, src/seeders/, src/scripts/ Schema changes, seed data, one-off CLI scripts.

docs.title: 6. Cross-cutting conventions
docs.text:
These come from the code and the project skills in .claude/skills/. When a skill and general NestJS habits disagree, the skill wins.

Topic Convention Skill Controllers Thin. No try/catch. Call the service, serialize, return ApiResponse. nestjs-error-handling, api-response-format Business errors Services throw Nest HTTP exceptions (NotFoundException, ConflictException, ForbiddenException, UnprocessableEntityException, ServiceUnavailableException, and so on). Pure domain/ code throws DomainError and knows nothing about HTTP. nestjs-error-handling State machines Status changes go through transition tables in domain/ folders (for example, src/assessments/domain/attempt-state.ts). An illegal move throws DomainError.invalidTransition, which becomes 409. - Validation class-validator on every DTO field, @Type() for query numbers, PartialType for updates. nestjs-validation Config Always ConfigService, never process.env, except in main.ts, data-source.ts, RabbitMQ constants, and scripts. config-service-usage Entities Explicit column name (snake_case) and type, timestamptz dates, named indexes, soft delete with deletedAt. Integer auto-increment ids; public ids use nanoid uid columns. typeorm-entity-patterns Migrations Every schema change needs a migration. Never edit an applied one. typeorm-migrations Transactions dataSource.transaction(async (manager) => ...) for multi-table writes. Use only manager inside the callback. Publish to RabbitMQ after the commit. nestjs-transactions Pagination Cursor-based: cursor (last id) and limit (max 50, default 20). Response has nextCursor and total. nestjs-pagination Queries Repository methods for simple reads, QueryBuilder for joins and filters. Avoid N+1 queries; select only needed columns. query-optimization Logging One new Logger(ClassName.name) per class. No console.*. Log ids, not personal data. logging-conventions Swagger Every route documents its envelope, errors, and auth. nestjs-swagger Tests Jest. Unit tests in tests/unit/<module>/ mirroring src/; e2e in tests/. jest-mock-patterns, test-naming-conventions, e2e-test-setup Types No any. Use interfaces or DTOs. -

docs.title: 7. Security notes
docs.text:
Topic Current behavior Where Authentication Bearer JWT only, no cookies. Every non-public request re-checks that the account is still active and verified. Refresh tokens are stored as SHA-256 hashes in Postgres. jwt-auth.guard.ts, auth.service.ts CORS (HTTP) enableCors({ origin: true, credentials: true }). This reflects any origin. Fine for development; tighten it for production. src/main.ts CORS (WebSocket) origin: '*'. src/events/events.gateway.ts Raw body The app is created with rawBody: true, so req.rawBody is available. The Razorpay webhook verifies x-razorpay-signature (HMAC) over the raw bytes, which is why the parsed JSON body is not enough. Webhook events are de-duplicated in webhook_events. src/main.ts, src/webhooks/ Swagger /api/docs is behind HTTP basic auth (SWAGGER_USER / SWAGGER_PASS). See the known issue below. src/main.ts Rate limiting Auth routes use the strict IP-based CLASS_A policy. AI generation uses its own scope with a higher cost per call. src/rate-limiter/ Validation Unknown fields are rejected (forbidNonWhitelisted). src/main.ts Not used No helmet. passport and passport-jwt are installed but not used; guards verify tokens with JwtService directly. package.json

Known issues to be aware of

  • Swagger basic auth may not block content. When credentials are missing or wrong, the middleware in src/main.ts sets 401 and WWW-Authenticate but then calls next(), so Swagger still sends the page body. The JSON spec route (/api/docs-json) is also outside the protected /api/docs path prefix.
  • WebSocket auth is lighter than HTTP auth. The handshake only verifies the JWT signature (src/events/events.service.ts). It does not re-check that the account is still active, unlike JwtAuthGuard.
  • Pushes are per instance. With more than one instance, a emitToUser call from a consumer on instance A does not reach a socket held by instance B.

docs.title: 8. Related pages
docs.text:
• Getting Started: run it locally.
  • ERD and Data Access Patterns: the data model.
  • API v1: every endpoint.
  • Jobs & Schedulers: the jobs table and retries.
  • Realtime Events: the socket protocol.

docs.title: Data Access Patterns
docs.text:
This page explains how the code talks to the database. The tables themselves are described in the Data model (ERD).

The rules here come from two places: the project skills in .claude/skills/ (query-optimization, nestjs-transactions, nestjs-pagination, typeorm-entity-patterns, typeorm-migrations) and what the code actually does today. Where the two differ, this page says so.

docs.title: The big picture
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    C["Controller"] --> S["Service"]
    S -->|"find / QueryBuilder"| R["Repository<Entity>"]
    S -->|"dataSource.transaction"| M["EntityManager"]
    S -->|"raw SQL for reports"| DS["DataSource.query"]
    R --> PG[("PostgreSQL")]
    M --> PG
    DS --> PG
    S -->|"safeGet / safeSet"| RH["RedisHelper"]
    RH --> RD[("Redis cache")]
    S -->|"publish after commit"| MQ[["RabbitMQ"]]
  • Services own the data. Controllers never touch a repository. A service returns entities; the controller turns them into JSON with the module's serializer.
  • One module owns each table. When another module needs that data, it calls the owning service. For example, AttemptsService calls AssessmentsService.findOne() instead of reading assessments itself.
  • Postgres is the source of truth. Redis only holds short-lived copies of some reads.

docs.title: Entities and registration
docs.text:
All 44 entities live in src/common/entities/ and are exported from src/common/entities/index.ts. A new entity must be added in four places:

  1. src/common/entities/index.ts (export it).
  2. The entities array in src/config/database/database.module.ts (used by the running app).
  3. The entities array in src/config/database/data-source.ts (used by the TypeORM CLI for migrations).
  4. TypeOrmModule.forFeature([...]) in every module that injects its repository.

The skills show old paths

The typeorm-entity-patterns and typeorm-migrations skills mention src/database/.... The real files are src/config/database/database.module.ts, src/config/database/data-source.ts and src/migrations/.

synchronize is false in every environment. The schema only changes through migrations (see Migrations).

docs.title: Repositories
docs.text:
TestFlow uses TypeORM's built-in Repository<T>. There are no custom repository classes. (The folder src/assessments/repositories/ exists but is empty.)

How When Example @InjectRepository(Entity) private readonly repo: Repository<Entity> Normal reads and single writes JobsService, TagsService, WebhooksService this.dataSource.getRepository(Entity) A service that already holds DataSource and needs a quick read UsageService.consume() reads Feature manager.find(Entity, ...), manager.save(...) Inside a transaction Every dataSource.transaction(...) callback

Inject DataSource with no decorator. It is provided globally by TypeOrmModule.forRootAsync().

docs.title: Reading data: find options, QueryBuilder or raw SQL
docs.text:
Pick the simplest tool that does the job:

Need Use Real example One row by id or a unique column repo.findOne({ where }), then throw NotFoundException if null AttemptsService.resolveAttempt() A simple list with plain filters repo.find({ where, order, take }) JobsService.findSections() "Does it exist?" repo.exists() or QueryBuilder .getExists() SubscriptionsService.checkout() (already has an active plan?) Joins with conditions, dynamic filters, sorting, paging, counts createQueryBuilder() AssessmentsService.paginateList(), AccessControlService.userHasPermission() Window functions, CTEs, heavy reports dataSource.query(sql, params) Leaderboard ranking, attempt analytics, admin stats

Raw SQL is used in only a few files: src/assessments/attempts/leaderboard.service.ts, src/assessments/attempts/analytics.service.ts, src/stats/admin.service.ts, src/learning-roadmaps/learning-roadmap-assessment.service.ts, src/newsletters/newsletters-dispatch.service.ts and the health check. Always pass values as $1, $2 parameters, never by string building.

docs.title: Rules that keep queries fast
docs.text:
• Never query inside a loop (the "N+1" problem). Load related rows with relations: { ... } or leftJoinAndSelect, or fetch them all at once with In([...ids]).
  • Never use eager: true on a relation. Load relations explicitly in the query that needs them.
  • Select only what a list needs. Use select: { ... }. Large columns can be hidden by default: learning_roadmaps.notepad has select: false, so only the notepad endpoints load it.
  • Index what you filter or sort by, and declare the index on the entity with a name such as @Index('IDX_<table>_<column>').
  • Run independent reads in parallel with Promise.all, as AuthService.getMe() and LeaderboardService.getLeaderboard() do.
  • Escape user text in LIKE searches with likeContains() from src/common/helpers/like.helper.ts. It escapes %, _ and \.
  • Turn decimal values into numbers. The pg driver returns decimal columns as strings. Use Number(row.score) before doing maths.

docs.title: Writing data and transactions
docs.text:
A transaction groups several writes so they all succeed or all fail. TestFlow uses one pattern only: the callback form of DataSource.transaction().

return this.dataSource.transaction(async (manager: EntityManager) => {
  const attempt = await manager.findOne(AssessmentAttempt, { where: { assessmentId, userId } });
  // ... more reads and writes, all through `manager`
});

If the callback throws, TypeORM rolls everything back. There is no createQueryRunner() / startTransaction() in application code; QueryRunner only appears inside migrations. A few services use this.repo.manager.transaction(...), which is the same thing.

docs.title: Transaction rules (from the nestjs-transactions skill)
docs.text: Rule Why Use a transaction for two or more writes that must succeed together A half-finished change leaves bad data Inside the callback, use only manager this.someRepository runs outside the transaction Reads that decide a write also go through manager So they see the same snapshot and hold the same locks Let errors propagate. Do not catch inside the callback unless you rethrow. The throw is what triggers the rollback. NotFoundException and friends work fine. Do not nest transactions One transaction per service call Single writes and pure reads need no transaction Extra cost for nothing

docs.title: Sharing one transaction across services
docs.text:
When one service must write as part of another service's transaction, its method takes an optional manager argument. If a manager is passed, it joins that transaction; if not, it opens its own. Examples:

  • SubscriptionsService.createFreeSubscription(userId, manager) is called inside AuthService.verifyEmail() and UsageService.consume().
  • UsageService.release(..., manager?) gives back a usage unit inside the caller's transaction, so the refund commits together with whatever caused it.
  • UsersService.markEmailVerified(userId, manager).

docs.title: Publish to RabbitMQ only after the commit
docs.text:
When a request creates a job, the job rows are written in a transaction first, and the message is published after the transaction commits. GenerationOrchestratorService does this: createJobs() runs in dataSource.transaction, then publishSections() runs. This way a worker never receives a message for a row that was rolled back. If the publish fails, the job row still exists and can be retried through JobsService.retry(), which republishes { jobId, ...payload }.

Usage that is charged before such a transaction is given back with UsageService.release() if the transaction fails.

docs.title: Concurrency: locks and other guards
docs.text: Several requests or workers can touch the same row at the same time. TestFlow uses these tools, from strongest to lightest:

docs.title: 1. Row locks (pessimistic_write)
docs.text:
SELECT ... FOR UPDATE locks a row until the transaction ends, so a second transaction waits. It is used where a read-then-write must not interleave:

Where Locked row Why UsageService.consume() and release() The user_feature_usage row Two generations must not both pass the quota check EvaluationOrchestratorService.claim() The EVALUATE_ATTEMPT job and the attempt Only one worker may claim an evaluation EvaluationAggregatorService.onChildSettled() The parent job Children finish in parallel; only one may close the parent GenerationAggregatorService The GENERATE_ASSESSMENT parent job Same, for section generation GenerationOrchestratorService.reopen() The parent job Two retry clicks must not both reopen it

Pattern: manager.createQueryBuilder(Job, 'job').setLock('pessimistic_write').where('job.id = :id', { id }).getOne(), always inside dataSource.transaction.

docs.title: 2. FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED (work queue claim)
docs.text: NewslettersDispatchService.claimDueNewsletters() moves due newsletters from SCHEDULED to SENDING in one UPDATE ... WHERE id IN (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED) RETURNING id. Two app instances running the cron at the same time split the rows instead of sending the same newsletter twice.

docs.title: 3. Unique indexes as the final guard
docs.text:
Sometimes it is simpler to try the insert and let Postgres reject the duplicate:

Case Unique index What the code does on a clash Random short uid collides UQ_organizations_uid, UQ_assessment_templates_uid, UQ_learning_roadmap_templates_uid Retries with a new uid (isUniqueViolation() in src/common/db-errors.ts) Two requests open the same AI conversation UQ_ai_conversations_context The loser re-reads and returns the winner's row (AiConversationsService.getOrCreate()) Same generate request sent twice with an Idempotency-Key UQ_jobs_created_by_idempotency_key Returns the first request's result (GenerationOrchestratorService) Same webhook delivered twice UQ_webhook_events_event_id Already processed, so ignored (WebhooksService) One attempt per user per assessment UQ_assessment_attempts_user_assessment startAttempt() returns the existing attempt

isUniqueViolation(error, 'UQ_name') checks Postgres error code 23505 and the constraint name, so you can react to one specific index.

docs.title: 4. Atomic counters
docs.text:
Counters are changed in SQL, not read-modify-write in JavaScript, so parallel updates do not lose each other:

  • manager.increment(Assessment, { id }, 'currentParticipants', delta) for seats.
  • manager.increment(Assessment, { id }, 'currTotalQuestions', n) when questions are written.
  • { totalVerificationEmail: () => '"total_verification_email" + 1' } in UsersService.
  • LearningRoadmapNode.positionIndex is shifted with one increment during the two-phase reindex in RoadmapGraphService, so the unique (learning_roadmap_id, position_index) never clashes mid-update.

docs.title: 5. State checks in domain/ files
docs.text: Status changes go through small functions in each module's domain/ folder (for example claimEvaluation(), assertAnswerable(), reopenJob() in src/assessments/domain/ and src/jobs/domain/). They throw when a move is not allowed, such as answering a submitted attempt. Combined with a row lock, this stops two workers from moving the same row twice.

docs.title: Known gaps
docs.text:
• Saving an answer (AttemptsService.upsertResponse()) is find-then-insert with no unique index on (attempt_id, assessment_question_id). Two parallel saves of the same question could create two rows.
  • The usage lock only covers an existing user_feature_usage row. The very first consume for a feature inserts without a unique index to stop a twin row.

See ERD → Known schema gaps.

docs.title: Pagination
docs.text: Two styles exist side by side. New list endpoints should use cursor pagination, as the nestjs-pagination skill requires.

docs.title: Cursor (keyset) pagination: the standard
docs.text:
A cursor is the id of the last row the client saw. The next page asks for rows "after" that id. It stays fast on large tables because Postgres jumps straight to the cursor using the index, instead of counting past skipped rows.

  • Query DTO: PaginationDto in src/common/dto/pagination.dto.ts (cursor?: number, limit 1 to 50, default 20). The skill says cursor is a UUID; the code uses an integer because every primary key is an int.
  • Response: PaginatedResponseDto<T> in src/common/dto/paginated-response.dto.ts: { data, nextCursor, total }. nextCursor: null means the last page.
  • Recipe: order by the sort column plus id as a tie-breaker, fetch limit + 1 rows, and if you got the extra row, drop it and return the last id as nextCursor. total is a separate count for display only.

Used by: user admin lists, organizations and members, assessment participants, learning roadmaps and roadmap templates, AI conversation messages, and the leaderboard. The leaderboard (LeaderboardService.getLeaderboard()) is a good model for a complex order: it keysets on (score DESC, time_taken_ms ASC, id ASC) in raw SQL.

docs.title: Offset pagination: older endpoints
docs.text:
page and limit with qb.skip((page - 1) * limit).take(limit) and getManyAndCount(). The response meta has page, limit, total and totalPages.

Still used by: assessment lists (AssessmentsService.paginateList()), my attempts, attempt review, tags, assessment prompts, assessment templates, question admin, plans, commerce admin, newsletters admin, AI admin and support tickets admin. These are fine for small, admin-sized tables. Do not copy this style into new user-facing lists.

Either way: an empty page is data: [], never a 404.

docs.title: Soft delete in practice
docs.text:
The tables that soft-delete are listed in the ERD.

Task How Soft delete repo.softDelete({ id }) or manager.softDelete(...). Do not set deletedAt by hand. Normal reads Nothing to do. find* and QueryBuilder add deleted_at IS NULL for you. Read deleted rows too withDeleted: true. Example: AuthService.storeRefreshToken() finds the user's soft-deleted token row and reuses it. Raw SQL Add "deleted_at" IS NULL yourself (the newsletter claim does). Uniqueness Use a partial unique index WHERE deleted_at IS NULL, so a deleted row does not block a new one.

Many "removals" are status changes instead of deletes: a participant becomes revoked, an attempt becomes rejected, a member can be suspended. Tables without deleted_at (attempts, responses, jobs, audit rows, orders, payments) are either kept forever or hard-deleted.

docs.title: Caching in Redis
docs.text:
Redis caches a few expensive reads. Postgres stays the source of truth.

  • Helper: RedisHelper in src/common/helpers/redis.helper.ts, with safeGet<T>(key) and safeSet(key, value, ttlSeconds).
  • Fail-open: if Redis is down, a read counts as a miss and a write is skipped. A Redis problem never fails a request.
  • Keys are prefixed with cache:v1: (src/config/redis/redis.constants.ts). Each key also carries its own version, for example attempts:result:v8:a<uid>:u<userId>. When the cached shape changes, bump that version so old entries are never read.
  • TTLs live in one place: CACHE_TTL_SECONDS in src/config/redis/cache-ttl.constants.ts. A TTL is required on every write.

docs.title: What is cached, and why it is safe
docs.text:
There is no explicit invalidation. Instead, each cached read is safe for one of two reasons:

Read Key (after cache:v1:) TTL Why it cannot go badly stale Attempt result attempts:result:v8:a{uid}:u{user} 1 hour Only cached once the attempt is evaluated or rejected, which are final Attempt question list attempts:questions:v4:a{uid}:u{user} 1 hour Only cached once the attempt is settled One attempt question attempts:question:v3:a{uid}:q{id}:u{user} 1 hour Question snapshots do not change after publish Attempt analytics attempts:analytics:v2:a{uid}:u{user}:i{minutes} 1 hour Settled attempts only Assistant attempt detail attempts:assistant:detail:v2:a{uid}:u{user} 1 hour Settled attempts only Assistant attempt list attempts:assistant:list:v2:u{user}:l{limit}:s{status} 60 s Short TTL: may include a live attempt Assistant assessment list and detail built in AssessmentsService 60 s Short TTL: counts may lag by up to a minute

Rule of thumb: cache only data that can no longer change, or accept a short, bounded staleness. If you add a cache, put the TTL in CACHE_TTL_SECONDS with a comment that explains why it is safe.

Other Redis users have their own connections and are covered elsewhere: the rate limiter (src/rate-limiter/) and the health check. There is also one small in-memory cache: AiModelRegistryService keeps built chat-model clients in a Map.

docs.title: Migrations
docs.text: A migration is a TypeScript file that changes the schema in a controlled, reversible way. Every schema change must have one. Never use synchronize: true and never run SQL by hand on a shared database.

docs.title: Where and how they are named
docs.text:
• Folder: src/migrations/.
  • File name: <YYYYMMDDHHmmss>-<kebab-description>.ts, for example 20261026000000-add-registration-window-to-assessments.ts. For several on the same day, bump the last digits (...000001, ...000002).
  • Class name: PascalCase description plus the same timestamp, for example AddJobIdToAssessments20260902000001.
  • One logical change per file.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
Command What it does npm run migration:show Lists applied [X] and pending [ ] migrations. Run this first. npm run migration:run Applies pending migrations npm run migration:revert Rolls back the last applied migration npm run migration:generate -- src/migrations/<name> Writes a migration from the difference between the entities and your local database npm run migration:run:prod, migration:show:prod, migration:revert:prod Same, against the compiled dist/ data source

All of them use src/config/database/data-source.ts, which reads DATABASE_* from .env.

docs.title: Workflow for a schema change
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A["Change the entity<br/>(column, index, relation)"] --> B["npm run migration:show<br/>local DB fully migrated?"]
    B --> C["Write the migration<br/>(or generate, then trim)"]
    C --> D["Name every index, FK and check<br/>IDX_ / UQ_ / FK_ / CHK_"]
    D --> E["Write down() in reverse order"]
    E --> F["npm run migration:run"]
    F --> G["npm run migration:revert<br/>then run again"]
    G --> H["Commit entity + migration together"]

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
Rule Why Every migration has a working down() that undoes up() in reverse order (drop FKs, then indexes, then the table) So a bad deploy can be rolled back. If a change truly cannot be undone, down() throws with a clear message. Name every constraint: IDX_<table>_<col>, UQ_<table>_<cols>, FK_<table>_<col>, CHK_<table>_<rule> Readable errors, and the name must match the entity's @Index('...') Never edit a migration that has already run on staging or production Other databases already applied the old version. Write a new migration instead. Data changes go in the migration: add the column as nullable, backfill with UPDATE, then make it NOT NULL Existing rows must be valid. See the 20261014000006 to 20261014000011 series, which split MCQ data into mcq_question_details this way. New "kinds" that will grow (question types, verdicts) can be varchar with a CHECK, not a Postgres enum Adding a Postgres enum value needs an ALTER TYPE migration New tables: int auto-increment id, created_at / updated_at with now() default, and deleted_at if the table soft-deletes Matches every other table Index every foreign key column Joins and parent deletes stay fast

Always review migration:generate output

Many existing foreign keys and unique constraints were created with readable names (FK_assessments_created_by) while the entities let TypeORM pick hashed names. So migration:generate produces dozens of DROP CONSTRAINT / ADD CONSTRAINT lines that change nothing. It also tries to drop things that exist only in migrations, such as UQ_assessment_attempts_user_assessment and two CHECK constraints. Keep only the lines for your change, or write the migration by hand with queryRunner.addColumn, createIndex and createForeignKey, as most existing migrations do. Full list: ERD → Known schema gaps.

docs.title: Seeds
docs.text: Reference data is filled by seeders in src/seeders/ (roles, permissions, features, plans, feature flags, AI models), run with npm run seed. Templates have their own scripts: npm run seed:assessment-templates and npm run seed:roadmap-templates. The first super admin is created with npm run bootstrap-admin.

docs.title: Common questions → where the answer lives
docs.text: Question Tables Service method How Who is this user, and what plan and flags do they have? users, subscriptions, plan_versions, plans, feature_flags AuthService.getMe() Four independent reads in Promise.all Can this user do questions:update? users_roles, roles, role_permissions, permissions AccessControlService.userHasPermission() (called by PermissionGuard) QueryBuilder join, getCount() > 0, exact key match Can this org member do it? organization_members → role_permissions AccessControlService.roleHasPermission() Same join, starting from the member's role_id What is the user's org context for /v1/orgs/:orgUid/...? organizations, organization_members OrganizationMembersService.resolveContext() One findOne on the user's active membership, joined to the organization by uid; a suspended org is refused Which assessments can I see? assessments, assessments_participants AssessmentsService.findAll() → paginateList() QueryBuilder, phase filters on the attempt window, offset paging Is this assessment open to me? assessments, assessments_participants AssessmentsService.findParticipantByAssessmentAndUser() + participantState() Rules in src/assessments/domain/ Start or resume my attempt assessment_attempts AttemptsService.startAttempt() Transaction; returns the existing attempt (unique per user and assessment) Save my answer assessment_attempt_responses AttemptsService.upsertResponse() Transaction; find, then update or insert, reset to pending Submit and grade assessment_attempts, jobs, responses AttemptsService.submitAttempt() → EvaluationOrchestratorService Opens an EVALUATE_ATTEMPT job; workers lock and grade My result attempts, responses, assessments_questions AttemptsService.getAttemptResult() Cached in Redis once final Leaderboard assessment_attempts, users LeaderboardService.getLeaderboard() Raw SQL with ranking, keyset cursor, plus "my row" Review or reject attempts (creator) attempts, responses AttemptReviewService.listAttempts(), getResponses(), reject() Offset paging; reject in a transaction Is generation done? jobs JobsService.findOne(), findSections() Ownership checked against payload.userId Do I have quota left? subscriptions, plan_features, user_feature_usage UsageService.consume(), getSubscriptionUsage() Transaction with a row lock; resets the period when it has passed What can my plan generate? plan_features (ALLOWED_QUESTION_TYPES) SubscriptionsService.getAllowedQuestionTypes() Reads the enum feature value Did the payment go through? payments, orders, subscriptions, webhook_events WebhooksService → PaymentsService.markPaymentCaptured() Idempotent by event_id; one transaction Show my roadmap graph learning_roadmaps, nodes, edges LearningRoadmapsService.getGraph() Edges load by roadmap_id in one query My roadmap list with progress roadmaps, nodes LearningRoadmapsService.list() Cursor paging; one grouped count over all roadmaps on the page (never one count per roadmap), served by the (learning_roadmap_id, status) index Chat history with the assistant ai_conversations, ai_conversation_messages AiConversationsService.getMessagesPage() Cursor paging by message id (ids are unique and always increase, so a cursor never lands between two equal timestamps) What did the LLM calls cost? llm_audit, ai_models src/ai/admin.service.ts Admin reports over the append-only audit table Is this feature flag on for me? feature_flags, feature_flag_roles, users_roles FeatureFlagsService.enabledFor() Off, on for all, or on for listed roles Platform numbers for admins many src/stats/admin.service.ts Raw SQL aggregates

docs.title: Checklist for new data code
docs.text:
• [ ] Reads use find options unless you need joins, paging or aggregates.
  • [ ] No query inside a loop. No eager relations.
  • [ ] Two or more writes are in one dataSource.transaction, using only manager.
  • [ ] Read-then-write races are covered by a row lock or a unique index.
  • [ ] New lists use cursor pagination with PaginationDto and PaginatedResponseDto.
  • [ ] Raw SQL uses $n parameters and filters deleted_at IS NULL.
  • [ ] Any cache has a TTL in CACHE_TTL_SECONDS, a versioned key, and a reason it is safe.
  • [ ] Schema changes come with a named, reversible migration that was run and reverted locally.

docs.title: Data Model (ERD)
docs.text:
This page describes the current PostgreSQL schema of the TestFlow backend. It was built from every *.entity.ts file and checked against the migrations in src/migrations (108 files, the newest is 20261029000000-backfill-order-statuses.ts). A local database migrated to the latest version was also compared with the entities using typeorm schema:log. The few differences it found are listed in Known schema gaps.

It replaces three older pages: erd.md, erd-organisation.md (a draft "workspaces" design that was never built; the real design is the organizations tables below) and complete-erd.md.

Where the code lives

  • All 44 entity classes: src/common/entities/ (re-exported from src/common/entities/index.ts).
  • All enums: src/common/enums/. Status enums live next to their rules in each module's domain/ folder (for example src/assessments/domain/attempt-state.ts) and are re-exported from src/common/enums.
  • Migrations: src/migrations/. How to write one: Data access patterns → Migrations.

docs.title: Naming
docs.text:
What Rule Example Table snake_case, usually plural assessment_attempts, users_roles Column snake_case, set with name: on every @Column created_by, is_active Entity property camelCase createdBy, isActive Index IDX_<table>_<column> IDX_jobs_status Unique index UQ_<table>_<column(s)> UQ_users_email Foreign key (in migrations) FK_<table>_<column> FK_assessments_created_by Check constraint CHK_<table>_<rule> CHK_assessment_sections_difficulty

Two table names do not match their class names. The class PlanVersionFeature maps to the table plan_features, and UserRole maps to users_roles.

docs.title: There is no base entity class
docs.text:
src/common/entities holds the entity files, but there is no shared BaseEntity. Every entity declares its own columns. The usual set is:

Column Decorator Type Notes id @PrimaryGeneratedColumn('increment') int Auto-increment. jobs.id and llm_audit.id are bigint (TypeScript type string). created_at @CreateDateColumn timestamptz Set on insert. updated_at @UpdateDateColumn timestamptz Set on every save. Missing on append-only tables. deleted_at @DeleteDateColumn timestamptz, nullable Only on soft-deletable tables.

All timestamps are timestamptz (time zone aware). The only date columns are user_feature_usage.period_start and period_end.

docs.title: Public ids
docs.text:
The numeric id is the internal key. Some tables also have a public id that clients use in URLs:

Kind Format Built by Tables Short uid 8 characters, letters and digits (nanoid) generateShortUid() in src/common/nano-id.ts organizations, assessment_templates, learning_roadmap_templates Prefixed id conv_<32 hex> or msg_<32 hex> generatePrefixedId() in src/common/prefixed-id.ts ai_conversations, ai_conversation_messages UUID Postgres uuid, generated on insert @Generated('uuid') assessment_attempts.uid

Short uids can collide. They sit behind a unique index, and the service retries the insert when Postgres reports a unique violation.

docs.title: Soft delete
docs.text:
A soft delete sets deleted_at to the current time instead of removing the row. TypeORM's find* methods and QueryBuilder hide these rows automatically. Raw SQL does not, so raw queries must add deleted_at IS NULL themselves.

Soft-deletable (deleted_at present) Not soft-deletable users, refresh_tokens, roles, permissions, role_permissions, users_roles assessment_sections, assessments_questions, mcq_question_details, coding_question_details, descriptive_question_details organizations, organization_members assessment_attempts, assessment_attempt_responses assessments, assessments_participants, questions, tags, assessment_prompts, assessment_prompt_tags, assessment_templates jobs, llm_audit, ai_conversations, ai_conversation_messages plans, plan_versions, features, plan_features, subscriptions, user_feature_usage, credit_packs, user_feature_credits orders, payments, webhook_events ai_models, learning_roadmap_templates, newsletters, support_tickets learning_roadmaps, learning_roadmap_nodes, learning_node_edges feature_flags, feature_flag_roles

Rules that follow from this:

  • Uniqueness only counts live rows. Most unique indexes on soft-deletable tables are partial: WHERE deleted_at IS NULL. So a deleted user does not block a new sign-up with the same email, and a removed member can be invited again.
  • Many "deletes" are really status changes. A participant who leaves becomes revoked. An attempt set aside by a reviewer becomes rejected. A membership can be suspended. These rows stay visible.
  • Hard deletes still happen on tables without deleted_at, for example the DELETE of a response in AttemptsService.deleteResponse().
  • Foreign keys cascade on hard delete only. A soft delete of a parent does not touch its children.

docs.title: Enums: Postgres enum or varchar?
docs.text:
Most status columns are real Postgres enum types (named <table>_<column>_enum). Adding a value needs an ALTER TYPE migration. A few columns are stored as varchar on purpose, so new values need no migration:

  • questions.type, assessment_sections.question_type, assessments_questions.type (QuestionType)
  • assessment_attempt_responses.evaluation_status and code_verdict (guarded by CHECK constraints instead)
  • llm_audit.status, jobs.type, jobs.queue, features.key, coding_question_details.checker_type

docs.title: Money and marks
docs.text: Prices, marks and costs use decimal(precision, scale). The pg driver returns decimal values as strings, even where the entity types them as number. Convert with Number() before doing maths. llm_audit types its decimals as string to make this explicit.

docs.title: 1. Identity and RBAC
docs.text:
RBAC (role-based access control) means a user gets permissions through roles. Platform roles (for example super_admin) are held through users_roles. Organization roles are held through organization_members (see section 2). Both kinds of role draw from the same permissions catalog. Design details: RBAC and Auth.

docs.text:
A person who can sign in. Entity: src/common/entities/user.entity.ts.

Column Type Null Default Notes id int no auto PK full_name varchar(200) no first_name varchar(100) no last_name varchar(100) no username varchar(100) no Unique among live rows email varchar(255) no Unique among live rows password varchar(255) no bcrypt hash. Google sign-up stores a generated default password. must_change_password boolean no false Forces a password change on an admin-created or Google-created account phone_number varchar(20) yes null Unique (plain constraint, not limited to live rows) is_active boolean no true is_verified boolean no false Email verified is_newsletter_subscribe boolean no true Newsletter opt-in total_verification_email int no 0 How many verification emails were ever sent last_verification_email_sent_at timestamptz yes null Used to throttle resends oauth_provider enum OAuthProvider yes null google, github oauth_id varchar(255) yes null Provider's user id

Timestamps: created_at, updated_at, deleted_at. Indexes: UQ_users_username and UQ_users_email (partial, deleted_at IS NULL); unique (oauth_provider, oauth_id) WHERE oauth_id IS NOT NULL; unique phone_number.

docs.title: refresh_tokens
docs.text:
Stores a hash of the user's refresh token. Entity: refreshToken.entity.ts.

Column Type Null Default Notes id int no auto PK token_hash varchar no SHA-256 of the raw token. The raw token is never stored. user_id int no FK users.id, ON DELETE CASCADE (in the database) expires_at timestamptz no

Timestamps: created_at, deleted_at (no updated_at). Index: IDX_refresh_tokens_user_id (created by migration).

There is one row per user, not one per device. AuthService.storeRefreshToken() finds the user's row (including a soft-deleted one) and overwrites it, or inserts the first one. Logout soft-deletes it.

docs.title: roles
docs.text:
A named set of permissions. Entity: roles.entity.ts.

Column Type Null Default Notes id int no auto PK key varchar(100) no For example super_admin, org_admin scope enum RbacScope no platform platform or organization organization_id int yes null FK organizations.id, CASCADE. null for built-in roles; set for an organization's own custom role.

Timestamps: all three. Indexes: UQ_roles_key on key where organization_id IS NULL AND deleted_at IS NULL (built-in keys are unique); UQ_roles_organization_id_key on (organization_id, key) for custom roles; IDX_roles_organization_id.

Built-in roles: super_admin and beta_tester (platform; beta_tester grants nothing and only unlocks feature flags), and org_owner, org_admin, org_member (organization, shared by every org).

docs.title: permissions
docs.text:
One grantable action, keyed resource:action (for example questions:update). Entity: permissions.entity.ts.

Column Type Null Default Notes id int no auto PK key varchar(100) no UQ_permissions_key description text yes null

Timestamps: all three. The valid resources and actions are the RbacResource and RbacAction enums in src/common/enums/identity.enums.ts. Actions: read, create, update, delete, upload, export.

Old resources table and the *:* wildcard

Older docs describe a resources table. Migration 20260929000003-move-permission-keys-and-drop-resources.ts replaced it with permissions. The *:* wildcard is also gone: src/seeders/super-admin-permissions.seeder.ts replaces it with an explicit grant for every pair, and the permission check (AccessControlService.userHasPermission) matches exact keys only.

docs.title: role_permissions

Column Type Null Default Notes id int no auto PK role_id int no FK roles.id, CASCADE. IDX_role_permissions_role_id permission_id int no FK permissions.id, CASCADE. See src/identity/rbac/interfaces/role-permission-meta.interface.ts.

Timestamps: all three. There is no unique index on (role_id, permission_id); the services prevent duplicates.

docs.title: 3. Assessments, questions and the content library
docs.text: An assessment is a test made of sections. Each section holds questions of one type. Questions live in a reusable bank (questions) and are copied (snapshotted) into the assessment as assessments_questions rows, so later edits to the bank never change a published test. Design: Assessments, Questions and tags, Assessment generation.

docs.text:
A group of same-type questions inside an assessment, with its own marking. Entity: assessment-section.entity.ts.

Column Type Null Default Notes id int no auto PK assessment_id int no FK, CASCADE. Indexed. title varchar(255) no description text yes question_type varchar(20) no QuestionType: mcq, coding, descriptive max_questions int no correct_marks decimal(5,2) no Marks for a right answer incorrect_marks decimal(5,2) no Marks taken off for a wrong answer order_index int no Order in the assessment difficulty int no 1 1 (easiest) to 5. Timestamps: created_at, updated_at (no soft delete).

docs.title: assessments_questions
docs.text:
A snapshot of one bank question placed in an assessment. Entity: assessment-question.entity.ts (class AssessmentQuestion).

Column Type Null Default Notes id int no auto PK. Responses point here, not at questions. assessment_id int no FK, CASCADE. Indexed. question_id int no FK questions.id, CASCADE. Indexed. section_id int no FK assessment_sections.id, CASCADE. Indexed. type varchar(20) no mcq QuestionType question_text text no Copied from the bank content jsonb no Type-specific copy: McqQuestionContent, CodingQuestionContent or DescriptiveQuestionContent topics jsonb yes Copy of questions.meta.topics: QuestionTopic[] correct_marks decimal(5,2) no incorrect_marks decimal(5,2) no order_index int no

Timestamps: created_at only. Unique: UQ_assessments_questions_assessment_question on (assessment_id, question_id), so a bank question can appear only once per assessment.

Why snapshot? A participant must see exactly what was published, and grading must use the answer key that was live at the time. Copying the content into content makes the assessment independent of later bank edits or deletes.

docs.title: assessments_participants
docs.text:
A user's place on an assessment. Entity: assessment-participants.entity.ts.

Column Type Null Default Notes id int no auto PK user_id int no FK, CASCADE. Indexed. assessment_id int no FK, CASCADE. Indexed. status enum ParticipantStatus no See below invited_by int yes null FK users.id, SET NULL. Null for self-registration. Indexed. invited_at timestamptz yes null invite_accepted_at timestamptz yes null revoked_at timestamptz yes null Cleared if the user is invited again or re-registers

Timestamps: all three. Unique: (assessment_id, user_id) among live rows.

ParticipantStatus Meaning invited Offered a seat by an organization member. Must accept first. active May sit the test (registered, accepted, or the creator) revoked Declined, left, or removed. May be invited again or re-register.

The creator also has an active row but does not use a seat. Progress through the test is the attempt's status, not the participant's. Source: src/assessments/domain/participant-state.ts.

JobType values and their payload interfaces:

JobType Payload interface (file) GENERATE_ASSESSMENT (parent) ParentGenerationPayload (src/assessments/generation/interfaces/generation-job.interface.ts) GENERATE_MCQ_SECTION, GENERATE_CODING_SECTION, GENERATE_DESCRIPTIVE_SECTION SectionGenerationPayload (same file) EVALUATE_ATTEMPT (parent) AttemptEvaluationPayload (src/assessments/attempts/interfaces/attempt-evaluation-job.interface.ts) EVALUATE_MCQ_RESPONSES, EVALUATE_CODING_RESPONSES, EVALUATE_DESCRIPTIVE_RESPONSES ResponseEvaluationPayload (src/assessments/evaluation/interfaces/evaluation-job.interface.ts) IMPORT_ORG_INVITATIONS InvitationImportPayload (src/organizations/interfaces/invitation-import.interface.ts) ANALYZE_ROADMAP_INTENT, GENERATE_ROADMAP, MODIFY_ROADMAP_GRAPH Roadmap payloads (src/learning-roadmaps/) CREATE_ASSESSMENT Older single-job generation, still routed by src/assessments/consumers/question-generation.consumer.ts

docs.title: 7. Commerce: plans, subscriptions, usage, orders, payments, credits
docs.text: A plan (for example Free or Pro) has versions. Each version has a price and a list of features with limits. A subscription links a user (or an organization) to one plan version. Usage rows count how much of a limited feature has been used in the current period. Credit packs are one-time purchases of extra usage, and credit balances hold what was bought. Orders and payments record checkout through Razorpay, for subscriptions and credit packs alike. Design: Commerce.

Entity: plan.entity.ts.

A priced version of a plan. Changing a price creates a new version so old subscribers keep their terms. Entity: plan-version.entity.ts.

Null = never expires. Always null for recurring versions.

FeatureKey Meaning AI_ASSESSMENT Number of AI assessment generations (a limit) AI_LEARNING_ROADMAP Number of AI roadmaps (a limit) AI_MODEL Which AI model the plan uses (an enum setting) ALLOWED_QUESTION_TYPES Comma-separated question types the plan may generate, for example mcq,coding

Indexed. display_name varchar(150) no Per-version label description text yes null feature_value varchar(255) no A number, "unlimited", a model code or a list, depending on type type enum PlanFeatureType no limit limit: a usage quota (a non-numeric value means unlimited). enum: a setting, never consumed. reset_period int yes null Days between usage resets. Null = never resets.

docs.title: subscriptions
docs.text:
Links a user, or an organization, to a plan version. Entity: subscription.entity.ts.

Column Type Null Default Notes id int no auto PK user_id int no FK, CASCADE. Indexed. Always the purchaser. organization_id int yes null FK, CASCADE. Indexed. Set for an organization's subscription. plan_version_id int no FK, CASCADE. Indexed. The plan is reached through the version. status enum SubscriptionStatus no See below starts_at timestamptz no expires_at timestamptz yes null Null for a ONE_TIME purchase with no expiry_days cancelled_at timestamptz yes null auto_renew boolean no true false for ONE_TIME

Timestamps: all three.

SubscriptionStatus Meaning PENDING Checkout started, not paid ACTIVE In use SUSPENDED Replaced: when a new personal plan is paid, other active personal subscriptions are suspended (PaymentsService.markPaymentCaptured()) PAST_DUE, CANCELLED, EXPIRED Defined for renewals and cancellation

A user with no active personal subscription gets a free one created on demand (SubscriptionsService.createFreeSubscription(), called from UsageService.consume() and from email verification).

Indexed. used int no 0 period_start date no period_end date no A far-future date when reset_period is null

docs.title: orders
docs.text:
What the user is buying. Entity: order.entity.ts.

Column Type Null Default Notes id int no auto PK user_id int no FK, CASCADE. Indexed. resource_type enum OrderResourceType no SUBSCRIPTION or CREDIT (renamed from AI_CREDITS by 20261027000002) resource_id int no Id of the thing bought: a subscriptions.id, or a credit_packs.id for CREDIT. No FK: it is polymorphic. total_amount decimal(10,2) no currency varchar(3) no provider enum PaymentProvider no RAZORPAY (in use), STRIPE (enum only, no integration) provider_order_id varchar(255) no Our checkout reference chk_<uuid>; the Razorpay order id is on the payment. UQ_orders_provider_order_id status enum OrderStatus no PENDING, PAID, FAILED, FULFILLED (see below) metadata jsonb yes null null for SUBSCRIPTION. For CREDIT, CreditOrderMetadata: { creditPackId, featureId, quantity, aiModelCode }, what the pack held at purchase. expires_at timestamptz no

Timestamps: created_at, updated_at. Index IDX_orders_resource_type_resource_id on (resource_type, resource_id).

status Set when PENDING Checkout created the order PAID Its payment was captured. Moves on to FULFILLED in the same transaction; stays PAID only for a CREDIT order with no credit metadata. FULFILLED What it bought was granted: the subscription activated, or the credits added FAILED Its payment failed while the order was still PENDING. A later capture of the same Razorpay order still moves it to PAID.

20261029000000-backfill-order-statuses.ts brought older rows in line: captured subscription orders to FULFILLED, and pending orders whose latest payment failed to FAILED.

docs.title: payments
docs.text:
One payment try against an order. Entity: payment.entity.ts.

Column Type Null Default Notes id int no auto PK order_id int no FK, CASCADE. Indexed. amount decimal(10,2) no currency varchar(3) no provider enum PaymentProvider no provider_order_id varchar(255) yes null Unique where not null provider_payment_id varchar(255) yes null Unique where not null status enum PaymentStatus no PENDING, SUCCESS, FAILED, REFUNDED failure_reason text yes null paid_at timestamptz yes null

Timestamps: created_at, updated_at.

On a captured payment, in one transaction: the payment becomes SUCCESS and the order PAID. Then, for a subscription, other active personal subscriptions become SUSPENDED, the ordered one ACTIVE, and the order FULFILLED; for credits, the balance grows and the order becomes FULFILLED. On a failed payment, in one transaction: the payment becomes FAILED, and the order FAILED if it was still PENDING.

Column Type Null Default Notes id int no auto PK provider varchar(50) no event_id varchar(255) no Unique. docs.title: credit_packs
docs.text:
The catalog of credits on sale, managed by admins. Entity: credit-pack.entity.ts.

Column Type Null Default Notes id int no auto PK. Checkout takes this id. name varchar(100) no description text yes null feature_id int no FK features.id, CASCADE. IDX_credit_packs_feature_id. Never AI_MODEL or ALLOWED_QUESTION_TYPES (the API refuses settings). ai_model_code varchar(150) yes null The model the credits run on, by ai_models.code. null = the free plan's AI_MODEL. A code, not an FK: a removed model falls back to the default. quantity int no Units of the feature per pack price decimal(10,2) no currency varchar(3) no is_active boolean no true false takes the pack off sale. There is no delete endpoint. sort_order int no 0 IDX_credit_packs_sort_order

docs.title: user_feature_credits
docs.text:
A purchased credit balance: one row per owner, feature and AI model. Entity: user-feature-credit.entity.ts.

Column Type Null Default Notes id int no auto PK user_id int no FK, CASCADE. Indexed. organization_id int yes null FK, CASCADE. Indexed. Always null today: only personal credits are sold. feature_id int no FK, CASCADE. Indexed. ai_model_code varchar(150) yes null Copied from the pack. null = the free plan's model. granted int no 0 Bought in total used int no 0 Spent. granted - used is what is left.

Timestamps: all three. Four partial unique indexes keep one row per owner, feature and model, with separate indexes for a null and a named model (a plain unique index would let null-model rows repeat):

Index Columns Where UQ_user_feature_credits_user_id_feature_id (user_id, feature_id) organization_id IS NULL AND ai_model_code IS NULL UQ_user_feature_credits_user_id_feature_id_ai_model_code (user_id, feature_id, ai_model_code) organization_id IS NULL AND ai_model_code IS NOT NULL UQ_user_feature_credits_organization_id_feature_id (organization_id, feature_id) organization_id IS NOT NULL AND ai_model_code IS NULL UQ_user_feature_credits_org_id_feature_id_ai_model_code (organization_id, feature_id, ai_model_code) organization_id IS NOT NULL AND ai_model_code IS NOT NULL

Grants are an INSERT ... ON CONFLICT on the matching index, so two first grants for the same user cannot both insert a row.
