docs.text:
Entity: learning-roadmap-node.entity.ts.

Column Type Null Default Notes id int no auto PK. Stays the same across modifications. learning_roadmap_id int no FK, CASCADE. Indexed. type enum NodeType no knowledge (learn) or practice (test yourself) title varchar(255) no description text yes null Learning material or practice brief position_index int no 0-based order status enum NodeStatus no not_started not_started, in_progress, completed, skipped. Owned by the learner; generation never changes it. completed_at timestamptz yes null meta jsonb yes null KnowledgeNodeMeta & PracticeNodeMeta: resources, estimated minutes, concepts; for practice nodes assessmentId, questionCount, coversNodeIds

Timestamps: created_at only. Unique UQ_learning_roadmap_nodes_position on (learning_roadmap_id, position_index). Index (learning_roadmap_id, status) for progress counts.

A practice node points to the assessment generated for it through meta.assessmentId. This is an app-level link with no FK.

docs.title: learning_node_edges
docs.text:
Links between nodes. They make the roadmap a graph (a DAG: a graph without loops) instead of a list. Entity: learning-node-edge.entity.ts.

Column Type Null Default Notes id int no auto PK roadmap_id int no FK, CASCADE. Copied from the nodes so a whole graph loads with one indexed query. from_node_id int no FK nodes, CASCADE. Indexed. to_node_id int no FK nodes, CASCADE. Indexed. meta jsonb yes null EdgeMeta: label, and an optional condition { type: 'score', operator: 'gte' or 'lt', value } for branching after a practice node

Timestamps: created_at only. Unique (roadmap_id, from_node_id, to_node_id). CHECK from_node_id <> to_node_id (in the migration only).

jsonb shapes for all three tables: src/learning-roadmaps/interfaces/roadmap-meta.interface.ts.

docs.title: learning_roadmap_templates
docs.text:
A ready-made goal a learner can pick instead of typing one. Entity: learning-roadmap-template.entity.ts.

Column Type Null Default Notes id int no auto PK uid varchar(8) no Unique among live rows slug varchar(180) no Unique among live rows name varchar(150) no description text no For the picker. Not sent to the model. goal text no Sent to the analysis job as if the learner typed it visibility enum RoadmapTemplateVisibility no private public, private is_active boolean no true created_by int no FK, CASCADE. Indexed.

Timestamps: all three.

docs.title: 9. Notifications and newsletters
docs.text:
Email templates are not stored in the database. They are TypeScript files in src/notifications/email/templates/ (verification, welcome, password reset, invitations, newsletter). The only table here is newsletters. Design: Notifications.

erDiagram
    newsletters {
        int id PK
        varchar subject
        text body_html
        enum status
        timestamptz scheduled_at
        int recipient_count
        int sent_count
        int failed_count
        int created_by FK
    }
    users ||--o{ newsletters : "writes"

docs.title: newsletters
docs.text:
An email sent to every subscribed user, now or at a set time. Entity: newsletter.entity.ts.

Column Type Null Default Notes id int no auto PK subject varchar(200) no body_html text no body_text text yes null Plain-text version status enum NewsletterStatus no SCHEDULED Indexed scheduled_at timestamptz no "Send now" stores the current time. Indexed. started_at timestamptz yes null Set when a dispatcher claims the row sent_at timestamptz yes null recipient_count int yes null sent_count, failed_count int no 0 error text yes null For operators only created_by int no FK, CASCADE. Indexed.

Timestamps: all three.

NewsletterStatus Meaning SCHEDULED Waiting for scheduled_at. The only status the dispatcher claims from. SENDING Claimed and being delivered SENT Done. Check failed_count: a partial failure still lands here. FAILED Could not be attempted, or every recipient failed

docs.title: 10. Platform: feature flags and support tickets
docs.text:
Design: Platform services.

erDiagram
    feature_flags {
        int id PK
        varchar key UK
        text description
        boolean enabled
        int updated_by FK
    }
    feature_flag_roles {
        int feature_flag_id PK
        int role_id PK
    }
    support_tickets {
        int id PK
        int user_id FK
        enum topic
        text query
        enum status
    }
    feature_flags ||--o{ feature_flag_roles : "limited to"
    roles ||--o{ feature_flag_roles : "unlocks"
    users ||--o{ support_tickets : "files"

docs.title: feature_flags
docs.text:
The current state of one feature flag. Keys and defaults come from code (FEATURE_FLAG_DEFINITIONS); admins only change enabled and the role list. Entity: feature-flag.entity.ts.

Column Type Null Default Notes id int no auto PK key varchar(100) no UQ_feature_flags_key description text no enabled boolean no true false turns it off for everyone updated_by int yes null FK users.id, SET NULL. Null when only the seeder wrote it.

Timestamps: created_at, updated_at.

How a flag is read: enabled = false → off for everyone. enabled = true with no roles → on for everyone. enabled = true with roles → on only for users holding one of those platform roles.

docs.title: feature_flag_roles
docs.text:
Which platform roles a flag is limited to. Entity: feature-flag-role.entity.ts.

Column Type Null Default Notes feature_flag_id int no Composite PK, FK, CASCADE role_id int no Composite PK, FK roles.id, CASCADE. IDX_feature_flag_roles_role_id

No timestamps. This is the only table with a composite primary key.

docs.title: support_tickets
docs.text:
A help request from a user. Entity: support-ticket.entity.ts.

Column Type Null Default Notes id int no auto PK user_id int no FK, CASCADE. Indexed. topic enum SupportTicketTopic no BILLING, TECHNICAL, ACCOUNT, ASSESSMENT, FEEDBACK, OTHER query text no status enum SupportTicketStatus no OPEN OPEN, IN_PROGRESS, RESOLVED, CLOSED. Indexed.

Timestamps: all three. Tickets are not linked to orders or assessments; the topic is only a label.

docs.title: Modules with no tables
docs.text: health, stats, events (WebSocket gateway), rate-limiter (counters live in Redis), code-execution and schedulers have no tables of their own. stats reads other tables with raw SQL.

docs.title: Real foreign keys between domains
docs.text:
From To Via On delete Almost every table users user_id, created_by, owner_user_id CASCADE jobs, llm_audit, feature_flags, *.invited_by, assessment_attempts.rejected_by users various SET NULL (the row outlives the user) assessments, subscriptions, user_feature_usage, roles organizations organization_id (nullable) CASCADE organization_members roles role_id RESTRICT feature_flag_roles roles role_id CASCADE assessments, learning_roadmaps jobs job_id SET NULL llm_audit jobs, ai_models job_id, ai_model_id SET NULL assessment_attempt_responses assessments_questions assessment_question_id CASCADE

A null organization_id always means "personal". A set one means "belongs to that organization".

These links exist only in code. The database does not check them.

Link Where it lives Why no FK Conversation → attempt or roadmap ai_conversations.context_type + context_id Polymorphic: points to different tables Order → subscription or credit pack orders.resource_type + resource_id Polymorphic Credit pack or balance → AI model credit_packs.ai_model_code, user_feature_credits.ai_model_code By code, so a removed model falls back to the default Practice node → assessment learning_roadmap_nodes.meta.assessmentId Lives inside jsonb Job → assessment, attempt, roadmap, org jobs.payload (assessmentId, attemptId, orgUid and so on) Payload shape depends on job type Roadmap → its jobs per phase learning_roadmaps.meta.analysisJobId, generationJobId, modificationJobIds History kept in jsonb; job_id holds the latest Webhook → payment webhook_events.payload Raw provider data

docs.title: Known schema gaps
docs.text:
These were found by comparing the entities with a database migrated to the latest version (typeorm schema:log, which only prints SQL) and by reading the migrations. None of them breaks the app today, but they matter when you change a table or run migration:generate.

Defined in a migration but not on the entity. The database has them; the entity does not say so. migration:generate will try to drop them, so remove those lines by hand.

What Table Created in Unique (user_id, assessment_id) assessment_attempts 20260618000004-add-uid-to-assessment-attempts.ts FK job_id → jobs (SET NULL) assessments 20260902000001-add-job-id-to-assessments.ts FK job_id → jobs and FK current_node_id → nodes (SET NULL) learning_roadmaps 20260902000002-add-job-id-to-learning-roadmaps.ts, 20260827000000-create-learning-roadmaps-tables.ts CHECK difficulty BETWEEN 1 AND 5 assessment_sections 20261014000014-add-difficulty-to-assessment-sections.ts CHECK from_node_id <> to_node_id learning_node_edges 20260827000000-create-learning-roadmaps-tables.ts Index on user_id, and ON DELETE CASCADE on its FK refresh_tokens 20260611000000-CreateRefreshTokensTable.ts Indexes on both FK columns assessment_prompt_tags 20260723000001-create-assessment-prompts-tables.ts

Declared on the entity but missing in the database.

  • IDX_learning_node_edges_roadmap (learning-node-edge.entity.ts). Lookups by roadmap_id still use the unique index, which starts with that column.

Foreign keys with no index. Deleting the parent row, or joining on these columns, scans the table: assessments.job_id, learning_roadmaps.job_id, learning_roadmaps.current_node_id, assessment_attempts.rejected_by, organization_members.invited_by, feature_flags.updated_by.

No unique index where the code expects one row.

  • assessment_attempt_responses (attempt_id, assessment_question_id): two parallel saves of the same answer could create two rows.
  • user_feature_usage (user_id, organization_id, plan_feature_id): the row lock in UsageService.consume() does not cover the very first insert.

Naming drift. Many FKs were created with readable names (FK_assessments_created_by) while the entities let TypeORM pick hashed names. Some unique constraints differ the same way (plans.code, webhook_events.event_id, users.phone_number, the users OAuth index). Because of this, migration:generate outputs long lists of drop-and-recreate statements that change nothing.

Stale comment. permissions.entity.ts still calls *:* "the super-wildcard", but that key is no longer granted or checked.

Nullable settings and column types match between the entities and the database. No entity column is missing a migration.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: This page takes you from a fresh clone to a running backend with data in it. It also lists every environment variable the code reads.

docs.title: 1. Prerequisites
docs.text:
Tool Version Why you need it Required? Node.js + npm 20 (the Docker image uses node:20-alpine) Runs the NestJS app, scripts, and tests. Yes PostgreSQL 15 (compose uses postgres:15-alpine) Main database. Yes Redis 7 Rate-limit buckets and the read cache. The app still starts if Redis is down (both uses "fail open"). Strongly recommended RabbitMQ 4 with the management plugin Background jobs: AI generation, evaluation, roadmaps, CSV invite import. Yes (the app connects at boot) Docker + Docker Compose Any recent Easiest way to run Postgres, Redis, and RabbitMQ. Optional An LLM API key OpenAI by default AI generation, descriptive grading, roadmaps, assistant. Needed for AI features Code runner Piston (self-hosted, separate piston repo) or an OnlineCompiler.io key Running and judging coding questions. Needed for coding questions SMTP server Any (Mailtrap, Gmail app password, etc.) Verification, reset, and invite emails. Its env vars are required at boot S3 bucket AWS S3, or MinIO / LocalStack locally Stores uploaded invitation CSVs. Its env vars are required at boot Razorpay test keys - Checkout and payment webhooks. Key ID and secret are required at boot

Required at boot

Some services read their variables with getOrThrow in their constructor, so the app will not start without them, even if you never use that feature. These are: the DATABASE_* vars, RABBITMQ_URL, SMTP_HOST, SMTP_USER, SMTP_PASSWORD, EMAIL_FROM, AWS_REGION, AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, AWS_S3_BUCKET, RAZORPAY_KEY_ID, RAZORPAY_KEY_SECRET, and GOOGLE_OAUTH2_CLIENT_ID. The JWT variables are needed as soon as anyone logs in. Put a placeholder value in when you do not need a feature.

docs.title: 2. Quick start
docs.text:
git clone <backend repo url> Test-Flow-Backend
cd Test-Flow-Backend
npm ci
cp .env.example .env          # then fill in the values (see section 3)

docs.title: Option A: run only the services in Docker, the app on your machine
docs.text:
docker compose up -d db redis rabbitmq

The compose file maps the ports like this, so update .env to match:

Service Host port Notes Postgres 5434 Set DATABASE_PORT=5434, DATABASE_HOST=localhost. Redis 6380 Set REDIS_PORT=6380. RabbitMQ 5672 (AMQP), 15672 (UI) RABBITMQ_URL=amqp://guest:guest@localhost:5672. Management UI at http://localhost:15672 (guest/guest).

Then:

npm run migration:run
npm run seed
npm run dev          # nest start --watch, on PORT (default 3000)

docs.title: Option B: run everything in Docker
docs.text:
docker compose up --build

This builds the dev stage of the Dockerfile and mounts ./src and ./tests, so code changes hot-reload. entrypoint.dev.sh waits for Postgres, runs npm run migration:run, then npm run dev. The compose file overrides DATABASE_HOST, REDIS_HOST, and RABBITMQ_URL so the app can reach the other containers. If you add an npm dependency, run docker compose up --build again.

File Used for docker-compose.yml Local full stack (app + db + redis + rabbitmq). Also used by the CI smoke test. docker-compose.dev.yml The shared dev server. It pulls a prebuilt image and has no database service (the dev DB is external). Dockerfile Multi-stage. dev stage for hot reload; the last (runtime) stage ships only dist/ and production deps. entrypoint.sh Runtime image: wait for Postgres, migration:run:prod, start:prod.

docs.title: Check that it works
docs.text: URL What you should see GET http://localhost:3000/ping A public ping response. GET http://localhost:3000/health Status of database, redis, and rabbitmq. http://localhost:3000/api/docs Swagger UI (asks for basic auth, see below).

docs.title: 3. Environment variables
docs.text:
The app loads .env through ConfigModule.forRoot({ isGlobal: true }) in src/app.module.ts. Code reads values through ConfigService. A few places read process.env directly because they run before Nest starts: src/main.ts (port, Swagger), src/config/database/data-source.ts (the TypeORM CLI), and the scripts.

Never commit real secrets

.env is git-ignored. Only .env.example is committed, and it must hold placeholders only. Ask a teammate for dev keys.

docs.title: App and docs
docs.text:
Variable Meaning PORT HTTP port. Default 3000. NODE_ENV Environment name. The question generator checks for the exact value testing: then it picks random questions from the bank instead of calling an LLM (see the note below). SWAGGER_USER / SWAGGER_PASS Basic-auth login for /api/docs. FRONTEND_URL Frontend base URL, used for links in emails. Default https://app.testflow.com. LOG_LEVEL Listed in .env.example but not read by any code today.

NODE_ENV=test vs testing

.env.example says test turns off LLM calls, but src/assessments/questions/questions.service.ts checks for testing. Use testing if you want to skip the LLM.

docs.title: Database (PostgreSQL)
docs.text: Variable Meaning DATABASE_HOST Host name. DATABASE_PORT Port (5434 if you use the compose Postgres from your machine). DATABASE_USERNAME / DATABASE_PASSWORD Login. DATABASE_NAME Database name (compose default testflow). DATABASE_SSL true to connect over SSL (with rejectUnauthorized: false).

docs.title: Auth (JWT and Google)
docs.text:
Variable Meaning JWT_ACCESS_SECRET Signs access tokens. Also used to check WebSocket tokens. JWT_REFRESH_SECRET Signs refresh tokens. JWT_ACCESS_EXPIRY Access token lifetime in seconds (the code converts the value with +value). JWT_REFRESH_EXPIRY Refresh token lifetime in seconds. JWT_EMAIL_VERIFICATION_SECRET / JWT_EMAIL_VERIFICATION_EXPIRY Secret and lifetime (seconds) of the email verification link. JWT_PASSWORD_RESET_SECRET / JWT_PASSWORD_RESET_EXPIRY Secret and lifetime (seconds) of the password reset link. Keep it short. GOOGLE_OAUTH2_CLIENT_ID Google client ID, used as the audience when verifying Google ID tokens on POST /v1/auth/google.

Use plain numbers for JWT expiry

.env.example shows 15m and 7d for the access and refresh expiry, but src/identity/auth/auth.service.ts turns them into numbers. +"15m" is NaN, so use seconds, for example 900 and 604800.

docs.title: Redis
docs.text: Variable Meaning REDIS_HOST / REDIS_PORT Shared by both Redis connections. REDIS_PASSWORD Leave blank for a local Redis with no auth. REDIS_DB Logical DB for rate-limit buckets. Default 0. REDIS_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_MS Per-command timeout for the rate limiter. Default 200. REDIS_CACHE_DB Logical DB for the read cache. Default 1. Separate so a cache flush never wipes rate limits. REDIS_CACHE_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_MS Per-command timeout for the cache. Default 500.

docs.title: RabbitMQ
docs.text: Variable Meaning RABBITMQ_URL AMQP URL, for example amqp://guest:guest@localhost:5672. CONSUMER true (default) means this instance also consumes queues. false means it only publishes. Use false for an API-only instance.

docs.title: LLM providers
docs.text:
Models live in the ai_models table. Each row stores the name of the env var that holds its key (apiKeyVariable) and, optionally, its base URL (baseUrlVariable). src/ai/ai-model-registry.service.ts reads those names at runtime. So the variables below only matter if a row points at them.

Variable Meaning OPENAI_API_KEY OpenAI key (used by the default seeded model). OPENAI_MODEL Model code the seeder registers as the default ai_models row. Default gpt-4. OPENAI_BASE_URL Optional base URL for an OpenAI-compatible host. ANTHROPIC_API_KEY Anthropic key, if you add an Anthropic model row. GOOGLE_API_KEY Google GenAI key, if you add a Google model row.

docs.title: Code execution
docs.text: Variable Meaning CODE_RUNNER_PROVIDER online-compiler (default) or piston. ONLINE_COMPILER_API_KEY OnlineCompiler.io REST key. If unset, runs are refused. ONLINE_COMPILER_BASE_URL Optional override. ONLINE_COMPILER_MAX_CONCURRENCY Parallel runs per key (the API allows 4). ONLINE_COMPILER_TIMEOUT_MS HTTP timeout. Default 40000. PISTON_API_KEY Raw secret shared with your Piston server (the runner sends its SHA-256). If unset, runs are refused. PISTON_BASE_URL Default http://127.0.0.1:2000. From Docker on a Mac, use http://host.docker.internal:2000. PISTON_MAX_CONCURRENCY Parallel runs. Default 4. PISTON_TIMEOUT_MS HTTP timeout. Default 60000. PISTON_MAX_RUN_TIMEOUT_MS / PISTON_MAX_RUN_CPU_TIME_MS / PISTON_MAX_RUN_MEMORY_MB Piston's own per-run limits. Requests are clamped to these so Piston does not reply 400.

docs.title: Email (SMTP)
docs.text: Variable Meaning SMTP_HOST SMTP server. SMTP_PORT Default 587. SMTP_SECURE true for TLS on connect (usually port 465). SMTP_USER / SMTP_PASSWORD SMTP login. EMAIL_FROM Sender address.

docs.title: Payments (Razorpay)
docs.text: Variable Meaning RAZORPAY_KEY_ID / RAZORPAY_KEY_SECRET API keys used to create orders. RAZORPAY_WEBHOOK_SECRET Secret used to verify the x-razorpay-signature header on POST /webhooks/razorpay. CHECKOUT_ORDER_TTL_MINUTES Minutes a pending checkout order stays valid.

docs.title: Newsletters
docs.text: Variable Meaning NEWSLETTER_SCHEDULER_ENABLED false stops the every-minute cron from sending. Use it on any machine that shares a DB with real subscribers. NEWSLETTER_DISPATCH_BATCH_SIZE Due newsletters claimed per pass. Default 5. NEWSLETTER_RECIPIENT_BATCH_SIZE Recipients per BCC email. Default 100.

docs.title: File storage (S3)
docs.text: Variable Meaning AWS_REGION Bucket region. AWS_S3_BUCKET Bucket name. AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID / AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY Credentials. AWS_S3_ENDPOINT Blank for AWS. Set it (for example http://localhost:9000) for MinIO or LocalStack; path-style URLs are turned on automatically.

docs.title: Scripts only
docs.text: Variable Meaning DEFAULT_PASSWORD_EXPORT_PATH Where the add-default-password-to-users migration writes its CSV of generated passwords. Defaults to the current folder.

docs.title: 4. Swagger (API docs)
docs.text:
• URL: http://localhost:3000/api/docs.
  • Protected by HTTP basic auth using SWAGGER_USER and SWAGGER_PASS (see src/main.ts).
  • To call protected routes, log in with POST /v1/auth/login, copy the access token, and click Authorize (access-token bearer scheme). Swagger remembers it (persistAuthorization).
  • Admin routes are grouped by tags such as Admin · Users.

docs.title: 5. Database migrations
docs.text:
The schema is managed only by migrations in src/migrations/. synchronize is off. The CLI uses src/config/database/data-source.ts.

Command What it does npm run migration:run Apply all pending migrations. npm run migration:show List migrations and which are applied. npm run migration:revert Undo the last migration. npm run migration:generate -- src/migrations/<Name> Create a migration from the diff between entities and the DB. npm run migration:run:prod (and show:prod, revert:prod) Same, but from compiled dist/. Used in the Docker runtime image.

Adding an entity

New entities live in src/common/entities/ and must be added to both src/config/database/data-source.ts (for the CLI) and src/config/database/database.module.ts (for the app). Then generate a migration. Read the typeorm-migrations and typeorm-entity-patterns skills first.

docs.title: 6. Seeders and scripts
docs.text:
Run these after migrations, in this order:

Command What it does npm run seed Runs src/seeder.ts, which calls DatabaseSeeder (src/seeders/index.ts). It seeds roles, permissions, super-admin permissions, org role permissions, plan features, plans, the default AI model (from OPENAI_MODEL), and feature flags. npm run bootstrap-admin -- --email <email> --password <password> Creates the first super_admin user. Needs npm run seed first. Safe to run twice. npm run seed:assessment-templates Seeds assessment templates from src/config/database/dummy-data/assessment-templates.ts. npm run seed:roadmap-templates Seeds learning roadmap templates from src/config/database/dummy-data/learning-roadmap-templates.ts.

The two template seeders accept --owner-email <email> (default owner is the system user), --dry-run, and --help. Some also accept --update to overwrite existing rows.

Inside the runtime Docker image

The ts-node scripts do not work in the slim runtime image. Use node dist/seeder.js and node dist/scripts/bootstrap-admin.js there.

docs.title: 7. Tests
docs.text:
Kind Where Command Unit tests/unit/<module>/... mirroring src/, files named *.spec.ts npm run test (watch: npm run test:watch) Coverage Collected from src/** into coverage/ npm run test:cov E2E tests/*.e2e-spec.ts, config in tests/jest-e2e.json npm run test:e2e Debug Runs Jest in band with the inspector npm run test:debug

Unit tests mock repositories, ConfigService, and the LLM layer. See the jest-mock-patterns, test-naming-conventions, and e2e-test-setup skills in .claude/skills/.

docs.title: 8. Lint and format
docs.text:
Command What it does npm run lint ESLint over src and tests, with --fix. npm run format Prettier over src/**/*.ts and tests/**/*.ts. npm run build Compile to dist/ with the Nest CLI. Good final check.

A Husky pre-commit hook runs npm run format. CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml) runs lint, type checks, unit tests, build, migrations, and a container smoke test. CD (cd.yml) deploys the dev branch.

docs.title: 9. Useful tips
docs.text:
• Code navigation. The repo is indexed by CodeGraph. Run npm run codegraph explore "<symbol or question>" to see a symbol's source and its callers.
  • Project skills. .claude/skills/ holds the team's rules for folders, entities, migrations, validation, errors, guards, pagination, transactions, Swagger, and logging. Read the relevant one before you write code.
  • API-only instance. Set CONSUMER=false to run an instance that publishes jobs but does not consume them.
  • Watch the queues. The RabbitMQ UI at http://localhost:15672 shows each queue and its message count. See Architecture for the full list.

docs.title: TestFlow — Business Overview
docs.text: TestFlow is a SaaS online assessment platform. It helps organizations create, deliver, and score tests at scale. It also lets any individual practice for an exam, a certification, or an interview on demand, by typing a single prompt.

docs.title: The problem it solves
docs.text: Hiring teams, schools, and training providers spend a lot of time writing tests, sending them out, and marking them by hand. At the same time, people preparing for competitive exams or interviews struggle to find realistic practice that fits their exact topic. TestFlow solves both problems on one platform.

docs.title: Who it is for
docs.text: Audience What they use TestFlow for Recruiters and HR teams Screening candidates with skill tests (MCQ, coding, written answers). Educators and training providers Testing learners across a course or program. Enterprises Internal certifications, compliance tests, and performance reviews, run inside an organization account. Individual learners Practicing any topic on demand and following an AI learning roadmap.

docs.title: Core value
docs.text:
1. AI-powered test creation. The creator describes what to test. An LLM writes the questions, answer options, correct answers, and coding test cases.
  2. Flexible configuration. Creators choose question types (MCQ, coding, descriptive), sections, question counts, difficulty, positive and negative marks, duration, time windows, and participant limits.
  3. Automatic scoring. MCQs are scored by rule, coding answers are run against test cases in a sandbox, and descriptive answers are graded by an LLM. All of it happens in the background after submission.
  4. Participant management. Invite people by email, let them register, track each attempt, review responses, reject a suspicious attempt, and show a leaderboard.
  5. Teams and roles. Organizations with owners, admins, and members. A permission system controls who can do what, both platform-wide and inside each organization.
  6. Subscription model. Plans and quotas decide how many AI assessments and roadmaps a user can generate, which question types they can use, and which AI model they get.

docs.title: Key use case: prompt to practice
docs.text:
"I want to practice for UPSC Prelims. Give me a mock test right now."

Any individual can type a prompt and sit a full, timed exam a few moments later. No admin setup or question bank is needed.

flowchart LR
    A["Learner types a prompt"] --> B["Backend plans sections and starts background jobs"]
    B --> C["LLM writes questions per section"]
    C --> D["Assessment becomes ready"]
    D --> E["Learner takes a timed attempt"]
    E --> F["Background evaluation scores it"]
    F --> G["Result, analytics, and AI chat about the attempt"]

Why it matters for the business

  • It opens a large B2C channel. Any student or job seeker can become a user without an organization.
  • It drives repeat usage. Learners come back for new topics, which supports retention and plan upgrades.
  • It makes TestFlow a universal practice platform, not only an enterprise testing tool.
  • It builds a data asset. Performance data across topics can power adaptive learning later.

docs.title: Business model
docs.text: TestFlow is a B2B and B2C SaaS. Revenue comes from tiered plans. A plan version lists features with limits, such as AI_ASSESSMENT (AI assessments per period), AI_LEARNING_ROADMAP, AI_MODEL (which LLM you get), and ALLOWED_QUESTION_TYPES. Payments go through Razorpay. See Commerce.

docs.title: What is built today
docs.text:
This table reflects the backend code as of the date at the top of this page.

Area Status Notes Email + password auth Built Signup, email verification, login, refresh tokens, logout, forgot and reset password. See Auth. Google sign-in Built POST /v1/auth/google verifies a Google ID token. GitHub exists only as an enum value; there is no GitHub login flow. RBAC Built Platform roles (super_admin, beta_tester) and org roles (org_owner, org_admin, org_member) share one permission catalog. See RBAC. Organizations Built Create an org, invite members one by one or by CSV upload (processed in the background), manage roles, suspend orgs (admin). See Organizations. Manual assessments Built Create, edit, add questions, publish, invite, register, and manage participants. See Assessments. AI assessment generation Built LLM-backed, through RabbitMQ. Auto or manual section layout, one job per section, retries, idempotency keys, and quota refunds on failure. See AI Assessment Generation. Question types Built MCQ, coding (with test cases), and descriptive. See Questions & Tags. Assessment templates and saved prompts Built Reusable section layouts and public or private prompts with tags. Attempts Built Start, answer, change answers, submit, results, analytics, leaderboard, and creator review or reject. See Attempts. Evaluation Built Background scoring split into MCQ, coding, and descriptive child jobs. See Evaluation. Code execution Built Live "run code" over WebSocket and judging at evaluation time, on Piston (self-hosted) or OnlineCompiler.io. See Code Execution. Multiple LLM providers Built OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google through LangChain. Models live in the ai_models table and are picked per plan. See AI Layer. AI assistant Built Chat over WebSocket with read-only tools for assessments, attempts, roadmaps, and the user's profile. See AI Assistant. Learning roadmaps Built Intent analysis, requirement questions, graph generation, graph edits by prompt, node progress, notes, and node practice tests. See Learning Roadmaps. Plans, subscriptions, usage Built Plan versions with features and limits, checkout, and usage counters. Payments Built (Razorpay only) Razorpay orders and signed webhooks. STRIPE and AI_CREDITS exist in enums but have no flow yet. Email Built SMTP via Nodemailer, with admin template previews. See Notifications. Platform services Built Rate limiting, feature flags, health checks, admin stats, newsletters (cron), support tickets, and S3 storage. See Platform Services.

docs.title: API Reference v1
docs.text:
This page lists every HTTP route in the TestFlow backend. Use it to find an endpoint fast. For how a feature works end to end, follow the link at the top of each section.

There are 178 routes in 40 controllers.

docs.title: Base URL and versioning
docs.text:
• There is no global prefix and no Nest versioning. Each controller puts v1/ in its own path, for example @Controller('v1/assessments').
  • So almost every route starts with /v1/....
  • Three routes have no v1: GET /ping, GET /health, and POST /webhooks/razorpay.
  • The server listens on PORT (default 3000). CORS is open to any origin, with credentials.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
Every route needs a valid access token unless it is marked @Public(). Send the token in the Authorization header:

GET /v1/auth/me
Authorization: Bearer <accessToken>
  • You get tokens from POST /v1/auth/login, /signup, /google, or /refresh.
  • Public routes need no header. If you send a token to a public route, it is ignored. The route does not know who you are.
  • A missing or bad token returns 401.

The global guards run in this order on every request:

  1. JwtAuthGuard checks the Bearer token (skipped on @Public() routes).
  2. RateLimitGuard applies the @RateLimit() policy, if the route has one.
  3. RolesGuard checks @Roles(). Only one route uses it.
  4. OrgContextGuard loads the organization for org routes.
  5. PermissionGuard checks @Permissions() and @OrgPermissions().

docs.title: What the "Auth" column means
docs.text:
Value Meaning Public No token needed. JWT Any logged-in user. The service may still check ownership (for example, "only the creator can edit"). Perm x:y Logged-in user whose platform role grants permission x:y. Missing permission returns 403 Missing permission: x:y. Org perm x:y Route acts inside an organization. The caller must be an active member, and their org role must grant x:y. Org header Route accepts the optional x-organization-id header. See below. Role super_admin Caller must have the super_admin platform role. AI cost N Uses the shared AI generation rate-limit bucket. See Rate limits.

See RBAC for roles and permission keys.

docs.title: Organization context
docs.text:
There are two ways a route can act inside an organization.

1. Path-scoped routes (@OrgScoped())

The org uid is in the path: /v1/orgs/:orgUid/....

  • The caller must be an active member of that org.
  • @Permissions() on these routes is checked against the caller's org role, not their platform roles.
  • If the caller is not a member, the API returns 404 Organization not found. It does not return 403, so it does not reveal that the org exists.

2. Header-scoped routes (@OrgHeaderScoped())

Send the org uid in a header:

x-organization-id: org_8f3k2l
  • The header is optional.
  • Without the header, the request runs in your personal scope. @OrgPermissions() is not checked. A plain @Permissions() is checked against your platform roles.
  • With the header, you must be an active member (else 404). Both @Permissions() and @OrgPermissions() are checked against your org role.

See Organizations.

docs.title: Success envelope
docs.text:
Every successful response (except 204) uses ApiResponse:

{
  "success": true,
  "message": "Assessments fetched successfully.",
  "data": [ { "id": 12, "title": "JavaScript Basics" } ],
  "meta": { "total": 42, "page": 1, "limit": 20, "totalPages": 3 }
}
  • message is always present.
  • data is always present. It is null when there is nothing to return.
  • meta is only present on list endpoints (and a few others, like the leaderboard).
  • 204 No Content responses have no body.

docs.title: Error envelope
docs.text:
All errors go through HttpExceptionFilter:

{
  "success": false,
  "message": "Missing permission: questions:create"
}
  • There is no nested error object and no statusCode field. Use the HTTP status code.
  • If the thrown exception carries extra fields, they are added at the top level. For example, GET /health returns data with its 503.
  • Any unexpected error returns 500 with "message": "Internal server error". The details are only logged on the server.
  • Business-rule errors from the domain layer are mapped to 409, 400, 403, or 422.

Common status codes:

Code When 200 OK 201 Created 202 Accepted. Work was queued. Poll the returned job id with GET /v1/jobs/:id. 204 Done, no body (most deletes) 400 Validation failed, or a bad request 401 Missing, invalid, or expired token 403 Missing permission or role, or not the owner 404 Not found, or not a member of the org 409 Conflict (duplicate, wrong state) 422 Business rule broken 429 Rate limit hit 503 A dependency is down, or a job could not be queued

docs.title: Validation errors
docs.text:
The global ValidationPipe runs with whitelist, forbidNonWhitelisted, and transform turned on.

  • Unknown fields in the body or query are rejected with 400. They are not silently dropped.
  • Query strings are converted to the right type (numbers, booleans).
  • All validation messages are joined into one string with ,:
{
  "success": false,
  "message": "email must be a valid email address, password must be at least 8 characters"
}

Path ids that must be numbers or UUIDs (ParseIntPipe, ParseUUIDPipe) also return 400 when wrong.

docs.title: Pagination
docs.text:
There are two styles. Each list endpoint uses one of them.

Page style (most lists, including most admin lists):

?page=1&limit=20
  • page starts at 1. limit defaults to 20 and is usually capped at 100.
  • meta looks like { "total": 42, "page": 1, "limit": 20, "totalPages": 3 }.

Cursor style (lists built on PaginationDto: invited assessments, participants, leaderboard, conversation messages, roadmaps, roadmap templates, org members, admin users, admin organizations):

?cursor=7&limit=20
  • cursor is the id of the last item from the previous page. Leave it out for the first page.
  • limit defaults to 20, max 50.
  • meta looks like { "nextCursor": "7", "total": 42 }. nextCursor: null means this was the last page.
  • Some endpoints add more to meta. The leaderboard adds me. Participants adds counts.

Many lists also take search, sort, and order (asc or desc). The tables below list the main ones.

docs.title: Rate limits
docs.text:
Routes are only limited when they have @RateLimit(). A method-level policy replaces the class-level one.

Tier Limit Keyed by Used for Class A 10 per 5 minutes IP Auth routes Class B 30 per minute User (IP if not logged in) Writes: create, update, submit, enrol Class C 120 per minute User (IP if not logged in) Reads, lists, polling AI generation Class B bucket, scope AI_GENERATION, each call costs 3 or 5 tokens User AI generation routes
  • Routes with the same scope share one bucket. All AI generation routes share the AI_GENERATION bucket. At cost 5, that is about 6 calls per minute.
  • Every limited response has X-RateLimit-Limit and X-RateLimit-Remaining headers.
  • When you hit the limit, you get 429 with a Retry-After header (seconds):
{
  "success": false,
  "message": "Rate limit exceeded. Please retry later."
}

docs.title: Swagger
docs.text:
• Interactive docs are at /api/docs.
  • The page is protected with HTTP Basic auth. The username and password come from SWAGGER_USER and SWAGGER_PASS.
  • Click Authorize and paste an access token to call protected routes. The token is kept across reloads.
  • The Razorpay webhook is hidden from Swagger.

docs.title: Webhooks and raw body
docs.text:
• The app is created with rawBody: true, so req.rawBody holds the exact bytes sent.
  • POST /webhooks/razorpay uses the raw body to check the x-razorpay-signature HMAC. A missing or wrong signature returns 401.
  • See Commerce.

{
  "name": "SQL Joins — Focused Practice",
  "title": "SQL Joins Practice",
  "description": "Practises the outer joins you missed most, at a gentler difficulty.",
  "prompt": "SQL joins at an intermediate level, focusing on LEFT and FULL OUTER JOIN semantics.",
  "duration": 20,
  "maxTotalQuestions": 10,

      "title": "Outer joins",
      "prompt": "LEFT and FULL OUTER JOIN results on small tables; ask what rows come back.",
      "questionType": "mcq",
      "questionCount": 10,
      "difficulty": 2,
      "positiveMark": 4,
      "negativeMark": 1

}

It is the start-ready part of an assessment template (no uid, slug, owner or visibility). To start it, send it as a manual-mode POST /v1/assessments/generate: mode: "manual", title, prompt, duration and the sections. That spends AI_ASSESSMENT as usual.

docs.title: Claude Code Architecture
docs.text: Architecture Diagram

docs.title: AI Assistant and Tools
docs.text:
The AI assistant is a chat bot inside TestFlow. A learner opens a conversation about an evaluated assessment attempt and asks questions like "Why did I get question 4 wrong?" or "What should I study next?". The assistant answers in short prose. To look up the learner's data it calls tools — small read-only functions that wrap our domain services.

This page covers the assistant loop, the tools, how conversations are stored, and the safety rules. For the model layer underneath (registry, providers, auditing) see AI layer.

docs.title: 1. Key terms
docs.text: Term Meaning Conversation One chat thread, attached to one context (an assessment attempt or a roadmap). Table ai_conversations. Message One turn in a conversation. Role user (the learner) or bot (the assistant). Table ai_conversation_messages. Tool A function the model may ask us to run, described to the model as a name, a description and a JSON Schema for its arguments. Tool call The model's reply says "run get_attempt with {attemptUid: ...}" instead of (or before) giving an answer. Tool loop Call the model → run any tools it asked for → send results back → call the model again, until it answers in plain text. requestId A correlation id the client sends with each message. It is echoed back on the reply and written on every log line.

docs.title: 2. Where the code lives
docs.text:
File Role src/ai/assistant/ai-assistant.module.ts AiAssistantModule. Imports AiModule and AiToolsModule. Imported by EventsModule. src/ai/assistant/conversation-assistant.service.ts ConversationAssistantService.answer() — the tool loop (a LangGraph graph). src/ai/prompts/conversation-assistant.prompt.ts System prompt + per-turn context prompt. src/ai/tools/ai-tools.module.ts AiToolsModule. Imports the domain modules the tools read from. src/ai/tools/ai-tools.service.ts Tool registry, definitions for the provider, argument validation, dispatch. src/ai/tools/*.tools.ts Tool definitions, grouped by domain. src/ai/tools/dto/* class-validator DTOs for each tool's arguments. src/ai/tools/conversation-context.resolver.ts Turns a stored context into ids the tools accept. src/ai/ai-conversations.service.ts Conversation and message storage and reads. src/ai/ai-conversations.controller.ts HTTP: read a conversation's messages page by page. src/events/events.gateway.ts, src/events/conversation-router.service.ts Socket.IO entry point. See Realtime events.

Why separate modules? Attempts and roadmaps import AiModule to store conversations. The tools import attempts and roadmaps. If the tools lived in AiModule there would be a dependency cycle. So the arrows go one way: ai/assistant → ai/tools → domain modules → ai.

flowchart LR
    EV["EventsModule - socket gateway"] --> AS["AiAssistantModule"]
    AS --> TOOLS["AiToolsModule"]
    AS --> AI["AiModule"]
    TOOLS --> DOM["Users, Assessments, Attempts, LearningRoadmaps modules"]
    TOOLS --> AI
    DOM --> AI

docs.title: 3.1 Storage
docs.text:
ai_conversations (src/common/entities/ai-conversation.entity.ts):

Column Notes id Internal key. uid Public id, conv_ + 32 hex chars. This is what clients and tools use. user_id Owner. Cascade-deletes with the user. context_type assessment_attempt or roadmap. context_id Row id of the attempt (assessment_attempts.id) or roadmap. created_at, updated_at updated_at is touched on every new message, so it means "last activity".

Unique on (context_type, context_id): one conversation per attempt (or roadmap).

ai_conversation_messages: id, uid, conversation_id (cascade delete), message (text), role (user / bot), created_at. Indexed on (conversation_id, created_at).

Only the user's text and the assistant's final reply are stored. Tool calls and tool results are not stored.

docs.title: 3.2 Opening a conversation
docs.text:
Step Where POST /v1/attempts/:attemptUid/conversations (rate limit CLASS_B) AttemptsController.createConversation Check the attempt belongs to the user, and its status has a result (evaluated). Otherwise a rule error. AttemptsService.getOrCreateConversation Find or create the conversation for this attempt. Two concurrent opens are safe: the loser of the unique-index race adopts the winner's row. AiConversationsService.getOrCreate Returns { conversationId: "conv_..." }

Why only after evaluation? While an attempt is live, the API hides the correct answers. A bot with attempt context would be a way around that.

The roadmap context type exists in the enum, the resolver and the prompt, but today no endpoint creates a roadmap conversation.

docs.title: 3.3 Reading messages over HTTP
docs.text:
GET /v1/conversations/:conversationId/messages (AiConversationsController, rate limit CLASS_B, JWT required).

  • Query: limit (default 20), cursor.
  • Returns messages newest first. The first page is the bottom of the chat. Pass meta.nextCursor back as cursor to load older messages. nextCursor: null means you reached the start.
  • The cursor is the internal message id.
  • 403 if the conversation belongs to someone else, 404 if it does not exist.

There is no HTTP endpoint for sending a message. Sending happens over the socket.

docs.title: 4.1 Transport: Socket.IO, request/reply, no streaming
docs.text:
The client sends a Socket.IO event ai.conversation.message with:

Field Rules requestId Required. Letters, digits, -, _. Max 64. conversationId Required. Max 64. content Required. Max 4000 characters.

The socket must have connected with a valid JWT (checked in handleConnection). WsJwtGuard checks the socket has a user. wsValidationPipe validates the DTO.

The server answers on the same socket with event ai.conversation.message and { requestId, userId, conversationId, content, sentAt }. Errors come back as an exception event (via WsExceptionFilter) that includes the requestId. The socket stays open.

The reply is sent once, when complete. Tokens are not streamed.

docs.title: 4.2 Sequence
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Client
    participant GW as EventsGateway
    participant R as ConversationRouterService
    participant A as ConversationAssistantService
    participant CS as AiConversationsService
    participant M as LLM default model
    participant T as AiToolsService
    participant D as AttemptsService

    C->>GW: ai.conversation.message with requestId, conversationId, content
    GW->>R: resolveAiConversationMessage with userId from socket
    R->>A: answer
    A->>CS: findOwnedByUid, 403 or 404 if not owned by the user
    A->>A: registry.getDefault, 503 if none
    A->>CS: getRecentMessages, last 20
    A->>A: resolve context to attemptUid
    A->>CS: appendMessage role user
    A->>M: system prompt, context prompt, history, new message, tool definitions
    M-->>A: tool call get_attempt with attemptUid
    A->>T: execute get_attempt with userId from socket
    T->>T: parse and validate args with DTO
    T->>D: getAttemptForAssistant with attemptUid and userId
    D-->>T: attempt detail
    T-->>A: ok true with data
    A->>M: same messages plus tool result
    M-->>A: plain text answer
    A->>CS: appendMessage role bot
    A-->>R: content, sentAt, toolsUsed
    R-->>GW: reply
    GW-->>C: ai.conversation.message with requestId and content

docs.title: 4.3 Step by step
docs.text:
1. Ownership. findOwnedByUid(conversationId, userId). Wrong owner → 403, unknown → 404.
  2. Model. Always the default model (AiModelRegistry.getDefault()), not the user's plan model. No default → 503, before anything is stored.
  3. History and context. Load the last 20 stored messages. Resolve the context: for an attempt, the stored context_id (a row id) is turned into the attempt uid that get_attempt accepts.
  4. Save the user message first. If the provider fails later, what the user said is not lost.
  5. Build messages:
    • System message 1: CONVERSATION_ASSISTANT_SYSTEM_PROMPT (static, so providers can cache it).
    • System message 2: buildConversationContextPrompt() — current date/time, what the conversation is attached to, and a hint like get_attempt({"attemptUid": "..."}).
    • The 20 history messages (user → human, bot → AI).
    • The new user message.
  6. Run the tool loop (next section).
  7. Save the reply as a bot message and return it.

docs.title: 4.4 The tool loop graph
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    S(["START"]) --> AG["agent: call the model"]
    AG -->|"reply has tool calls"| TL["tools: run each call in order"]
    TL --> AG
    AG -->|"no tool calls"| E(["END"])

State: messages (LangGraph MessagesAnnotation, appended to), round (model calls so far), toolsUsed (tool names, for logs).

  • agent binds the tool definitions to the model with bindTools and calls it. Each call is audited in llm_audit with jobType = ASSISTANT_REPLY, jobId = null, and the user id.
  • tools runs every tool call from the last model message, one after another, and appends a ToolMessage for each.
  • Round limit. Tools are offered for rounds 1–4 (MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS = 4). On the 5th call the model is called without tools, so it must answer. Worst case: 5 provider calls per user message.
  • If the final message has no text → 503 The assistant is temporarily unavailable.
  • If the model does not support tool calling (bindTools missing) → 503.
  • Any provider error → 503. The user message stays stored, the bot message is not written.

docs.title: 5. Tools
docs.text:
All tools only read. None of them write, so a hallucinated tool call cannot change data.

Defined in src/ai/tools/*.tools.ts. Names are in AssistantToolName (src/common/enums/ai.enums.ts). The names are part of the contract with the provider; renaming one breaks old transcripts.

Tool What it returns Inputs Service method Access check get_user_profile The caller's name, username, email, verified flag, join date none UsersService.getProfileForAssistant(userId) Always the caller. No way to pass another user. list_assessments Caller's assessments (title, schedule, duration, question count), newest first role: enrolled (default) or created; limit 1–25 (default 10) AssessmentsService.listAssessmentsForAssistant Query is filtered by createdBy = userId or an active participant row for userId. get_assessment One assessment: title, schedule, status, generation status, sections (type, count, marks, difficulty), createdByMe, participant status. Never questions or answers. assessmentId (int ≥ 1) AssessmentsService.getAssessmentForAssistant No ownership check — see the warning below. list_attempts Caller's attempts, newest first, with score and right/wrong counts status (optional AttemptStatus); limit 1–25 AttemptsService.listAttemptsForAssistant Uses findMyAttempts(userId). get_attempt One attempt. After evaluation: per-section results and every question with the user's answer, correct option and explanation (MCQ), or problem and saved code (coding). Before evaluation: answersAvailable: false, questions: null. attemptUid (UUID v4) AttemptsService.getAttemptForAssistant resolveAttempt(attemptUid, userId) — must be the caller's attempt. list_roadmaps Caller's roadmaps with step counts and progress status (optional RoadmapStatus); limit 1–25 LearningRoadmapsService.listRoadmapsForAssistant Listed for userId only. get_roadmap One roadmap with its ordered steps and the current step roadmapId (int ≥ 1) LearningRoadmapsService.getRoadmapForAssistant findOwnedOr404(roadmapId, userId). get_roadmap_node One step in full: description, resources, estimated time, previous and next steps roadmapId, nodeId LearningRoadmapsService.getRoadmapNodeForAssistant Goes through the owned roadmap. get_conversation Another conversation: its context (with usable id), dates, message count, last 20 messages conversationId (conv_ + 32 hex) AiConversationsService.getConversationForAssistant + context resolver findOwnedByUid(..., userId). get_conversation_messages A conversation's transcript, oldest first, up to 100 most recent, with hasMore conversationId; limit 1–100 (default 100) AiConversationsService.getConversationMessagesForAssistant findOwnedByUid(..., userId).

docs.title: 5.1 How a tool call is executed
docs.text:
AiToolsService.execute(name, rawArguments, context) never throws. Every failure becomes { ok: false, tool, error } so the model can read it and correct itself on the next round.

  1. Unknown tool name → error listing the available tools.
  2. Arguments are not a JSON object → error.
  3. Arguments are converted with plainToInstance and checked with class-validator (whitelist: true). Extra keys are dropped, not rejected. "limit": "5" is converted to a number.
  4. Validation errors → Invalid arguments: ....
  5. The handler runs with context.userId.
  6. An HttpException from the service (404, 403, 400) is passed through with its message, e.g. "This conversation does not belong to you".
  7. Any other error is logged with its stack and the model gets a generic "That lookup failed" message. No internal detail reaches the transcript.

The result goes back to the model as JSON in a ToolMessage.

docs.title: 5.2 Limits that keep prompts small
docs.text:
Limit Value Where History replayed each turn 20 messages REPLAYED_HISTORY_MESSAGES Tool rounds per turn 4 (+1 answer-only call) MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS List tool rows default 10, max 25 src/ai/tools/ai-tools.constants.ts Transcript tool max 100 messages, no paging MAX_CONVERSATION_TRANSCRIPT_MESSAGES in src/ai/ai.constants.ts Conversation preview 20 messages CONVERSATION_PREVIEW_MESSAGES User message length 4000 characters ConversationMessageDto

Because tool results are not stored, a follow-up question in a later turn makes the model call the tool again. The prompt tells it to do so rather than "recall" numbers.

docs.title: 6. Safety and authorization
docs.text:
The user id never comes from the model. AssistantToolContext.userId is taken from the authenticated socket. No tool has a userId argument. Each domain method receives that id and filters or checks ownership with it.

Answers are protected in three layers:

  1. A conversation can only be opened for an evaluated attempt.
  2. get_attempt returns answersAvailable: false and no questions for any attempt that is not yet evaluated (the user may ask about another, live attempt).
  3. The system prompt forbids working out or hinting at answers for a test the user is still taking, and forbids calling ungraded answers right or wrong. It still allows teaching the topic.

Grounding. The prompt says every claim about the user's data must come from a tool result, never invent ids, and say plainly when a tool returns nothing or an error.

Only reads. No tool writes anything.

get_assessment has no access check

AssessmentsService.getAssessmentForAssistant (src/assessments/assessments.service.ts, around line 820) loads the assessment with findOne(assessmentId) and does not check that the caller created it or is registered for it. A user who guesses a numeric id can get the metadata of any assessment: title, schedule, status, section layout, marks and participant counts. It never returns questions or answers. Every other tool is scoped to the caller.

docs.title: 6.1 Rate limits and usage limits
docs.text:
• No commerce usage limit applies to the assistant. answer() does not call UsageService. Chat does not count against any plan quota, and it always runs on the default model.
  • No rate limit on the socket message. The ai.conversation.message handler has no @RateLimit. Cost per message is limited only by the 4000-character cap and the 5-call round limit.
  • The HTTP endpoints (POST .../conversations, GET .../messages) use rate-limit policy CLASS_B.
  • Every assistant model call is recorded in llm_audit with jobType = ASSISTANT_REPLY, so admins can see chat cost per user through GET /v1/admin/llm-audits?jobType=ASSISTANT_REPLY (see AI layer).

docs.title: 7. Adding a new tool
docs.text:
1. Add the name to AssistantToolName in src/common/enums/ai.enums.ts (snake_case).
  2. Add an args DTO in src/ai/tools/dto/ with class-validator rules. Use @Type(() => Number) for numbers, because models often send numbers as strings.
  3. Add a read-only method on the domain service that takes userId and checks ownership itself. Keep the result small.
  4. Add the tool object (name, description written for the model, JSON Schema parameters with additionalProperties: false, argsType, handler) to the matching *.tools.ts file, or a new file registered in the AiToolsService constructor.
  5. If the tool needs a new domain module, import it in AiToolsModule, not in AiModule.
  6. If the model should know when to use it, update CONVERSATION_ASSISTANT_SYSTEM_PROMPT.
  7. Add unit tests under tests/unit/ai/.

docs.title: AI Layer — LLM, Structured Output and LangGraph
docs.text:
AI is implemented

Older pages said AI was "not implemented". That is wrong. All of src/ai/ is live code: model selection, three LLM providers, two LangGraph question-generation pipelines, roadmap prompts, descriptive grading, a chat assistant and a per-call cost audit.

This page covers the internals of src/ai. Other pages cover the features that call into it:

Feature Page Assessment generation (API → RabbitMQ → consumer → this layer) Assessment generation Learning roadmaps (analysis, generation, modification jobs) Learning roadmaps Descriptive answer grading Evaluation The chat assistant and its tools AI assistant Code runners used to check coding problems Code execution

docs.title: 1. Words you will see
docs.text: Term Meaning LLM Large Language Model. A hosted model (GPT, Claude, Gemini) that takes text and returns text. Provider The company that hosts the model: openai, anthropic or google (AiModelProvider in src/common/enums/ai.enums.ts). Model code The exact model name sent to the provider API, e.g. gpt-4o. Stored in ai_models.code. LangChain The library we use to talk to every provider through one interface (BaseChatModel). LangGraph A LangChain library for writing a pipeline as a graph: nodes are steps (functions), edges say which step runs next, and conditional edges pick the next step from the current state. All nodes read and update one shared state object. Structured output Asking the model to answer with JSON that matches a schema, instead of free prose. Zod schema A TypeScript schema (library zod) that both describes the JSON shape and validates it. Repair turn When the model's JSON is invalid, we send it its own answer back plus the exact error, and ask for a fixed version. Tool call The model asks us to run a named function with JSON arguments. We run it and send the result back. Tokens The unit providers bill by. Input tokens = prompt, output tokens = answer.

docs.title: 3.1 Models live in the database, not in code
docs.text:
Models are rows in the ai_models table (entity src/common/entities/ai-model.entity.ts). Admins manage them through the admin API (section 9). Each row holds:

Column Purpose provider openai, anthropic or google. code Model name sent to the API. Unique among non-deleted rows. display_name Human name. api_key_variable Name of the env var that holds the API key, e.g. OPENAI_API_KEY. The key itself is never stored in the DB. base_url_variable Optional name of an env var holding a custom base URL (for proxies or OpenAI-compatible hosts). null = provider default host. input_price_per_1m, output_price_per_1m USD per 1 million tokens. Used for cost tracking. capabilities (JSONB) vision, toolCalling, structuredOutput, streaming, contextWindow, maxOutputTokens. Only structuredOutput: false changes runtime behavior today (section 4). is_active Inactive rows are ignored. is_default Exactly one default. A partial unique index (UQ_ai_models_is_default) enforces it.

The seeder src/seeders/ai-model.seeder.ts creates the first default row: an OpenAI model named by OPENAI_MODEL (fallback gpt-4), with apiKeyVariable = OPENAI_API_KEY and baseUrlVariable = OPENAI_BASE_URL, prices 0.

docs.title: 3.2 The registry
docs.text:
AiModelRegistry loads all active rows at startup (onModuleInit) and after every admin write.

For each row it reads the named env vars:

  • API key env var missing or empty → the model is skipped (logged as a warning).
  • base_url_variable set but the env var is empty → the model is skipped. It does not fall back to the default host, because a key for a proxy probably will not work on the real host.

The result is a map of RegisteredAiModel objects. Each holds the row data plus a chatModel(options) function that returns a cached LangChain client (one client per distinct option set, e.g. one for temperature: 0, one for default).

The registry is per process

Each app instance keeps its own copy. An admin change reloads only the instance that served the request. Other instances see it after restart.

docs.title: 3.3 The selector: which model does a user get?
docs.text:
AiModelSelector.forUser(userId):

  1. Reads the user's plan feature AI_MODEL through UsageService.getFeatureValue (see Commerce). Its value is a model code.
  2. Blank or missing → use the default model.
  3. A code that is unknown, inactive or unavailable → log a warning and use the default model.
  4. No default available → 503 Service Unavailable.

So the plan decides the model. There are no feature flags involved in model choice.

Caller Model used MCQ / coding / descriptive generation (QuestionsService) The requesting user's plan model Roadmap analysis, generation, modification consumers The roadmap owner's plan model Descriptive grading (DescriptiveEvaluator) The assessment creator's plan model (not the candidate's) Chat assistant Always the default model, whatever the plan

docs.title: 3.4 The chat model factory
docs.text:
createChatModel(provider, code, credentials, options) in src/ai/llm/chat-model.factory.ts:

Provider LangChain class Base URL option openai ChatOpenAI (@langchain/openai) configuration.baseURL anthropic ChatAnthropic (@langchain/anthropic) anthropicApiUrl google ChatGoogleGenerativeAI (@langchain/google-genai) baseUrl

Settings:

  • Native integrations. Each provider uses its own LangChain class, not an OpenAI-compatible shim. This means structured output and tool calling use the provider's real mechanism.
  • Transport retries: maxRetries: 2 for network/HTTP errors (handled inside the SDK).
  • Temperature: only set when a caller pins it. Grading, reviews and roadmap prompts use 0 (same input → same answer). Writing steps use the provider default.
  • Max tokens / timeouts: not set. The provider default applies. There is no explicit request timeout in our code.

docs.title: 4. Structured output — getting reliable JSON
docs.text: Almost every LLM call in TestFlow must return one JSON object. All of them go through StructuredOutputService.run() (src/ai/llm/structured-output.service.ts). It is itself a tiny LangGraph loop.

docs.title: 4.1 The request
docs.text: Field Meaning model, context Which model, and what the audit row is filed under (jobId, jobType, userId). systemPrompt, userMessage The prompts. parse(value) Turns the JSON into the result, or throws an Error whose message is written for the model. That message is sent back as the repair instruction. structured Optional { schema, name }. If present, the provider's native structured output is used. maxAttempts Total calls allowed, including repairs. Every caller uses 2 (one try + one repair). temperature Optional.

docs.title: 4.2 The loop
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    S(["START"]) --> G["generate: one provider call"]
    G --> V["validate: extract JSON and run parse"]
    V -->|"valid"| E(["END: return result"])
    V -->|"invalid and budget used up"| F(["END: throw 503"])
    V -->|"invalid and budget left"| R["repair: add rejected reply and reason to messages"]
    R --> G

State fields: messages (the chat so far, appended to), attempt, completion (last reply), lastReason, result, native (use native structured output on the next call?), bonusAttempts.

Step by step:

  1. Build the prompt. If a schema is given, STRUCTURED_JSON_CONTRACT is appended to the system prompt and STRUCTURED_JSON_REMINDER to the user message. If native output is off, the JSON Schema itself (from zod.toJSONSchema) is also put into the user message so the model knows the exact keys.
  2. generate. If native output is on, call chatModel.withStructuredOutput(schema, { includeRaw: true }). Otherwise call the model as plain chat. Every call is wrapped in LlmAuditService.track() (one audit row per call).
  3. validate. Use the provider-decoded object if there is one, else run extractJsonObject(text). Then run parse. On error, store the message as lastReason.
  4. repair. Append the rejected reply (max 8000 chars) and buildJsonRepairPrompt(reason) ("Your previous response was REJECTED for this reason: …"). Go back to generate.
  5. End. Success returns the value. Out of budget throws ServiceUnavailableException("<label> returned an invalid response").

Why a repair turn instead of a plain retry? A plain retry samples the same mistake again. Telling the model exactly what was wrong ("outline had 4 items — it must have exactly 5") fixes it much more often.

docs.title: 4.3 Native output fallbacks
docs.text:
Some OpenAI-compatible endpoints accept a schema and then send replies the SDK cannot decode (code fences, a stray {" prefix). The service handles this:

What happened Treated as Effect SDK could not decode the reply (SyntaxError, OutputParserException) Model output problem Switch to plain JSON for the rest of this call. This call does not use up an attempt (bonusAttempts + 1). Same model fails to decode natively 3 times (NATIVE_DECODE_FAILURE_LIMIT) Model does not honour schemas Native output is disabled for that model until restart. Set capabilities.structuredOutput = false to make it permanent. SDK decoded but its own Zod check failed Content problem Normal repair turn, costs an attempt, native stays on. Reply cut off at token limit / content filter Not counted against the model Repair turn with a message like "be more concise". Network or HTTP error Real outage 503 "<label> is temporarily unavailable". No repair. Empty reply Outage 503.

docs.title: 4.4 JSON extraction
docs.text:
extractJsonObject() (src/ai/llm/json-extraction.util.ts) is used when we parse text ourselves:

  • Strips one outer code fence (```json).
  • Tries every { (up to 8) as a possible start, and takes the first balanced object that parses. This handles gateways that prefix {" before the real object.
  • Removes trailing commas before } or ].
  • Does not guess at ambiguous damage (single quotes, unquoted keys). Those fail and go to the repair turn.

docs.title: 4.5 Schemas
docs.text:
All in src/ai/schemas/. zodParser(schema) (zod-parser.ts) turns a Zod schema into a parse function. Its errors are formatted as "path": message; … so they read well to the model.

Schema Used for Key rules QUESTION_PLAN_SCHEMA MCQ and coding plan assessmentTitle; outline[] of { focus, difficulty: easy/medium/hard, topics: 1–4 kebab-case slugs } QUESTION_BATCH_SCHEMA One batch of MCQs Each question: text, exactly 4 options with ids 1–4, correctOptionId that matches an option, 1–4 weighted topics QUESTION_REVIEW_SCHEMA MCQ review Per question: number, reasoning, answerOptionId, verdict: ok/ambiguous/incorrect, issue QUESTION_GENERATION_SCHEMA Final MCQ result check Title + at least one question CODING_PROBLEM_SCHEMA One coding problem Title, statement, input/output format, constraints, starter code for python, java, cpp, 7–15 test cases (≥2 visible, ≥5 hidden, all inputs unique), Python referenceSolution, topics CODING_REVIEW_SCHEMA Coding review verdict, issue, outputs[] (the reviewer's traced output per test input) DESCRIPTIVE_GENERATION_SCHEMA Descriptive questions Text, 2–6 checkpoints with integer weightage 1–100, maxWords 30–1000, topics DESCRIPTIVE_GRADING_SCHEMA Descriptive grading completedCheckpointIds: number[]

Each caller adds extra checks in its parse function. Examples: "outline must have exactly N items", "reviews must cover questions 1..N once each", "checkpoint id 7 does not exist".

Non-blank strings use a Zod .refine() instead of .trim(), because a transform cannot be expressed in the JSON Schema sent to the provider.

Roadmap prompts are different. They use no Zod schema and no native structured output. The JSON contract lives inside the prompt text (JSON_ONLY_CONTRACT), and RoadmapAiService validates the result with hand-written checks (parseAnalyzedIntent, parseGeneratedRoadmap, parseGeneratedDiff) whose error messages feed the repair turn. The reason given in the code: some gateways implement JSON mode by pre-filling the reply, which corrupts it.

docs.title: 5. Prompts
docs.text:
All in src/ai/prompts/, re-exported from index.ts.

Prompt What it asks for QUESTION_PLAN_SYSTEM_PROMPT Act as an examiner. Produce exactly N distinct outline items (focus, difficulty, topic slugs) plus an assessment title. Spread coverage, stay in scope. QUESTION_GENERATION_SYSTEM_PROMPT Write one MCQ per outline item. Test understanding, not recall. Plausible distractors, Markdown-safe formatting. QUESTION_REVIEW_SYSTEM_PROMPT Act as an independent examiner. Solve each question without the answer key, pick an option, give a verdict and a one-line issue. CODING_PLAN_SYSTEM_PROMPT Plan exactly N coding problems (algorithmic idea, difficulty, topics) plus a title. CODING_GENERATION_SYSTEM_PROMPT Write one full coding problem: statement, formats, constraints, starter code, test cases, Python reference solution. CODING_TOOLS_SYSTEM_PROMPT Extra rules when writing with tools: run the reference solution with run_code and copy its output into expectedOutput, then call submit_problem. CODING_REVIEW_SYSTEM_PROMPT Judge the statement and trace the reference solution on each test input, without seeing the expected outputs. DESCRIPTIVE_GENERATION_SYSTEM_PROMPT Write N free-text questions, each with 2–6 concrete, non-overlapping checkpoints and weightages summing to 100. DESCRIPTIVE_GRADING_SYSTEM_PROMPT Read the answer and return only the ids of the checkpoints it completes. Marks are computed in code. ROADMAP_ANALYSIS_SYSTEM_PROMPT Name the learning goal and ask the fewest questions (3–6) that would change the roadmap. ROADMAP_GENERATION_SYSTEM_PROMPT Build a personalised DAG of knowledge and practice nodes, using ref numbers and fromRef/toRef edges. ASSESSMENT_SUGGESTION_SYSTEM_PROMPT Act as a tutor. From one attempt's result (overall, per section, per topic), design one follow-up assessment: weak areas first, difficulty by accuracy (<40% easier, 40–75% same, >75% harder), only the allowed question types, within the generation limits. ROADMAP_MODIFICATION_SYSTEM_PROMPT Change an existing roadmap from a plain-language instruction. Return a diff (added, updated, removed, edges) so surviving nodes keep their ids and progress. CONVERSATION_ASSISTANT_SYSTEM_PROMPT The chat assistant's rules: ground every fact in a tool result, never reveal answers before evaluation, keep replies short. See AI assistant. buildConversationContextPrompt() Second system message for chat: current date and what the conversation is attached to. JSON_ONLY_CONTRACT Strict "one raw JSON object, nothing else" rules, embedded in the three roadmap prompts. STRUCTURED_JSON_CONTRACT / STRUCTURED_JSON_REMINDER Lighter JSON rules appended to every schema call. Allows Markdown inside string values. buildJsonRepairPrompt(reason) The repair turn text. difficultyGuidance(level) Turns a section difficulty 1–5 into an easy/medium/hard mix (e.g. 3 → 30/50/20).

docs.title: 6. LangGraph pipelines
docs.text:
There are four LangGraph graphs in src/ai:

Graph File Used by Structured output loop llm/structured-output.service.ts Every JSON call (section 4) MCQ generation llm/question-generation.graph.ts AiService.generateQuestions Coding generation llm/coding-question-generation.graph.ts AiService.generateCodingQuestions Assistant tool loop assistant/conversation-assistant.service.ts Chat. See AI assistant.

Descriptive generation and grading, and all three roadmap prompts, are single structured-output calls (no multi-step graph).

Each graph is built and compiled inside run() on every call. State lives only in memory for that one run. Nothing is checkpointed, so a crashed process loses the run and the job must be retried by its consumer.

docs.title: 6.1 MCQ generation graph
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    S(["START"]) --> P["plan"]
    P --> G["generate"]
    G --> RV["review"]
    RV -->|"flags and revisionRounds less than 1"| RS["revise"]
    RS --> RV
    RV -->|"no flags or budget used"| E(["END"])
    E --> B["balanceAnswerPositions and final schema check"]

State

Field Meaning assessmentTitle From the plan. outline N items: focus, difficulty, topics. questions Written questions, same order as the outline. toReview Indexes the next review pass checks. All at first, then only revised ones. flagged { index, feedback } for questions the reviewer disputes. revisionRounds How many revise passes ran.

Nodes

  1. plan — One call. Produces exactly count outline items and the title. Difficulty mix comes from difficultyGuidance(section difficulty).
  2. generate — Splits the outline into batches of 5 and writes them with at most 3 calls in parallel.
  3. review — Batches of 5, 3 in parallel, temperature 0. The reviewer gets questions and options but not the answer key. A question is flagged if the verdict is not ok or the reviewer picks a different option than the key. If a review call fails, that batch is skipped with a warning (questions ship unreviewed).
  4. revise — Rewrites each flagged question with the reviewer's feedback (3 in parallel). A failed rewrite keeps the original.
  5. End — Max 1 revision round. Questions still flagged are kept (logged as a warning), because a short assessment is worse for the creator.
  6. After the graph — balanceAnswerPositions moves correct answers so each group of four questions uses positions 1–4 once (models favour the same slot). Then the whole result is checked against QUESTION_GENERATION_SCHEMA.

Why plan first? Writers in parallel batches cannot see each other. A shared outline stops duplicate questions and fixes the difficulty mix up front.

docs.title: 6.2 Coding generation graph
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    S(["START"]) --> P["plan"]
    P --> G["generate"]
    G --> VF["verify"]
    VF --> RV["review"]
    RV -->|"flags and revisionRounds less than 2"| RS["revise"]
    RS --> VF
    RV -->|"no flags or budget used"| E(["END"])

State — like MCQ (assessmentTitle, outline, problems, toReview, flagged, revisionRounds) plus:

Field Meaning executed Problems whose expected outputs came from actually running the reference solution. executionUnavailable true when there is no code runner, or it failed. Review then checks outputs by tracing instead.

Nodes

  1. plan — Same as MCQ, with the coding plan prompt.
  2. generate — One call per problem, 3 in parallel. Each problem is written by writeWithTools (section 6.3). If tool writing is not possible or fails, it falls back to one structured-output call.
  3. verify — For every problem awaiting review, run the Python reference solution on each test input with the code runner (CODE_RUNNER, see Code execution). Default limits: 2000 ms, 256 MB. What it prints becomes the expected output. A crash, timeout or over-long output flags the problem with the stderr as feedback. The first runner error (not configured, busy, down) turns execution off for the rest of the run.
  4. review — One call per problem, temperature 0. The reviewer sees the statement, solution and inputs, but not the expected outputs. If the verdict is not ok, the problem is flagged. If outputs were not executed, the reviewer's traced outputs are compared with the expected ones and any mismatch flags it. A failed review call flags the problem.
  5. revise — Rewrites flagged problems. Rewritten problems lose their executed mark until verify runs them again.
  6. End — Max 2 revision rounds. Unlike MCQ, any problem still flagged fails the whole run with a 503. A wrong expected output would fail every correct submission, which is worse than a missing problem.

docs.title: 6.3 Writing a coding problem with tools
docs.text:
CodingProblemToolWriter (src/ai/llm/coding-problem-tool-writer.ts) is a plain loop, not a LangGraph graph. It is used when a code runner supports Python and the chat model has bindTools.

sequenceDiagram
    participant W as CodingProblemToolWriter
    participant M as LLM
    participant R as Code runner
    W->>M: system and user prompt, tools run_code and submit_problem, tool_choice any
    M-->>W: tool call run_code with code and stdin
    W->>R: run Python with limits
    R-->>W: stdout, stderr, status, time
    W->>M: tool result as JSON
    M-->>W: tool call submit_problem with the full problem
    W->>W: validate with CODING_PROBLEM_SCHEMA
    alt valid
        W-->>W: return problem
    else invalid
        W->>M: Rejected with reason, submit again
    end

Limits: max 8 model turns (the last turn offers only submit_problem), max 40 run_code runs per problem, outputs echoed back are cut to 2000 chars (stderr 1000). Every turn is a tool call (tool_choice: 'any'). Any failure raises ToolWriterError, and the graph falls back to plain structured output.

docs.title: 6.4 Parallelism and batching summary
docs.text:
Setting MCQ Coding Items per call 5 questions 1 problem Calls in flight per step (MAX_PARALLEL_CALLS) 3 3 Attempts per call (incl. repair) 2 2 Revision rounds 1 2 Still flagged at the end Kept, warning logged Run fails (503)

mapWithConcurrency keeps output order equal to input order. The cap of 3 is how we stay under provider rate limits. There is no other client-side rate limiter for LLM calls.

docs.title: 7. Callers
docs.text:
Caller Method Pipeline Audit jobType QuestionsService.generateFromPrompt (sync endpoint or job) AiService.generateQuestions MCQ graph job type, or INLINE_QUESTION_GENERATION QuestionsService.generateMcqSection (section job) AiService.generateQuestions MCQ graph section job type QuestionsService.generateCodingSection AiService.generateCodingQuestions Coding graph section job type QuestionsService.generateDescriptiveSection AiService.generateDescriptiveQuestions 1 structured call section job type DescriptiveEvaluator.evaluate AiService.findCompletedCheckpoints 1 structured call, temp 0 EVALUATE_DESCRIPTIVE_RESPONSES RoadmapAnalysisConsumer RoadmapAiService.analyzeRoadmapIntent 1 structured call, temp 0 roadmap job type RoadmapGenerationConsumer RoadmapAiService.generateRoadmap 1 structured call, temp 0 roadmap job type RoadmapModificationConsumer RoadmapAiService.modifyRoadmapGraph 1 structured call, temp 0 roadmap job type ConversationAssistantService.answer (own loop) Assistant graph ASSISTANT_REPLY AttemptSuggestionService.suggestNext (inline, on POST /v1/attempts/:uid/next-assessment) AssessmentSuggestionAiService.suggestNextAssessment 1 structured call (Zod schema assessment_suggestion), up to 3 attempts, always the default model ASSESSMENT_SUGGESTION

In the testing environment (NODE_ENV=testing) QuestionsService skips the LLM entirely and returns banked or fixed questions.

For the full request → queue → consumer flow see Assessment generation and Learning roadmaps.

docs.title: 8. Token and cost tracking
docs.text:
LlmAuditService.track(model, context, attempt, call) wraps every provider call: structured output attempts, tool-writer turns and assistant turns. It writes one row to llm_audit (src/common/entities/llm-audit.entity.ts):

  • job_id, job_type, user_id — from the LlmCallContext.
  • ai_model_id, provider, model, model_code.
  • status (SUCCESS / FAILED), attempt, error_message (max 2000 chars).
  • started_at, completed_at, duration_ms.
  • input_tokens, output_tokens, cached_input_tokens, total_tokens — read from LangChain's usage_metadata.
  • Prices at call time and input_cost, output_cost, total_cost = tokens × price / 1,000,000.

Notes:

  • Cached input tokens are billed at the full input price (no cached rate is stored).
  • A failure to write the audit row is logged and never fails the LLM call.
  • A repair turn is a separate, separately billed row.

docs.title: 9. Admin endpoints
docs.text:
Controller: src/ai/admin.controller.ts, base path /v1/admin. Protected by the global JwtAuthGuard and PermissionGuard (see RBAC). Rate-limit policy CLASS_C.

Method & path Permission What it does POST /v1/admin/ai-models ai_models:create Register a model. isDefault: true unsets the old default in the same transaction. GET /v1/admin/ai-models ai_models:read Paged list. Filters provider, isActive. Default model first. GET /v1/admin/ai-models/:id ai_models:read One model.
