PATCH /v1/admin/ai-models/:id ai_models:update Partial update. capabilities replaces the whole object. DELETE /v1/admin/ai-models/:id ai_models:delete Soft delete. The default model cannot be deleted (422). GET /v1/admin/llm-audits llm_audits:read Audit rows grouped by job, newest first, with totals under usage and the calls under calls. Filters: jobId, jobType, userId, modelCode, provider, status, startedFrom, startedTo. Paging counts jobs. A call with no job is its own group.

Rules enforced by AiAdminService:

  • The default model must be active (422 otherwise).
  • Duplicate code → 409. Two requests racing to set a default → 409 "please retry".
  • After every committed write the registry is reloaded (on this instance only).

docs.title: 10. Error handling summary
docs.text:
Situation What happens No default model available 503 No default AI model is available Plan names an unavailable model Warning, falls back to the default Network / HTTP error from provider SDK retries 2 times, then 503 "<label> is temporarily unavailable" Invalid JSON or schema mismatch Repair turn, then 503 "<label> returned an invalid response" MCQ review call fails Batch ships unreviewed, warning Coding review call fails Problem flagged; may fail the run Code runner down Verify turns off; review traces outputs instead Coding problem still disputed Run fails with 503

Inside jobs, these exceptions propagate to the RabbitMQ consumer, which marks the job failed or retries it. See Jobs and schedulers.

docs.title: 11. How to add a new provider
docs.text:
1. Add the value to AiModelProvider in src/common/enums/ai.enums.ts. The column is a Postgres enum, so write a migration that adds the value to the enum type.
  2. Ask the team before adding the LangChain package (e.g. @langchain/mistralai) — new npm packages need approval.
  3. Add a case to createChatModel in src/ai/llm/chat-model.factory.ts. Pass model, apiKey, temperature, maxRetries: MAX_TRANSPORT_RETRIES and the base URL option.
  4. Make sure the DTO enum check in CreateAiModelDto accepts it (it uses AiModelProvider, so step 1 covers it).
  5. Set the API key env var on every instance.
  6. Register a model through POST /v1/admin/ai-models with its prices and capabilities. If the provider does not honour JSON schemas, set structuredOutput: false.
  7. Point a plan's AI_MODEL feature at the new code, or make it the default.

docs.title: 12. How to add a new graph or LLM call
docs.text:
1. Schema. Add a Zod schema in src/ai/schemas/. Keep it expressible as JSON Schema (use .refine(), not transforms).
  2. Prompt. Add a system prompt in src/ai/prompts/ and export it from index.ts. Describe the fields. Do not repeat JSON formatting rules — StructuredOutputService adds them.
  3. Single call? Call StructuredOutputService.run() with structured: { schema, name }, parse: zodParser(schema) plus any extra checks, and maxAttempts: 2. Throw plain Errors with messages written for the model.
  4. Multi-step? Create an @Injectable() class in src/ai/llm/ like QuestionGenerationGraph:
    • Define state with Annotation.Root({...}).
    • Add nodes that return partial state.
    • Use addConditionalEdges for loops, and always cap loops with a counter in state.
    • Use mapWithConcurrency(items, 3, fn) for fan-out.
    • Route every provider call through StructuredOutputService or LlmAuditService.track so it is audited.
  5. Expose it through a method on AiService (or a new service) that takes a RegisteredAiModel and an LlmCallContext. Register the class in AiModule.providers.
  6. Call it from the domain module: resolve the model with AiModelSelector.forUser(userId), and pass the job id and type for auditing. Long-running work should run in a RabbitMQ consumer, not in an HTTP request.
  7. Test it in tests/unit/ai/ with a mocked chat model.

docs.title: 1. Purpose
docs.text:
A user describes a test in plain words ("Intermediate Postgres: indexing, MVCC, query plans") and the backend builds the whole assessment with an LLM.

The work is slow (seconds to minutes) and can fail, so it runs in the background:

  1. The API checks the request, charges the quota, creates the assessment and some job rows, and publishes messages to RabbitMQ. It returns at once.
  2. One worker per section picks a message up, calls the AI layer, and saves the questions.
  3. An aggregator watches the section jobs and finishes the assessment when all of them are done.
  4. The client polls GET /v1/jobs/:jobId to show progress.

This page covers the assessment side. The LLM internals (models, LangGraph graphs, prompts, structured output) are on AI Layer.

docs.title: 2. Key concepts
docs.text: Term Meaning Mode auto: the backend lays out the sections from a total count, the allowed types and a difficulty. manual: the client gives every section (type, count, difficulty, marks, its own prompt). Section One group of same-type questions. Each section is generated by its own job, so sections run in parallel and fail on their own. Parent job One jobs row of type GENERATE_ASSESSMENT. It is never published to a queue. It only tracks its sections. assessments.job_id points to it. Section job One jobs row per section, of type GENERATE_MCQ_SECTION, GENERATE_CODING_SECTION or GENERATE_DESCRIPTIVE_SECTION, with parent_job_id set. Aggregator GenerationAggregatorService. Runs every time a section job settles and decides what that means for the parent and the assessment. Idempotency key Optional Idempotency-Key header. Resending the same request with the same key returns the first result and charges nothing. Quota One unit of the AI_ASSESSMENT plan feature per generation (and per retry). Refunded once if the generation fails.

docs.title: 3. Data it uses
docs.text:
See the ERD:

  • jobs (parent and section rows: type, status, payload, result, error, attempts, max_attempts, parent_job_id, idempotency_key, status_description). There is a partial unique index on (created_by, idempotency_key).
  • assessments, assessment_sections, assessments_participants (creator row).
  • questions + details tables, and assessments_questions (written per section).
  • Commerce usage rows (via UsageService), and llm_audit (via the AI layer).

Parent job payload (ParentGenerationPayload in src/assessments/generation/interfaces/generation-job.interface.ts): assessmentId, userId, orgId, mode, requestHash, and usage { charged, chargedAt, refunded }.

Section job payload (SectionGenerationPayload): parentJobId, assessmentId, sectionId, sectionTitle, questionType, count, difficulty, prompt, userId.

docs.title: 4. The request
docs.text:
POST /v1/assessments/generate, body GenerateAssessmentRequestDto (src/assessments/generation/dto/generate-assessment-request.dto.ts).

Field Mode Rule prompt both Required, 10–5000 chars. Becomes the assessment's description. title both Optional, 3–255. If missing, the AI's suggested title is used, or the description. duration both 1–180 minutes. maxParticipants both Required for org assessments (1–10,000). Ignored for personal ones, which always get 10. registrationStartTime … attemptEndTime both Org: attempt start and end required. Personal: ignored, fixed 30-day window. See Assessments. mode both auto or manual. totalQuestions auto 1–50. questionTypes auto At least one, no repeats. descriptive is not allowed in auto mode. difficulty auto 1–5. sections[] manual 1–3 sections. Each: title? (≤100), prompt (10–5000, checked again after trimming), questionType, questionCount ≥ 1, difficulty 1–5, positiveMark 0.01–999.99, negativeMark 0–999.99.

Limits (GENERATION_LIMITS in generation/generation.constants.ts):

MCQ Coding Descriptive Max per section (manual) 20 5 10 Max per assessment (manual) 60 5 10

docs.title: 4.1 Two-step validation
docs.text:
1. The DTO (class-validator) checks each field on its own.
  2. AssessmentGenerationValidatorService checks rules that need more than one field, collects all errors and returns them in one 400:
    • the fields of the other mode must not be sent (sections is not allowed in auto mode),
    • the fields of this mode are required,
    • auto: total must cover every requested type, coding-only is capped at 5, no descriptive,
    • manual: section count, per-section and per-type limits (sectionLimitErrors, shared with templates),
    • org: maxParticipants and the schedule.

It then returns a typed GenerationRequest (auto or manual), trimmed and in a fixed key order so it can be hashed.

docs.title: 4.2 Planning the sections
docs.text:
planSections() in generation/generation-planner.ts is a pure function:

  • Manual: one planned section per request section, in order. A missing title becomes "Multiple Choice", "Coding" or "Descriptive". Each section is generated from its own prompt.
  • Auto, one type: one section with all the questions.
  • Auto, MCQ + coding: coding gets 10% of the total (at least 1, at most 5), MCQ gets the rest. Order is MCQ then coding. Example: 20 questions → 18 MCQ + 2 coding. Auto sections use the assessment prompt and the default marks (MCQ +1/0, coding +10/0).

docs.title: 5.1 Starting a generation
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant C as Client
    participant API as AssessmentsController
    participant V as GenerationValidator
    participant O as GenerationOrchestrator
    participant U as UsageService
    participant DB as PostgreSQL
    participant MQ as RabbitMQ
    participant W as Section worker
    participant AI as AiService and graphs
    participant AG as GenerationAggregator

    C->>API: POST /v1/assessments/generate with Idempotency-Key
    API->>V: validate(dto, org)
    V-->>API: typed GenerationRequest or 400
    API->>O: start(request, userId, org, key)
    O->>DB: find parent job by user and key
    alt same key seen before
        O-->>C: 200 first response, nothing charged
    end
    O->>O: planSections
    O->>U: assert plan allows these question types
    O->>U: consume 1 AI_ASSESSMENT
    O->>DB: BEGIN
    O->>DB: INSERT assessment draft, sections, creator participant
    O->>DB: INSERT parent job - processing
    O->>DB: INSERT one section job per section - pending
    O->>DB: UPDATE assessments.job_id
    O->>DB: COMMIT
    O->>MQ: publish one message per section to its type queue
    O-->>C: 200 assessmentId, jobId, status draft

    MQ->>W: section message
    W->>DB: claim job - check type, not settled, parent still processing
    W->>DB: mark section processing, attempts plus 1
    W->>AI: generate questions for this section
    AI-->>W: drafts and suggested title
    W->>DB: BEGIN
    W->>DB: save bank questions and snapshots, bump curr_total_questions
    W->>DB: mark section completed with result
    W->>DB: COMMIT
    W->>AG: onSectionSettled(parentJobId)
    AG->>DB: lock parent row, read all sections
    alt some sections still running
        AG->>DB: statusDescription 1 of 2 sections generated
    else all completed
        AG->>DB: assessment ready or published, title set, parent completed
    else all settled, some failed
        AG->>U: release 1 AI_ASSESSMENT once
        AG->>DB: parent failed with failedSections
    end

    loop until parent is completed or failed
        C->>API: GET /v1/jobs/:jobId
        API-->>C: parent status and section jobs
    end

Notes on the diagram:

  • Steps before the transaction (replay check, plan check, quota) can each refuse the request without creating anything.
  • If the transaction fails, the quota unit is released right away. If it failed because a parallel request with the same key won the race (unique violation), the API answers with that request's result.
  • If publishing a section message fails, that section job is marked failed on the spot, the aggregator runs, and the API returns 503 "Assessment created, but question generation could not be started". The assessment exists and can be retried.
  • No WebSocket events and no emails are sent for generation. Progress is only visible by polling the job. See Jobs & Schedulers.

docs.title: 5.2 Calling the AI layer
docs.text:
Each queue has its own consumer in src/assessments/generation/consumers/. They all hand off to the shared SectionGenerationWorker, passing a type-specific generator from QuestionsService:

Queue (routing key) Consumer Generator AI call question-section-mcq-queue (question.section.mcq) McqSectionConsumer generateMcqSection AiService.generateQuestions → QuestionGenerationGraph (plan, generate, review, revise) question-section-coding-queue (question.section.coding) CodingSectionConsumer generateCodingSection AiService.generateCodingQuestions → CodingQuestionGenerationGraph (test cases checked by an independent review) question-section-descriptive-queue (question.section.descriptive) DescriptiveSectionConsumer generateDescriptiveSection AiService.generateDescriptiveQuestions → StructuredOutputService with a Zod schema

All queues are bound to the question.generation topic exchange (src/config/rabbitmq/). One queue per type means slow coding generation never blocks MCQ sections.

Before each call the model is picked by AiModelSelector.forUser(userId), so the user's plan decides the model. Each LLM call is audited against the section job (llm_audit). The graphs, prompts and output validation are described on AI Layer.

docs.title: 5.3 Checking and saving generated questions
docs.text:
The AI layer validates the structure of the output (schemas, exact counts, review steps). On the assessment side:

  1. Only the first count questions are kept (slice(0, count)).
  2. MCQ: options and correct option are taken as given; explanation is null.
  3. Coding: the title is joined into the question text, the reference solution is dropped, fixed limits are applied (2000 ms, 256 MB, exact checker, python/java/cpp).
  4. Descriptive: checkpoints are renumbered from 1 and their weights normalised to sum to 100. assertCheckpointWeights runs again before saving.
  5. SectionQuestionWriter.append refuses drafts whose type does not match the section, then saves bank rows, details rows and snapshots in one transaction together with completing the section job. See Questions & Tags.

docs.title: 5.4 Finishing
docs.text:
When every section job is completed, the aggregator (inside the parent's row lock):

  1. takes the first non-empty suggested title from the section results,
  2. calls AssessmentsService.markGenerated: sets the title if the user gave none, and moves the status with settleByCapacity (full → ready; a personal assessment that is full goes straight to published),
  3. marks the parent completed with { sections, questionsGenerated }.

docs.title: 6. Job status lifecycle
docs.text: The job rules live in src/jobs/domain/. The outcome of a parent from its children is childOutcome() (running / completed / failed), re-exported as generationOutcome in src/assessments/domain/generation-outcome.ts.

docs.title: 6.1 Section job
docs.text:
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> pending : created with the assessment
    pending --> processing : worker claims it
    pending --> failed : message could not be published
    processing --> processing : redelivered after a crash
    processing --> completed : questions saved
    processing --> failed : AI or save error
    failed --> pending : retry, if attempts are left
    completed --> [*]

docs.title: 6.2 Parent job
docs.text:
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> processing : created, sections queued
    processing --> processing : a section settles, others still running
    processing --> completed : every section completed
    processing --> failed : all settled, at least one failed
    failed --> processing : POST generation retry
    completed --> [*]

The assessment status moves alongside: it stays draft while the parent is processing or failed, becomes ready (or published for personal) on completed, and goes back to draft if a ready assessment is retried. See Assessments.

docs.title: 7.1 What happens when a section fails
docs.text:
• The worker catches the error, marks only that section job failed, and still acks the RabbitMQ message. It does not rethrow, so a prompt the LLM can never satisfy does not loop forever.
  • The other sections carry on.
  • When all sections have settled and one or more failed, the aggregator:
    • refunds the quota once (usage.refunded flag on the parent payload; the refund is skipped if the usage period has reset since chargedAt),
    • marks the parent failed with error.failedSections (job id, section id, reason),
    • keeps the questions of the sections that completed.

docs.title: 7.2 Retrying
docs.text:
POST /v1/assessments/:id/generation/retry (GenerationOrchestratorService.retry). Rate limited like generate.

  1. Caller must be able to manage the assessment.
  2. The assessment must have a GENERATE_ASSESSMENT parent job in status failed. Otherwise 409.
  3. The assessment must not be published.
  4. Every failed section must still have attempts left (attempts < max_attempts, max 3). Otherwise 409.
  5. The plan must still allow the failed sections' question types (403).
  6. One AI_ASSESSMENT unit is charged again (the failure refunded the first).
  7. In one transaction, under a row lock on the parent: parent failed → processing with a fresh unrefunded charge, failed sections failed → pending, assessment back to draft. A second concurrent retry gets 409 "already being retried".
  8. Only the failed sections are republished. Completed sections are not re-run.

Generation jobs cannot be retried through the generic POST /v1/jobs/:id/retry; it returns 409 and points to the assessment route.

docs.title: 7.3 Redelivery and duplicates
docs.text:
• A message is acked when the handler returns. If a worker process dies mid-run, RabbitMQ redelivers it. claimJob lets a job that is already processing be picked up again, which is the recovery path.
  • A redelivered message for a job that is already completed or failed is dropped (isClaimable).
  • A message whose parent is no longer processing is dropped, so a section that waited in the queue after its generation failed does not run.
  • Concurrent aggregator calls are serialised by a SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on the parent row, so exactly one call finishes the generation.

docs.title: 7.4 Dead-lettering
docs.text: There is no dead-letter exchange or queue configured (src/config/rabbitmq/rabbitmq.module.ts). Failures are recorded on the job rows instead, and retry is an explicit API call.

docs.title: 8. Idempotency
docs.text:
1. The client may send Idempotency-Key (1–100 chars). Blank or too long is a 400.
  2. The orchestrator hashes the validated request (SHA-256) and stores it as requestHash on the parent job, with the key in jobs.idempotency_key.
  3. A later request from the same user with the same key:
    • same hash → returns the first { assessmentId, jobId, status }; nothing is created or charged,
    • different hash → 422 "Idempotency-Key was already used for a different generation request",
    • assessment since hard-deleted → 409.
  4. Two simultaneous requests with the same key: the unique index (created_by, idempotency_key) lets only one insert win. The loser releases its quota unit and answers with the winner's result.
  5. Without a key, every request creates a new assessment.

docs.title: 9. Business rules and edge cases
docs.text:
1. Plan checks come first. A question type not in the plan's ALLOWED_QUESTION_TYPES is a 403 before any charge. In an org, the org's plan and pooled quota are used, never the member's personal plan.
  2. Quota exhausted → 422, nothing created.
  3. Fewer questions than asked. If a generator returns fewer drafts than count, the section still completes. The assessment then stays draft (not full) while the parent job is completed, and retry is refused because nothing failed. The creator must fill the gap by hand.
  4. Auto mode MCQ-only can make one section of up to 50 questions, above the manual-mode per-section cap of 20.
  5. Personal assessments always get 10 seats and a 30-day window, whatever the request says.
  6. Who can poll. GET /v1/jobs/:id only allows the user in payload.userId. Other org admins cannot poll a colleague's generation.
  7. Retry budget. Each section may run 3 times in total. The parent's attempts counts retries but is not itself capped.
  8. Testing environment. With NODE_ENV=testing, no LLM is called; stand-in questions are used (see Questions & Tags).

docs.title: 10. Endpoints summary
docs.text:
Method Path Purpose POST /v1/assessments/generate Start a generation (optional Idempotency-Key) POST /v1/assessments/:id/generation/retry Retry failed sections GET /v1/jobs/:jobId Poll the parent job; includes its section jobs GET /v1/assessments/:id Assessment with sections and generationStatus

Both POST routes need login, org_assessments:create when the org header is sent, and spend 5 units of the AI_GENERATION rate-limit scope. Full reference: API v1.

docs.title: 11. Queues, events and emails
docs.text:
Kind Name Notes Exchange question.generation (topic) Shared by all generation queues Queue question-section-mcq-queue GENERATE_MCQ_SECTION jobs Queue question-section-coding-queue GENERATE_CODING_SECTION jobs Queue question-section-descriptive-queue GENERATE_DESCRIPTIVE_SECTION jobs Queue question-generation-queue (question.generate) Older single-MCQ pipeline, see §13 Message { jobId, ...section payload } Every producer publishes exactly this, so JOB_ROUTES (src/jobs/job-routes.ts) plus the row can rebuild any message WebSocket none Clients poll GET /v1/jobs/:id Email none

Consumers only register when the instance runs with CONSUMER=true (the default). Set CONSUMER=false for API-only instances. See Jobs & Schedulers.

docs.title: 12. Where the code lives
docs.text: Path What src/assessments/assessments.controller.ts generate and retryGeneration routes, Idempotency-Key parsing src/assessments/generation/dto/ Request DTOs src/assessments/generation/assessment-generation-validator.service.ts Cross-field validation src/assessments/generation/generation-planner.ts Section layout src/assessments/generation/generation-entitlement.service.ts Plan question-type check src/assessments/generation/generation-orchestrator.service.ts Start, retry, idempotency, publish src/assessments/generation/section-generation.worker.ts Claim, generate, save, hand to aggregator src/assessments/generation/consumers/ One RabbitMQ consumer per type src/assessments/generation/generation-aggregator.service.ts Parent outcome, refund, finish src/assessments/generation/generation.constants.ts, section-limits.ts Limits, auto split, default marks, job types src/assessments/questions/questions.service.ts, section-question-writer.ts Generators and saving src/assessments/consumers/question-generation.consumer.ts Older pipeline consumer src/jobs/ Job entity rules, routes, GET /v1/jobs/:id src/ai/ LLM layer, see AI Layer

docs.title: 13. Known gaps and TODOs
docs.text:
1. Older pipeline still in use. AssessmentsService.generate() + QuestionGenerationConsumer (job type CREATE_ASSESSMENT, queue question-generation-queue) build a single MCQ section. Learning roadmaps use it (learning-roadmap-assessment.service.ts). Unlike the new pipeline it:
    • never refunds the AI_ASSESSMENT unit when publishing or generation fails,
    • saves bank questions and snapshots in separate transactions,
    • ignores the caller's maxParticipants for personal assessments (always 10), even though the roadmap sends its own value,
    • has a stale comment saying status "defaults to CREATING" (assessments.service.ts:177).
  2. No sweeper for stuck jobs. If a worker commits the section but dies before calling the aggregator, the redelivered message is dropped as already settled and the parent stays processing forever. No scheduler checks for this.
  3. No dead-letter queue and no automatic retry with back-off. All retries are manual.
  4. No push notification (WebSocket or email) when a generation finishes or fails.
  5. Short generations look "completed" but stay draft (see rule 3 in §9), with no retry path.

docs.title: 1. Purpose
docs.text:
An assessment is a test that people sit. It has a title, a schedule, a time limit, a seat limit and one or more sections of questions.

The assessments module (src/assessments/) owns:

  • creating assessments (by hand, or by AI generation),
  • their schedule and settings,
  • the draft → ready → published lifecycle,
  • who can take part (registration, invitations, removal),
  • reusable presets: assessment templates and assessment prompts,
  • admin read access to every assessment on the platform.

It does not own taking the test or scoring it. Those live in src/assessments/attempts and src/assessments/evaluation (see Attempts and Evaluation). Questions and tags have their own page: Questions & Tags. The AI generation pipeline has its own page too: AI Assessment Generation.

docs.title: 2. Key concepts
docs.text: Term Meaning Personal assessment Created without the x-organization-id header. organization_id is NULL. Owned by one user. Organization assessment Created with the x-organization-id header. Belongs to that organization. Members manage it through org roles. Section A group of questions of one type (mcq, coding or descriptive). Each section has its own question cap, difficulty and marking scheme. An assessment has 1–3 sections. Status Stored lifecycle: draft, ready or published. See §5. Phase Derived from the clock, never stored: upcoming, ongoing or completed, based on the attempt window. Registration window registration_start_time → registration_end_time. People may register or be invited only inside it. Attempt window attempt_start_time → attempt_end_time. Participants may start and answer only inside it. Duration Minutes allowed for one attempt (1–180). Separate from the attempt window. Seat A place on the assessment. Held by every invited or active participant except the creator. max_participants caps seats. Participant A row in assessments_participants: invited, active or revoked. The creator is always an active participant but holds no seat. Generation status The status of the background job that is generating the questions (assessments.job_id → jobs). Not the same as the assessment status. Template A reusable preset of settings and sections (assessment_templates). Assessment prompt A saved, reusable prompt text with tags (assessment_prompts), for the "prompt library".

docs.title: 3. Data it uses
docs.text:
All tables are described in the ERD. This module reads and writes:

  • assessments, assessment_sections, assessments_questions (question snapshots), assessments_participants
  • assessment_templates
  • assessment_prompts, assessment_prompt_tags, tags
  • jobs (generation progress, via assessments.job_id)
  • questions and its detail tables (when adding bank questions)

Things worth knowing about the shape:

  • Marking lives on the section, not the assessment. The response field correctMarks / incorrectMarks on an assessment is read from its first section (lowest order_index). Each question snapshot also copies the marks, because scoring reads the per-question marks.
  • max_total_questions is the sum of the section caps. curr_total_questions counts the questions actually in place.
  • current_participants (column) counts seats taken. The API response replaces currentParticipants with a live count of invited + active people including the creator, and exposes the stored seat count as seatsTaken (AssessmentsService.loadAssessments).
  • Assessments, participants, templates, prompts and tags are soft-deleted (deleted_at).

docs.title: 4.1 Personal vs organization
docs.text: Setting Personal Organization Schedule Fixed. Registration and attempts both open at creation and close 30 days later (PERSONAL_ASSESSMENT_WINDOW_DAYS in domain/assessment-schedule.ts). Any schedule fields in the request are ignored, and cannot be edited later. attemptStartTime and attemptEndTime are required. Registration defaults to "now → attempt end" when not given. maxParticipants Manual create: taken from the request. AI generation: always 10 (GENERATED_ASSESSMENT_MAX_PARTICIPANTS); the request value is ignored. Required, 1–10,000. Who can manage Creator only. Creator, or a member whose org role grants org_assessments:update / org_assessments:delete. Who can be invited Any email address. Unknown emails get a placeholder account. Only active members of the organization. Auto-publish after generation Yes. A fully generated personal assessment goes straight to published. No. It stops at ready so members can review it. Quota pool for AI The user's own plan. The organization's pooled plan.

docs.title: 4.2 Schedule rules
docs.text:
scheduleErrors() in src/assessments/domain/assessment-schedule.ts checks every schedule (on create and on update):

  1. registrationEndTime must be after registrationStartTime.
  2. attemptEndTime must be after attemptStartTime.
  3. registrationEndTime must not be after attemptEndTime.

Registration may open before attempts, and may stay open after attempts start. The DTO also uses the IsAfterField validator (src/assessments/validators/is-after-field.validator.ts) so that each "end" field is after its "start" field when both are sent in the same request.

docs.title: 4.3 Other limits (manual create, CreateAssessmentDto)
docs.text: Field Rule title Optional, 3–255 chars. If missing, a generated assessment takes the AI's suggested title, or the description. description Required, 10–500 chars. duration 1–180 minutes. maxTotalQuestions 1–200. correctMarks, incorrectMarks 0–999.99, 2 decimals. incorrectMarks is a positive amount that is deducted.

docs.title: 5.1 Assessment status
docs.text:
The rules live in src/assessments/domain/assessment-state.ts and assessment-transitions.ts.

stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> draft : created by hand or by generation
    draft --> ready : last question in place
    ready --> draft : cap raised or generation retried
    ready --> published : creator publishes
    draft --> published : personal generated assessment fills up
    published --> [*]
  • draft: being built. Generation may be running, may have failed, or questions are still missing.
  • ready: every section is full. The creator reviews it and may still edit anything.
  • published: open to participants. Questions are frozen. This is terminal; there is no unpublish.

The draft → published arrow is the auto-publish of a personal AI-generated assessment. In code it is ready then published in the same write (AssessmentsService.generatedOutcome).

settleByCapacity() is the single rule that moves between draft and ready: full means ready, not full means draft. It runs after adding questions, after a generation finishes, and when maxTotalQuestions is edited.

Generation progress and failure are not assessment statuses. They live on the parent job. A failed generation simply leaves the assessment in draft.

docs.title: 5.2 Phase (derived)
docs.text:
phaseAt() in domain/assessment-invariants.ts:

  • before attemptStartTime → upcoming
  • after attemptEndTime → completed
  • otherwise → ongoing

The list endpoint's status query parameter filters by phase, not by stored status.

docs.title: 5.3 Participant status
docs.text:
The rules live in domain/participant-state.ts, participant-transitions.ts and participant-invariants.ts.

stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> active : registers or is the creator
    [*] --> invited : invited by email
    invited --> active : accepts or registers
    invited --> revoked : declines or invite revoked
    active --> revoked : leaves or is removed
    revoked --> invited : invited again
    revoked --> active : registers again

Each transition returns a seatDelta (+1, 0 or −1). The service adds it to assessments.current_participants inside the same transaction. Accepting an invitation has delta 0 because the seat was taken when the invite was sent.

docs.title: 6.1 Ways to create an assessment
docs.text: Path Endpoint What happens Manual POST /v1/assessments Creates an empty draft with one MCQ section. Questions are added later from the question bank. AI generation (auto or manual mode) POST /v1/assessments/generate Creates a draft with 1–3 sections and generates every section in the background. See AI Assessment Generation. From a template Client reads GET /v1/assessment-templates, then calls POST /v1/assessments/generate in manual mode with the template's sections There is no "create from template" endpoint. The template is a preset the client turns into a generate request. Its prompt fills every section that has no prompt of its own. From a saved prompt Client reads GET /v1/assessment-prompts/..., then uses its text as the prompt of a generate request Same idea: a prompt is only reusable text. From a learning roadmap LearningRoadmapAssessmentService calls AssessmentsService.generate() Older single-section MCQ pipeline. See Learning Roadmaps and §13.

docs.title: 6.2 Manual creation, then adding questions
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant C as Client
    participant Ctrl as AssessmentsController
    participant Svc as AssessmentsService
    participant DB as PostgreSQL

    C->>Ctrl: POST /v1/assessments
    Ctrl->>Svc: create(dto, userId, org)
    Svc->>Svc: scheduleFor - fixed 30 days if personal, else from request
    Svc->>DB: BEGIN
    Svc->>DB: INSERT assessments - status draft
    Svc->>DB: INSERT assessments_participants - creator, active, no seat
    Svc->>DB: INSERT assessment_sections - one MCQ section with cap and marks
    Svc->>DB: COMMIT
    Ctrl-->>C: 201 assessment

    C->>Ctrl: POST /v1/assessments/:id/questions
    Ctrl->>Svc: addQuestions(id, dto)
    Svc->>DB: load bank questions - all must exist and be MCQ
    Svc->>DB: BEGIN
    Svc->>Svc: creator or org_assessments:update, and not published
    Svc->>Svc: fits remaining capacity, none already assigned
    Svc->>DB: INSERT assessments_questions - snapshot of each question
    Svc->>DB: UPDATE curr_total_questions and status via settleByCapacity
    Svc->>DB: COMMIT
    Ctrl-->>C: 201 added questions

When the last question is added the assessment becomes ready. The creator then calls POST /v1/assessments/:id/publish. A manually built personal assessment is not auto-published.

docs.title: 6.3 Editing and publishing
docs.text:
• PATCH /v1/assessments/:id (AssessmentsService.update):
    • In draft or ready, every field may change. Changing marks rewrites the marks on the first section and on every question snapshot, so the shown and scored marks never drift apart.
    • Once published, only title, description and maxParticipants may change (PUBLISHED_EDITABLE_FIELDS). Anything else is a 409.
    • A personal assessment's schedule can never be edited (400).
    • maxParticipants cannot go below seats already taken. maxTotalQuestions cannot go below questions already in place.
  • PUT /v1/assessments/:id/questions/:assessmentQuestionId replaces the text, options, correct option and explanation of one snapshot. MCQ only, and only before publishing. The bank question is untouched.
  • POST /v1/assessments/:id/publish moves ready → published. Publishing a draft fails with "Only an assessment with all its questions in place can be published".
  • DELETE /v1/assessments/:id soft-deletes. Needs creator or org_assessments:delete. There is no status check, so a published assessment with participants can be deleted.

docs.title: 6.4 Registering for an assessment
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant U as User
    participant Ctrl as AssessmentsController
    participant Svc as AssessmentsService
    participant Dom as Domain rules
    participant DB as PostgreSQL

    U->>Ctrl: POST /v1/assessments/:id/register
    Ctrl->>Svc: register(id, userId, org)
    Svc->>DB: BEGIN
    Svc->>DB: find assessment in scope - personal or this org
    Svc->>Dom: assertOpenToParticipants - must be published
    Svc->>Dom: assertNotEnded - attempt window not closed
    Svc->>DB: find existing participant row
    alt user holds an open invitation
        Svc->>Dom: acceptInvitation - seatDelta 0
    else no row, or revoked
        Svc->>Dom: register - seatDelta 1
        Svc->>Dom: assertRegistrationOpen
        Svc->>Dom: assertSeatsAvailable
    end
    Svc->>DB: upsert participant - status active
    Svc->>DB: increment current_participants by seatDelta
    Svc->>DB: COMMIT
    Ctrl-->>U: 201 participant

Leaving (POST /:id/unregister) does the reverse: the row becomes revoked, revoked_at is set and the seat is given back. An active participant may leave only while registration is open and before they have started an attempt (isParticipationLocked). Declining an invitation is always allowed. The creator can never leave.

docs.title: 6.5 Inviting people
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant A as Creator or org admin
    participant Inv as AssessmentInvitationsService
    participant Users as UsersService
    participant DB as PostgreSQL
    participant Mail as EmailService

    A->>Inv: POST /v1/assessments/:id/invitations with emails
    Inv->>Users: findByEmails - dedupe case-insensitively
    Inv->>DB: BEGIN
    Inv->>Inv: can manage, published, registration open
    Inv->>Inv: skip creator, non-members on org, existing invited or active
    Inv->>Inv: assertSeatsAvailable for the whole batch
    Inv->>Users: create placeholder account for unknown emails - personal only
    Inv->>DB: upsert participants - status invited, invited_by, invited_at
    Inv->>DB: increment current_participants
    Inv->>DB: COMMIT
    Inv-)Mail: sendAssessmentInvitationEmail - fire and forget
    Inv-->>A: 201 invited list and skipped list with reasons
  • Up to 50 emails per request (MAX_INVITES_PER_REQUEST).
  • Each invite reserves a seat at once. The whole batch must fit, or nothing is saved.
  • The invitee accepts with POST /:id/invitations/accept. This works until the attempt window ends, even after registration has closed and even if the assessment is now full.
  • A placeholder account is unverified, with a random password and a placeholder username. Signing up with the same email takes over that row, so the invitation is already there.
  • If someone signs up with one of the emails during the request, the unique email index fires and the API returns 409 "please retry".

docs.title: 6.6 Managing participants
docs.text:
• GET /:id/participants lists everyone (invited, active, revoked), newest first, cursor-paged, with meta.counts per status. The creator is listed with isCreator: true.
  • DELETE /:id/participants/:userId revokes an open invitation at any time, or removes an active participant only while registration is open and before they started an attempt. The creator cannot be removed.
  • GET /v1/assessments/invited lists the caller's own open invitations (org-scoped by the header).
  • POST /:id/check-enrollment tells the caller whether they are enrolled. An open invitation returns { enrolled: false, invited: true }.

docs.title: 7.1 Assessment templates
docs.text:
Code: assessment-templates.controller.ts, assessment-templates.service.ts.

A template stores: name, slug, a public 8-character uid, optional title, description, duration, maxParticipants, an ordered sections JSON array (type, count, difficulty, marks, optional title and prompt), an optional shared prompt, visibility (public / private) and isActive.

Rules:

  1. A template must always be "generatable". Its sections must pass the same limits as a manual-mode generate request (sectionLimitErrors in generation/section-limits.ts: 1–3 sections, per-type caps). Every section needs a prompt, its own or the template's.
  2. slug is derived from name unless given, and must be unique among live templates. uid is retried up to 5 times on collision.
  3. Only the owner can update or delete. Seeded templates belong to the system user, so they are read-only to everyone else.
  4. The schedule is never stored on a template. It comes from the caller, or the fixed personal schedule.
  5. GET /v1/assessment-templates is public (no login) and lists only public + active templates.

Seeding. npm run seed:assessment-templates (src/scripts/seed-assessment-templates.ts) inserts the 10 public templates in src/config/database/dummy-data/assessment-templates.ts (DSA, DBMS, networks, OS, OOP, backend, frontend, system design, DevOps, aptitude).

  • Owner: the system user (run npm run bootstrap-admin first), or --owner-email <email>.
  • Idempotent by slug: existing rows are skipped.
  • --update overwrites the seeded content of existing rows (never their uid, owner or active flag).
  • --dry-run only reports.

docs.title: 7.2 Assessment prompts (prompt library)
docs.text:
Code: assessment-prompts.controller.ts, assessment-prompts.service.ts.

A prompt has title, description, prompt text, visibility (public / private), status (draft / active / archived) and tags (via assessment_prompt_tags, referenced by tag slug).

  • GET /v1/assessment-prompts lists the caller's own prompts.
  • GET /v1/assessment-prompts/public lists public + active prompts from everyone. It can filter by tag slugs (any match) and by owner username.
  • PUT /:id replaces the whole prompt. Missing visibility / status reset to private / draft. Tags are re-synced: removed pairs are soft-deleted, new pairs are inserted.
  • Unknown tag slugs give a 404.
  • Only the owner can update or delete.

docs.title: 8. Business rules and edge cases
docs.text:
1. Scope check. Every user route resolves the assessment with findOneInScope: a personal request only sees personal assessments, an org request only sees that org's. Anything else is a 404, not a 403.
  2. Who can manage. assertCanManage allows the creator, or in an org a member whose role grants org_assessments:update (or :delete for delete). Route guards only check org_assessments:read or :create; the update/delete check happens in the service, because a creator without those permissions may still manage their own assessment (assessments.constants.ts).
  3. Published is open, nothing else is. Register, invite and accept all require published (assertOpenToParticipants).
  4. Questions freeze on publish. Adding or editing questions on a published assessment is a 409 (assertQuestionsEditable).
  5. The creator holds no seat. A personal assessment with 10 seats can have 10 people plus the creator.
  6. Seat counting is transactional. Every change to a participant and its current_participants delta happen in one DB transaction.
  7. Manual add is MCQ only. POST /:id/questions rejects coding and descriptive bank questions, and always adds into the first section.
  8. Per-question marks on manual add come from the request item, not the section. A later marks edit overwrites them all with the section's marks.
  9. Search on the user list matches description only (the admin list matches title or description).
  10. GET /v1/assessments/:id is public. It needs no login and does not check scope. It returns settings and sections, never questions.
  11. Questions with answers (GET /:id/questions) are only for people who can manage the assessment, because they include the correct options.
  12. Assistant reads are cached in Redis per user (listAssessmentsForAssistant, getAssessmentForAssistant). The phase is recomputed on read so a cached entry never shows a stale phase. Edits are not invalidated; they show after the TTL.

docs.title: 9. Endpoints summary
docs.text:
Full details live in the API reference. All user routes accept the optional x-organization-id header.

Method Path Who Purpose POST /v1/assessments logged in, org: org_assessments:create Manual create POST /v1/assessments/generate logged in, org: org_assessments:create AI generation (details) POST /v1/assessments/:id/generation/retry manager Retry failed sections GET /v1/assessments logged in List mine (personal) or the org's GET /v1/assessments/invited logged in My open invitations GET /v1/assessments/:id public Details with sections PATCH /v1/assessments/:id manager Edit settings DELETE /v1/assessments/:id manager (:delete) Soft delete POST /v1/assessments/:id/questions manager Add bank MCQs GET /v1/assessments/:id/questions manager Questions with answers PUT /v1/assessments/:id/questions/:assessmentQuestionId manager Edit one MCQ snapshot POST /v1/assessments/:id/publish manager ready → published POST /v1/assessments/:id/invitations manager Invite by email POST /v1/assessments/:id/invitations/accept invitee Accept GET /v1/assessments/:id/participants manager List participants DELETE /v1/assessments/:id/participants/:userId manager Revoke or remove POST /v1/assessments/:id/register logged in Register POST /v1/assessments/:id/unregister participant Leave or decline POST /v1/assessments/:id/check-enrollment logged in Am I enrolled? GET /v1/assessment-templates public Public templates POST / PATCH / DELETE /v1/assessment-templates[/:uid] logged in / owner Manage templates GET /v1/assessment-prompts, /public, /:id logged in Prompt library POST / PUT / DELETE /v1/assessment-prompts[/:id] logged in / owner Manage prompts GET /v1/admin/assessments, /v1/admin/assessments/:id platform assessments:read See every assessment

"Manager" means the creator, or an org member whose role grants org_assessments:update.

Admin endpoints (src/assessments/admin.controller.ts, admin.service.ts) are read-only. They list every assessment (personal and org) with filters workspace (personal / organization), organization (uid), assessment_status, search, plus the shared phase/sort/paging filters. They include the owner and organization, and report the stored seat count.

Rate limits. The controller uses policy CLASS_B. generate and generation/retry also spend 5 units of the AI_GENERATION scope. See Platform Services.

Leaderboard. The leaderboard lives in src/assessments/attempts/leaderboard.*. See Attempts.

docs.title: 10. Async work, events and emails
docs.text: What When Where Assessment invitation email After a successful invite, one per invited person. Fire and forget; a failure is only logged. EmailService.sendAssessmentInvitationEmail (Notifications) Question generation jobs (RabbitMQ) POST /generate and retry AI Assessment Generation WebSocket events None from this module. Clients poll GET /v1/jobs/:jobId for generation progress. Realtime Events

docs.title: 11. Usage limits (commerce)
docs.text:
• Manual creation, invitations and registration are not metered.
  • AI generation spends one unit of the AI_ASSESSMENT feature and checks ALLOWED_QUESTION_TYPES against the plan. In an org, the org's pooled plan is used. Details in AI Assessment Generation and Commerce.

docs.title: 12. Where the code lives
docs.text:
Path What src/assessments/assessments.controller.ts User routes src/assessments/assessments.service.ts Create, update, publish, add questions, register, list, assistant reads, the older generate() src/assessments/assessment-invitations.service.ts Invite and accept src/assessments/assessment-participants.service.ts List and remove participants src/assessments/admin.controller.ts, admin.service.ts Platform admin reads src/assessments/assessment-templates.*, assessment-prompts.* Templates and prompt library src/assessments/domain/ Pure rules (see below) src/assessments/validators/is-after-field.validator.ts IsAfterField class-validator constraint src/assessments/assessments.constants.ts Org permission strings, personal seat limit, default section title src/assessments/serializers/assessments.serializer.ts Response shapes src/assessments/repositories/ Empty. Services use TypeORM repositories and DataSource directly. src/scripts/seed-assessment-templates.ts Template seeding

The domain/ folder holds pure functions and enums with no Nest or DB code, so the rules can be unit tested on their own:

File Rules assessment-state.ts AssessmentStatus, AssessmentPhase, shape types assessment-transitions.ts Allowed status moves, settleByCapacity, publishAssessment, reopenForGeneration assessment-invariants.ts phaseAt, registration open, published only, seats available, seat limit covers taken seats, locked fields after publish assessment-schedule.ts Personal 30-day schedule, org schedule defaults, schedule ordering errors participant-*.ts Participant status, transitions with seat deltas, who may leave generation-outcome.ts Generation outcome from section jobs (see AI Assessment Generation) descriptive-invariants.ts Checkpoint weight rules (see Questions & Tags) attempt-*.ts, response-*.ts Attempt and response rules (see Attempts, Evaluation)

Rule violations throw DomainError (rule → 400, conflict → 409, forbidden → 403).

docs.title: 13. Known gaps and TODOs
docs.text:
1. Two generation pipelines. POST /generate uses the new section pipeline. The older AssessmentsService.generate() (single MCQ section, CREATE_ASSESSMENT job, QuestionGenerationConsumer) is still used by learning roadmaps. It never refunds the quota on failure.
  2. Multi-section edits only touch the first section. update() writes maxTotalQuestions and marks onto the first section only, and applies those marks to every question in the assessment. For a generated assessment with MCQ and coding sections this can give coding questions MCQ marks and give the first section the whole assessment's cap.
  3. Manual add always targets the first section, even when that section is coding or descriptive.
  4. No way for normal users to browse the question bank. Manual add needs bank question IDs, but listing the bank is admin-only (/v1/admin/questions).
  5. No "my templates" or "get template by uid" endpoint. A user cannot list their own private templates.
  6. GET /v1/assessment-prompts/:id does not check visibility or owner. Any logged-in user can read anyone's private or draft prompt by ID.
  7. GET /v1/assessments/:id is public and unscoped. Org assessment settings and the description (which, for generated ones, is the full prompt) are readable without login.
  8. Swagger text is out of date in a few places (publish says "draft to ready"; update says only maxParticipants may change after publish; invite says "has not ended" but the code requires registration to be open).
  9. Delete has no status guard. A published assessment with active participants can be soft-deleted.
  10. GET /v1/assessments/invited reports invitedAt from the row's created_at, which is wrong for someone invited again after being revoked.

docs.title: 1. Purpose
docs.text:
An attempt is one participant sitting one assessment. The attempts feature covers everything from "Start test" to "see my result":

  • start (or resume) an attempt, after checking the user may sit the assessment
  • show the questions without leaking the answers
  • save, change and clear answers while the test is open
  • run code for coding questions (streamed over WebSocket)
  • submit the attempt and hand it to evaluation
  • show the result, analytics, and an AI conversation once the attempt is graded
  • let reviewers list attempts, read answers, and reject an attempt
  • rank evaluated attempts on a leaderboard

The code lives in src/assessments/attempts/. The rules (what may happen in which state) live in small pure functions in src/assessments/domain/.

docs.title: 2. Key concepts
docs.text: Term Meaning Attempt A row in assessment_attempts. Each user has at most one attempt per assessment. It has a public uid (UUID) used in all URLs. The numeric id is internal. Response A row in assessment_attempt_responses. It holds the user's answer to one question in one attempt. Participant A row in assessment_participants. A user must be an active participant to start. See assessments. Attempt window attemptStartTime to attemptEndTime on the assessment. You can only start an attempt and write answers inside this window. Registration window registrationStartTime to registrationEndTime. Users can register (become active) only inside it. This is separate from the attempt window. Settled attempt An attempt in evaluated or rejected. Nothing changes it any more (except evaluated to rejected), so reads about it are cached. Code run Running the user's code against the visible test cases, or once on custom input, during the test. Nothing is saved. Rejection A reviewer sets an attempt aside with a reason. The score is kept for the record, but the user sees the reason instead of a result, and the attempt leaves the leaderboard.

docs.title: 3. Data used
docs.text:
See ERD: Assessment Engine for full table definitions. This feature reads and writes:

  • assessment_attempts: status, started_at, submitted_at, score, counters (total_questions, attempted_questions, correct_responses, incorrect_responses), rejection fields (rejected_at, rejected_by, rejection_reason), and next_assessment_suggestion (jsonb, section 5.7). A unique constraint UQ_assessment_attempts_user_assessment on (user_id, assessment_id) enforces one attempt per user.
  • assessment_attempt_responses: answer (jsonb: the MCQ option or descriptive text), language and source_code (coding), evaluation_status, code_verdict, is_correct, marks_awarded, evaluation_result (jsonb), answered_at, evaluated_at.
  • jobs: the submit step creates an EVALUATE_ATTEMPT job row. See jobs and schedulers.
  • Reads assessments, assessment_sections, assessment_questions and assessment_participants.

docs.title: 4. Attempt lifecycle
docs.text:
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> in_progress: start
    in_progress --> submitted: user submits
    submitted --> evaluating: evaluation job claims it
    evaluating --> evaluated: all responses graded and scored
    in_progress --> rejected: reviewer rejects
    submitted --> rejected: reviewer rejects
    evaluating --> rejected: reviewer rejects
    evaluated --> rejected: reviewer rejects
    rejected --> [*]
    evaluated --> [*]
Status What it means What the user can do in_progress Being sat. Answers can change. Read questions, save/clear answers, run code, submit submitted Handed in. Waiting for the evaluation job. Wait. Result returns 400 "not evaluated yet". evaluating The evaluator is grading responses. Wait. evaluated Graded and scored. See result, analytics, open AI conversation, appear on leaderboard rejected Set aside by a reviewer. Result returns 409 with the reviewer's reason

The transition table is ATTEMPT_TRANSITIONS in src/assessments/domain/attempt-transitions.ts.

Each response also has its own small lifecycle (pending, processing, completed, failed, cancelled). Every saved answer starts as pending. Grading happens only after submit. See evaluation.

docs.title: 5.1 Start, answer, submit
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor U as Participant
    participant C as AttemptsController
    participant S as AttemptsService
    participant DB as Postgres
    participant MQ as RabbitMQ
    U->>C: POST /v1/attempts/:assessmentId/start
    C->>S: startAttempt
    S->>DB: load assessment and participant
    S->>S: check participant active, assessment published, window open
    S->>DB: find attempt for user and assessment
    alt attempt exists
        S-->>U: existing uid - resume
    else no attempt yet
        S->>DB: insert attempt in_progress
        S-->>U: new uid
    end
    U->>C: GET /v1/attempts/:uid/questions
    C-->>U: question list with saved answers
    U->>C: GET /v1/attempts/:uid/questions/:qid
    C-->>U: question detail without answer key
    U->>C: PUT /v1/attempts/:uid/responses/:qid
    C->>S: upsertResponse
    S->>S: attempt in_progress and window open
    S->>DB: upsert response as pending, clear old grade
    C-->>U: true
    U->>C: POST /v1/attempts/:uid/submit
    C->>S: submitAttempt
    S->>DB: TX - update status to submitted where status is in_progress
    S->>DB: TX - insert EVALUATE_ATTEMPT job
    S->>MQ: publish attempt.evaluate
    C-->>U: true

Starting (AttemptsService.startAttempt) checks, in order:

  1. The assessment exists (404 otherwise).
  2. The user is an active participant (assertActive in domain/participant-invariants.ts). An invited user gets 403 "Accept the invitation before starting". No row, or a revoked row, gets 403 "You are not registered". The creator has an active participant row too, so they can sit their own assessment.
  3. The assessment is PUBLISHED (assertOpenToParticipants). Drafts cannot be attempted by anyone, the creator included, because their questions can still change.
  4. Now is inside the attempt window (assertOngoing). Before it: "has not started yet". After it: "has ended".
  5. Inside a transaction: if an attempt for this user and assessment already exists, its uid is returned. Otherwise a new in_progress attempt is inserted with startedAt = now and totalQuestions = assessment.currTotalQuestions.

There is no separate organization-membership check at start. For organization assessments, access comes from the participant row created when the invitation is accepted. See organizations.

Saving an answer (upsertResponse) requires the attempt to be in_progress, the window to be open, and the question to belong to the attempt's assessment. The body depends on the question type:

Question type Body Extra checks MCQ { optionId } optionId must be one of the question's options Coding { language, code } language must be in the question's supportedLanguages Descriptive { text } none. A blank text is kept and later grades to zero.

Sending fields of another type (for example code on an MCQ) is a 400. Every save resets evaluationStatus to pending and clears isCorrect, marksAwarded, codeVerdict and evaluationResult. A client can autosave coding answers safely because each save replaces the last one.

Clearing an answer (DELETE /v1/attempts/:uid/responses/:qid) has the same checks and deletes the response row. A question with no response is simply not graded (zero marks, no penalty).

Submitting (submitAttempt) runs one transaction:

  1. UPDATE assessment_attempts SET status='submitted', submitted_at=now WHERE id=? AND status='in_progress'. If no row changed, it throws 409 "already submitted".
  2. Insert a jobs row: type EVALUATE_ATTEMPT, queue attempt-evaluation, maxAttempts = 3, payload { attemptId, attemptUid, assessmentId, userId }.

After the commit, it publishes { jobId, ...payload } to exchange attempt with routing key attempt.evaluate. If the publish fails, the job is marked FAILED (it can be retried later) but the submission still stands and the user gets true. Grading then continues asynchronously. See evaluation.

docs.title: 5.2 What the user sees during the test
docs.text:
• GET /questions returns, for each question: id, order, section, and the user's saved answer (selectedOptionId, code, or text).
  • GET /questions/:qid returns the question text, type, options (without correctOptionId), the coding view (input/output format, constraints, starter code, languages, limits, and visible test cases only), and the descriptive view (maxWords only, because checkpoints are the answer key).
  • The answer key and explanation are only returned by GET /result, which needs an evaluated attempt.

Caching (Redis, via RedisHelper.safeGet/safeSet):

Read Cached when Key prefix TTL Question list with answers attempt is settled attempts:questions:v4: 1 hour Single question detail always (it carries no answer) attempts:question:v3: 1 hour Result always (only reachable when evaluated) attempts:result:v8: 1 hour Analytics attempt is settled attempts:analytics:v2: 1 hour

docs.title: 5.3 Running code during an attempt
docs.text:
Code runs go over the Socket.IO connection, not REST, so results can stream back case by case. The engine behind it is described in code execution.

sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor U as Participant socket
    participant G as EventsGateway
    participant R as CodeRunService
    participant CR as CodeRunner
    U->>G: emit code.run with requestId, attemptUid, questionId, language, code, mode
    G->>R: start
    R->>R: attempt in_progress, coding question of this assessment, language allowed
    R->>R: one run in flight per user, 5 second cooldown
    R-->>U: code.run.started with total
    loop each visible test case or the one custom input
        R->>CR: run
        CR-->>R: result
        R-->>U: code.run.case with passed, stdout, stderr, time, memory
    end
    R-->>U: code.run.completed with passed and total
    Note over R,U: on a runner error R emits code.run.failed instead

Rules (src/assessments/attempts/code-run/code-run.service.ts):

  1. mode: "samples" runs the question's visible test cases. Hidden test cases are never run here. They belong to grading.
  2. mode: "custom" runs once on the given stdin and returns the output in code.run.completed.
  3. The question must be a coding question of the attempt's assessment, and the language must be one the question offers and one the configured runner supports.
  4. One run in flight per user, and at most one new run every 5 seconds (CODE_RUN_COOLDOWN_MS). A refused run comes back as a socket exception event (409 or 429 with retryAfterMs).
  5. Code and stdin are each capped at 50,000 characters (RunCodeDto).
  6. Nothing is saved. The user must still PUT the response to keep the code.
  7. Events go only to the socket that started the run, not to the user's other tabs.

docs.title: 5.4 After submission: result, analytics, AI conversation
docs.text:
Endpoint Available when Notes GET /v1/attempts/:uid/result evaluated Full per-question breakdown: chosen and correct option, explanation, submitted code, test-case results (hidden cases show only pass/fail and a generic message), descriptive checkpoint results, marks, and per-section breakdown. Also nextAssessmentSuggestion: the stored suggestion, or null (see 5.7). rejected gives 409 with the reason. Any other status gives 400. POST /v1/attempts/:uid/next-assessment evaluated Suggests the next assessment to take and stores it on the attempt. See 5.7. GET /v1/attempts/:uid/analytics any status Score, accuracy, negative marks, a timeline in buckets of intervalMinutes (1 to 60, default 5), topic and section stats. A live attempt is recomputed on every call. POST /v1/attempts/:uid/conversations evaluated Opens (or returns) an AI conversation about this attempt. Blocked earlier so the bot cannot leak answers mid-test. See AI assistant. GET /v1/attempts any The caller's attempts, newest first, filterable by status and assessmentId, paginated.

Hidden test cases stay hidden even after evaluation, because other participants may still be sitting the same assessment.

docs.title: 5.5 Reviewing and rejecting attempts
docs.text:
Two sets of routes share one service (AttemptReviewService):

  • Organization reviewers use /v1/assessments/:id/attempts.... These need the x-organization-id header (400 without it). Permissions are checked against the member's org role, and only that organization's assessments resolve.
  • Platform admins use /v1/admin/assessments/:id/attempts.... These are checked against platform roles and reach any assessment. See RBAC.
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor R as Reviewer
    participant C as Review or Admin controller
    participant S as AttemptReviewService
    participant DB as Postgres
    R->>C: POST .../attempts/:attemptUid/reject with reason
    C->>S: reject
    S->>DB: resolve assessment in scope
    S->>DB: TX - load attempt
    S->>S: rejectAttempt - fails if already rejected
    S->>DB: TX - update status rejected where status is unchanged
    alt no row updated
        S-->>R: 409 attempt changed, try again
    else updated
        S-->>R: attempt with rejection details and maxScore
    end

Effects of a rejection:

  • An in_progress attempt is closed. Because start returns the existing row, the user cannot restart.
  • A submitted or evaluating attempt stops being graded. Child evaluation jobs see the new status and cancel themselves. See evaluation.
  • An evaluated attempt keeps its score, but GET /result returns 409 with the reason, and it drops off the leaderboard.

GET .../attempts lists attempts newest first, with filters for status and search (username, email or full name, ILIKE). Each row includes maxScore, which is the sum of every question's correctMarks. GET .../attempts/:attemptUid/responses returns every question with the participant's answer and the full grading detail, including hidden test-case inputs and outputs.

docs.title: 5.6 Leaderboard
docs.text:
GET /v1/assessments/:id/leaderboard (LeaderboardService):

  1. Only evaluated attempts are ranked. Users with deleted accounts are left out.
  2. Order: higher score first, then shorter time_taken_ms (submitted_at - started_at, whole milliseconds).
  3. Rank uses SQL RANK(), so ties share a rank and the next rank skips (1, 1, 3).
  4. Paging is keyset-based. cursor is the attempt id of the last row on the previous page (meta.nextCursor). The page size is limit (default 20).
  5. meta.me is the caller's own entry wherever it falls, or null if they have no evaluated attempt.
  6. Access: for a personal assessment, the creator and active participants only (invited or revoked users get 403). Inside an organization, members whose role grants org_assessments:read, and the assessment must belong to that organization.

docs.title: 5.7 Next-assessment suggestion
docs.text:
After an attempt is evaluated, the user can ask for the next assessment to take. The AI reads how they did and designs a follow-up test that targets their weak sections and topics, at a difficulty set by their accuracy. The suggestion is shaped like an assessment template, so the client starts it the same way as a template: as a manual-mode generate request.

The suggestion is not saved as a template. It is a JSON object stored on the attempt, in assessment_attempts.next_assessment_suggestion. Each attempt has at most one.

sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Client
    participant API as AttemptsController
    participant S as AttemptSuggestionService
    participant U as UsageService
    participant AI as AssessmentSuggestionAiService
    participant DB as Postgres

    C->>API: POST /v1/attempts/:uid/next-assessment
    API->>S: suggestNext(attemptUid, userId)
    S->>DB: load attempt (must be the caller's, status evaluated)
    S->>U: getFeatureValue(AI_ASSESSMENT_SUGGESTION)
    alt plan does not include it
        S-->>C: 403
    end
    alt attempt already has a suggestion
        S-->>C: 200 stored suggestion (no LLM call)
    end
    S->>DB: attempt analytics, assessment, sections
    S->>U: getFeatureValue(ALLOWED_QUESTION_TYPES)
    S->>AI: suggestNextAssessment(performance, default model)
    AI-->>S: name, title, description, prompt, duration, sections
    S->>DB: UPDATE assessment_attempts SET next_assessment_suggestion WHERE id AND next_assessment_suggestion IS NULL
    S-->>C: 200 suggestion

What the model gets: the assessment taken (title, description, duration), the overall result, one row per section (question type, difficulty, accuracy, correct, incorrect and unanswered counts, score) and one row per topic. These come from the same analytics as GET /analytics. It also gets the question types the user's plan allows.

What it returns (and what is stored):

Field Notes name, title, description title is what the new assessment is created with. description tells the user why this test, from their result. prompt What the whole assessment covers. duration Minutes, 5 to 180. maxTotalQuestions The sections' question counts summed (computed, not from the model). sections[] 1 to 3, in order. Each has title, prompt, questionType, questionCount, difficulty (1–5), positiveMark, negativeMark. generatedAt ISO time it was made.

Rules:

  1. Plan feature. Generating needs AI_ASSESSMENT_SUGGESTION on the user's personal plan, with any non-blank value. Without it, 403. It is a setting, not a quota: nothing is consumed. See Commerce.
  2. Evaluated only. The same check as GET /result: rejected gives 409, any other status gives 400.
  3. One per attempt, generated once. A POST on an attempt that already has a suggestion returns it with no LLM call. The plan is still checked first.
  4. Two requests at once. Both may call the model, but the write only lands while the column is null. The second request reads back and returns the first one's suggestion.
  5. Default model. The call always uses the registry's default model, not the plan's AI_MODEL.
  6. Generation limits are enforced on the output. Section count, per-section and per-assessment question limits, and the plan's allowed question types are checked in the parse step. A violation is sent back to the model as a repair turn (up to 3 calls in all).
  7. Difficulty rule (in the prompt, not enforced in code): accuracy below 40% → one level easier; 40–75% → same level; above 75% → one level harder.
  8. Marks are not the model's choice. Each section reuses the marks of the first section of the same question type in the attempted assessment. A type that assessment did not have gets +1 / −0.
  9. Starting it costs a normal generation. The suggestion only describes the assessment. Starting it is a manual-mode POST /v1/assessments/generate, which spends AI_ASSESSMENT like any other generation. maxParticipants is not stored; a personal assessment uses its fixed default.

Reading it back. GET /v1/attempts/:uid/result returns nextAssessmentSuggestion (the stored object, or null). The client shows the suggestion when it is there, and a "Suggest my next test" button when it is null. The result is cached in Redis once evaluated (section 5.4), but the suggestion is not part of the cached entry. It is read from the attempt on every call, so a suggestion made after the first read still appears.

docs.title: 6. Business rules and edge cases
docs.text:
1. One attempt per user per assessment. This is enforced by the unique constraint and by startAttempt returning the existing attempt. There is no "max attempts" setting and no retake.
  2. Resuming is the same call as starting. POST /start returns the existing uid whatever its status. The client then reads /questions to restore saved answers.
  3. No server-side timer. The assessment has a duration field, but the backend does not enforce it per attempt. There is no auto-submit, no scheduler, and no delayed queue. The only time limit is the assessment's attempt window: after attemptEndTime, starting and saving or clearing answers fail with "This assessment has ended". The client is expected to show the countdown and call submit.
  4. Submitting after the deadline is allowed. submitAttempt does not check the window, so an attempt can be handed in (and graded) after attemptEndTime. Only the answers saved before the end are graded, because writes were blocked after it.
  5. Never-submitted attempts stay in_progress forever. They are never graded and never appear on the leaderboard.
  6. Double submit is safe. The status update is conditional on status = 'in_progress', so only one of two racing requests wins. The other gets 409 "already submitted". Only one evaluation job is created.
  7. Double start (race). Two concurrent first starts can both see no attempt. The second insert then breaks the unique constraint. This is not caught, so it surfaces as a 500 (see section 10).
  8. Answers must match the question type. Sending fields of another type gives a 400. An MCQ option must be one of the question's options. A coding language must be offered by the question.
  9. Questions are frozen once published. Questions can only be edited while the assessment is a draft, so question detail is safe to cache during a live attempt.
  10. Rejection is final. rejected has no outgoing transitions, and rejecting twice gives 409.
  11. The result is only for evaluated. A submitted or evaluating attempt gives 400 "not evaluated yet". The client polls until it is ready (no push event, see section 8).

docs.title: 7. Endpoints summary
docs.text:
Full request and response shapes are in API v1.

Method Path Who Purpose GET /v1/attempts owner List my attempts POST /v1/attempts/:assessmentId/start active participant Start or resume, returns { uid } GET /v1/attempts/:attemptUid/questions owner Question list with saved answers GET /v1/attempts/:attemptUid/questions/:assessmentQuestionId owner One question, no answer key PUT /v1/attempts/:attemptUid/responses/:assessmentQuestionId owner Save or replace an answer DELETE /v1/attempts/:attemptUid/responses/:assessmentQuestionId owner Clear an answer (204) POST /v1/attempts/:attemptUid/submit owner Submit for evaluation GET /v1/attempts/:attemptUid/result owner Graded result GET /v1/attempts/:attemptUid/analytics owner Analytics POST /v1/attempts/:attemptUid/conversations owner Open the AI conversation POST /v1/attempts/:attemptUid/next-assessment owner, plan AI_ASSESSMENT_SUGGESTION Suggest the next assessment (stored on the attempt) GET /v1/assessments/:id/leaderboard creator, participants, org members Ranked board GET /v1/assessments/:id/attempts org: assessment_attempts:read List attempts (org) GET /v1/assessments/:id/attempts/:attemptUid/responses org: assessment_attempt_responses:read Read answers (org) POST /v1/assessments/:id/attempts/:attemptUid/reject org: assessment_attempts:update Reject (org) GET /v1/admin/assessments/:id/attempts platform: assessment_attempts:read List attempts (admin) GET /v1/admin/assessments/:id/attempts/:attemptUid/responses platform: assessment_attempt_responses:read Read answers (admin) POST /v1/admin/assessments/:id/attempts/:attemptUid/reject platform: assessment_attempts:update Reject (admin)

Rate limits: most routes use policy CLASS_C. start, submit, conversations and next-assessment use the stricter CLASS_B. See platform services.

docs.title: 8. Async events, queues and WebSocket events
docs.text:
Kind Name Direction Notes RabbitMQ exchange attempt, key attempt.evaluate, queue attempt-evaluation-queue published on submit Message is { jobId, attemptId, attemptUid, assessmentId, userId } Job row EVALUATE_ATTEMPT in jobs created on submit Can be polled with GET /v1/jobs/:id if the id is known Socket in code.run client to server Body is RunCodeDto Socket out code.run.started, code.run.case, code.run.completed, code.run.failed server to the same socket Every event carries the client's requestId Socket out exception server to client A refused run (validation, wrong attempt, rate limit)

No WebSocket event or email is sent when an attempt is submitted, evaluated or rejected.

docs.title: 9. Where the code lives
docs.text: Path What src/assessments/attempts/attempts.controller.ts / attempts.service.ts Participant routes: start, questions, responses, submit, result, conversation src/assessments/attempts/analytics.service.ts Attempt analytics SQL src/assessments/attempts/attempt-suggestion.service.ts Next-assessment suggestion: plan check, analytics to prompt input, store on the attempt src/assessments/attempts/leaderboard.controller.ts / leaderboard.service.ts Leaderboard (raw SQL with RANK()) src/assessments/attempts/attempt-review.controller.ts / attempt-review.service.ts Org reviewer routes and shared review logic src/assessments/attempts/admin.controller.ts / admin.service.ts Platform-admin wrappers over the review service src/assessments/attempts/code-run/ Live code runs (service, DTO, socket event shapes) src/assessments/attempts/section-breakdown.helper.ts Per-section stats for the result src/assessments/attempts/serializers/attempts.serializer.ts Response shaping, including serializeNextAssessmentSuggestion src/assessments/domain/attempt-*.ts, response-*.ts, participant-invariants.ts, assessment-invariants.ts State machines and rules src/events/events.gateway.ts Socket.IO code.run handler src/common/helpers/question-content.helper.ts Candidate-safe views of questions and grades

docs.title: 10. Known gaps and TODOs found in code
docs.text:
1. No duration enforcement and no auto-submit. assessment.duration is only displayed. Nothing closes an attempt when its time runs out or when the window ends (attempts.service.ts startAttempt and submitAttempt).
  2. Submit ignores the window (attempts.service.ts:339-341), while saving answers does not (resolveAnswerableQuestion, line 229).
  3. Code runs ignore the window. CodeRunService.prepare checks only assertAnswerable (code-run.service.ts:72-73), so code can still be run after attemptEndTime while the attempt is in_progress.
  4. The start race gives a 500. The unique violation on UQ_assessment_attempts_user_assessment is not caught in startAttempt (attempts.service.ts:86-99).
  5. Out-of-date Swagger text. The PUT response route says MCQ answers are "graded at once" (attempts.controller.ts:335), but every answer is saved pending and graded after submit. The start route lists "already completed it" as a 400 (attempts.controller.ts:136), but start just returns the existing attempt.
  6. Code-run limits are per process. The in-flight set and the cooldown map live in memory (code-run.service.ts:46-48). With several instances, a user can run once per instance. The lastRunAt map is never pruned.
  7. No push when grading finishes. The client has to poll GET /result. The submit response does not include the job id.
  8. The result header marks come from the first section. assessment.correctMarks/incorrectMarks in GET /result come from findSectionMarks, while grading uses each question's own marks (attempts.service.ts:400, 459-460). These can differ when an assessment has several sections.

docs.title: 1. Purpose
docs.text:
This module answers one question for every request: "Who is calling, and can their account still be used?"

It covers:

  • Sign-up and sign-in: email or username plus password, and Google sign-in.
  • Email verification: a link sent by email. An account must be verified before it can call any protected route.
  • Password reset: a "forgot password" email with a one-time link.
  • Tokens: a short-lived access token for API calls and a longer-lived refresh token to get new access tokens.
  • The global auth guard: it runs on every HTTP request and puts the caller on request.user.
  • The current user's profile (GET /v1/auth/me).
  • Admin user management: listing users and adding or removing platform roles.

This module does not decide what a signed-in user is allowed to do. Roles and permissions do that. See RBAC and Organizations.

The old docs were wrong

Earlier versions of this page said there was no Google sign-in, no email verification and no password reset. All three exist now. Auth does not use Redis. Refresh tokens are stored in Postgres. Redis is used by the rate limiter (see Platform services).

docs.title: 2. Key terms
docs.text: Term Meaning JWT JSON Web Token. A signed string that carries a small JSON payload. The server can check the signature without calling the database. Access token A JWT sent as Authorization: Bearer <token> on every API call. Signed with JWT_ACCESS_SECRET. Refresh token A JWT used only on POST /v1/auth/refresh to get a new token pair. Signed with JWT_REFRESH_SECRET. Its SHA-256 hash is stored in refresh_tokens. Token payload { sub, email, username }. sub is the user id. The type is JwtPayload in src/identity/auth/guards/jwt-auth.guard.ts. Verified account users.is_verified = true. The user clicked the email link, or signed in with Google. Active account users.is_active = true. A token for an inactive (deactivated) account is rejected. Placeholder account An unverified account the system creates for someone invited to an organization who has no account yet. Its username starts with invited_. See Organizations. mustChangePassword A flag on the user. It is set when the system generated the password (Google sign-in). Login returns it so the client can ask the user to pick a new password. @Public() A decorator that tells the global auth guard to skip a route.
