In src/common/decorators/public.decorator.ts. @CurrentUser() A parameter decorator that returns request.user (the JwtPayload). In src/identity/auth/decorators/current-user.decorator.ts.

docs.title: 3. Data it uses
docs.text:
See the ERD for the full table definitions. This module reads and writes:

Table Used for users Account details, bcrypt password hash (cost 10), is_active, is_verified, must_change_password, oauth_provider / oauth_id, and the verification email counters (total_verification_email, last_verification_email_sent_at). refresh_tokens token_hash, user_id, expires_at, deleted_at. One row per user (see rule 6). users_roles, roles Platform roles. The admin user endpoints read and write them. subscriptions A free subscription is created when an account becomes verified (see Commerce).

Uniqueness rules on users:

  • email and username are unique among rows that are not soft-deleted.
  • (oauth_provider, oauth_id) is unique when oauth_id is set.
  • phone_number is unique.

docs.title: 4. Configuration
docs.text:
Env var Meaning JWT_ACCESS_SECRET, JWT_ACCESS_EXPIRY Access token secret and lifetime in seconds. JWT_REFRESH_SECRET, JWT_REFRESH_EXPIRY Refresh token secret and lifetime in seconds. JWT_EMAIL_VERIFICATION_SECRET, JWT_EMAIL_VERIFICATION_EXPIRY Verification link token. Example: 86400 (1 day). JWT_PASSWORD_RESET_SECRET, JWT_PASSWORD_RESET_EXPIRY Reset link token. Example: 900 (15 minutes). GOOGLE_OAUTH2_CLIENT_ID Google client id. Google ID tokens must have this as their audience. FRONTEND_URL Base URL for email links (/verify-email?token=..., /reset-password?token=...).

The code reads every expiry with +value. So each one must be a plain number of seconds. See Known gaps for the problem with .env.example.

docs.title: 5.1 Sign-up and email verification
docs.text:
1. The client calls POST /v1/auth/signup with first name, last name, username, email, password and an optional phone number.
  2. UsersService.create checks the email:
    • No account has that email: it checks that the username and phone are free, then creates a new user.
    • An unverified account has that email (an unfinished sign-up, or a placeholder made by an org invite): it takes over that row. It replaces the name, username, phone and password. The row keeps its id, so any org invitation waiting on it stays attached.
    • A verified account has that email: 409 Conflict.
  3. The server signs a token pair and stores the refresh token. It returns the tokens, but they cannot be used yet, because the guard rejects unverified accounts.
  4. The server sends a verification email. It does not wait for the send to finish (fire-and-forget). The link holds a JWT with { email }. The send time and a counter are saved on the user.
  5. The user clicks the link. The frontend calls GET /v1/auth/verify-email?token=....
  6. In one transaction, the user is marked verified and a free subscription is created. Then a welcome email is sent.
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant C as Client
    participant A as AuthController
    participant S as AuthService
    participant U as UsersService
    participant DB as Postgres
    participant M as EmailService
    C->>A: POST /v1/auth/signup
    A->>S: signup(dto)
    S->>U: create(dto)
    U->>DB: find user by email
    alt no user or unverified user
        U->>DB: insert new user or take over unverified row
    else verified user exists
        U-->>C: 409 Conflict
    end
    S->>S: sign access and refresh tokens
    S->>DB: upsert refresh_tokens row with hash
    S-->>M: send verification email, not awaited
    S->>DB: bump verification counter and timestamp
    S-->>C: 200 with tokens
    Note over C: Tokens fail on protected routes until verified
    C->>A: GET /v1/auth/verify-email?token=...
    A->>S: verifyEmail(token)
    S->>S: verify JWT with email verification secret
    S->>DB: BEGIN, set is_verified, create free subscription, COMMIT
    S-->>M: send welcome email, not awaited
    S-->>C: 200 Email verified successfully

docs.title: 5.2 Login with password
docs.text:
1. The client calls POST /v1/auth/login with either email or username, plus password.
  2. The server looks up the user. A missing user and a wrong password return the same error: 401 Invalid credentials.
  3. If the account is not verified, the server may send a fresh verification email. Then it returns 401 Please verify your email before logging in. It only sends a new email when the last one has expired (it is older than JWT_EMAIL_VERIFICATION_EXPIRY). This stops people from using login to spam someone's inbox.
  4. Otherwise, the server signs a token pair and saves the refresh token hash.
  5. If mustChangePassword is true, the response also contains mustChangePassword: true.
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant C as Client
    participant S as AuthService
    participant DB as Postgres
    participant M as EmailService
    C->>S: POST /v1/auth/login with email or username and password
    S->>DB: find user
    alt user missing or bcrypt compare fails
        S-->>C: 401 Invalid credentials
    else not verified
        opt last verification email has expired
            S-->>M: send new verification email
        end
        S-->>C: 401 Please verify your email
    else ok
        S->>S: sign access and refresh tokens
        S->>DB: upsert the user's single refresh_tokens row
        S-->>C: 200 accessToken, refreshToken, maybe mustChangePassword
    end

Login does not check is_active. A deactivated user can still get tokens, but the guard rejects them on the first protected call.

docs.title: 5.3 Google sign-in
docs.text:
The frontend uses Google's sign-in button to get a Google ID token and sends it to the backend. The backend has no redirect flow and no Passport strategy.

  1. The client calls POST /v1/auth/google with { idToken }.
  2. GoogleOAuthService.verifyIdToken checks the token with google-auth-library. The audience must equal GOOGLE_OAUTH2_CLIENT_ID, and Google must say the email is verified. Otherwise the server returns 401.
  3. Inside one transaction, the server finds the user by email and takes one of three paths:
Case What happens No account Create a user. The name comes from Google. The username is made from the email prefix and is unique. The password is a random 8-character one, with mustChangePassword = true and isVerified = true. The Google ids are saved. A free subscription is created. Unverified account (unfinished sign-up or org placeholder) "Claim" it. Replace the name and any placeholder username. Set a new random password. Mark it verified and link Google. Revoke all its refresh tokens. Create a free subscription. This blocks account pre-hijacking: someone who signed up with your email but never verified it cannot keep a password on your account. Verified account Link Google to it (save oauth_provider and oauth_id) if it is not linked yet. The password stays the same.
  1. The server signs a token pair.
  2. In the first two cases only, the server sends a welcome email with the username and generated password, so the user can also log in with a password later. The password is never logged and never returned in the API response.
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant C as Client
    participant G as Google
    participant S as AuthService
    participant O as GoogleOAuthService
    participant DB as Postgres
    participant M as EmailService
    C->>G: Sign in with Google button
    G-->>C: Google ID token
    C->>S: POST /v1/auth/google with idToken
    S->>O: verifyIdToken
    O->>G: check signature and audience
    O-->>S: googleId, email, first and last name
    S->>DB: BEGIN, find user by email
    alt new user
        S->>DB: insert verified user with random password
        S->>DB: create free subscription
    else unverified user
        S->>DB: claim row, new password, revoke refresh tokens
        S->>DB: create free subscription
    else verified user
        S->>DB: link Google ids if needed
    end
    S->>DB: COMMIT
    S->>DB: upsert refresh token row
    opt account created or claimed
        S-->>M: welcome email with username and password
    end
    S-->>C: 200 accessToken and refreshToken

docs.title: 5.4 Token refresh (rotation)
docs.text:
Each refresh token works once. Using it returns a new pair and kills the old token. This is called rotation.

  1. The client calls POST /v1/auth/refresh with { refreshToken }. The route is @Public().
  2. The server verifies the JWT with JWT_REFRESH_SECRET.
  3. It hashes the token with SHA-256 and looks for a live row with that user_id and token_hash. If there is no row, or expires_at has passed, it returns 401.
  4. It soft-deletes the row, signs a new pair, and stores the new hash. Storing the hash brings the same row back with the new hash and expiry.
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant C as Client
    participant S as AuthService
    participant DB as Postgres
    C->>S: POST /v1/auth/refresh with refreshToken
    S->>S: verify JWT with refresh secret
    S->>S: sha256 of the token
    S->>DB: find live row by user id and hash
    alt not found or expired
        S-->>C: 401 Invalid or expired refresh token
    else found
        S->>DB: soft delete row
        S->>S: sign new access and refresh tokens
        S->>DB: restore row with new hash and new expiry
        S-->>C: 200 new token pair
    end

docs.title: 5.5 Logout
docs.text:
1. The client calls POST /v1/auth/logout with { refreshToken }. The route is @Public(), so it works even when the access token has expired.
  2. The server hashes the token and soft-deletes any row with that hash.
  3. It always returns 200, even if it did not know the token.
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant C as Client
    participant S as AuthService
    participant DB as Postgres
    C->>S: POST /v1/auth/logout with refreshToken
    S->>S: sha256 of the token
    S->>DB: soft delete refresh_tokens where token_hash matches
    S-->>C: 200 Logged out successfully
    Note over C,S: The access token still works until it expires

docs.title: 5.6 Forgot and reset password
docs.text:
1. The client calls POST /v1/auth/forgot-password with { email }. The response is always the same message, so nobody can use this route to find out which emails have accounts.
  2. If the account exists and is active, the server emails a reset link. The link holds a JWT with { sub: userId }.
  3. The JWT is signed with JWT_PASSWORD_RESET_SECRET plus the user's current password hash. When the password changes, the key changes, so every older reset link stops working. This makes the link single-use without storing it anywhere.
  4. The client calls POST /v1/auth/reset-password with { token, password }. The server reads sub from the token, loads that user, and then verifies the token with that user's key. Every failure returns the same error: 401 Invalid or expired password reset token.
  5. In one transaction, the server saves the new password, clears mustChangePassword, and revokes all the user's refresh tokens.

docs.title: 5.7 How a request is authenticated
docs.text:
JwtAuthGuard (src/identity/auth/guards/jwt-auth.guard.ts) is the first global guard in src/app.module.ts. The full order is:

JwtAuthGuard → RateLimitGuard → RolesGuard → OrgContextGuard → PermissionGuard

Steps inside JwtAuthGuard:

  1. If the route or its controller has @Public(), let the request through.
  2. Read the Authorization: Bearer <token> header. If it is missing: 401 Missing access token.
  3. Verify the JWT with JWT_ACCESS_SECRET. If it is bad or expired: 401.
  4. Load the account status from the database with UsersService.findAccountStatusById. It selects only id, is_active and is_verified. This runs on every authenticated request. Then:
    • user deleted: 401 Account no longer exists
    • not active: 401 Account has been deactivated
    • not verified: 401 Please verify your email before continuing
  5. Set request.user = payload ({ sub, email, username }).

Controllers read the caller with @CurrentUser() user: JwtPayload. They usually use user.sub as the user id.

flowchart TD
    R["Incoming HTTP request"] --> P{"Route marked Public?"}
    P -- yes --> OK["Continue to next guard"]
    P -- no --> H{"Bearer token present?"}
    H -- no --> E1["401 Missing access token"]
    H -- yes --> V{"JWT valid?"}
    V -- no --> E2["401 Invalid or expired"]
    V -- yes --> D["Load is_active and is_verified from DB"]
    D --> S{"Account usable?"}
    S -- no --> E3["401 deleted, deactivated or unverified"]
    S -- yes --> U["Set request.user to the payload"] --> OK

RabbitMQ consumers are also marked @Public(). The global guard runs for them too, and they have no HTTP request to read a token from.

docs.title: 6. Business rules and edge cases
docs.text:
1. Password policy (IsStrongPassword in src/identity/auth/decorators/is-strong-password.decorator.ts): 8 to 255 characters, with at least one lowercase letter, one uppercase letter, one digit and one special character. Sign-up and reset use it. Login only checks that the password has at least 8 characters.
  2. Username: 3 to 100 characters, using only letters, digits and _. First and last names may use only letters, spaces, - and '.
  3. Login identifier: send email or username. If both are sent, email is used.
  4. Unverified accounts cannot call protected routes, even with a valid token.
  5. Verification email throttle: login sends a new link only after the previous link has expired.
  6. One refresh token per user. storeRefreshToken keeps exactly one refresh_tokens row per user and overwrites it on every login, sign-up, Google sign-in and refresh. So logging in on a second device makes the first device's refresh token stop working. This comes from how the code is written. No setting changes it.
  7. Logout only revokes the refresh token. There is no access token denylist. The access token keeps working until it expires. The exception is a deactivated or deleted account, because the guard checks those on every call.
  8. Resetting the password logs the user out everywhere (all refresh tokens are revoked). Claiming an unverified account through Google does the same.
  9. Google requires email_verified. If a verified TestFlow account has the same email, Google is linked to it automatically.
  10. Generated passwords (generateDefaultPassword in src/identity/helpers/default-password.helper.ts) use crypto.randomInt. They have at least one character from each class and leave out characters that look alike.
  11. The free subscription is created only when an account becomes verified (email link or Google), never at sign-up.
  12. Emails are fire-and-forget. A failed send is logged and does not fail the request.
  13. Email matching is case-sensitive in login, sign-up and Google sign-in (findByEmail compares with =). Only the org invite lookup lowercases emails.

docs.title: 7. Endpoints summary
docs.text: The API reference has the full details.

docs.title: Auth (/v1/auth, src/identity/auth/auth.controller.ts)
docs.text:
Method and path Auth Rate limit Purpose POST /login Public CLASS_A Password login POST /signup Public CLASS_A Create an account and send the verification email GET /verify-email?token= Public CLASS_A, own bucket Verify the email and create the free plan POST /forgot-password Public CLASS_A, own bucket Send the reset email POST /reset-password Public CLASS_A, own bucket Set a new password with a reset token GET /check-username?username= Public CLASS_A, own bucket Returns { exists } POST /google Public CLASS_A Google sign-in with an ID token POST /refresh Public CLASS_A Rotate the token pair POST /logout Public CLASS_A Revoke the refresh token GET /me Bearer CLASS_C Profile, current plan, allowed question types and enabled feature flags

GET /me makes four reads at the same time: the profile (UsersService.getMe), the current plan and the allowed question types (SubscriptionsService), and the enabled feature flags (FeatureFlagsService). If the feature flag read fails, it uses the defaults from code instead of failing.

docs.title: Admin users (/v1/admin, src/identity/users/admin.controller.ts)
docs.text:
All of these use the CLASS_C rate limit and need a platform permission (see RBAC).

Method and path Permission Purpose GET /users users:read Cursor-paged list, newest first. Filters: search (name, username, email), role, isActive, isVerified. Each user includes their platform role keys. meta has nextCursor and total. GET /users/:username/roles users:read A user's platform roles POST /users/:username/roles users:create Add a platform role. Body: { roleKey }. DELETE /users/:username/roles/:roleKey users:delete Remove a platform role (soft delete)

Admin rules (src/identity/users/admin.service.ts):

  • You cannot change your own roles (403).
  • You can only add roles with scope platform here. Org roles come from org membership (400).
  • Adding a role the user already has returns 409.

docs.title: 8. Async work, emails and events
docs.text:
This module uses no queues and no websocket events. It sends these emails through EmailService (see Notifications):

Email When Verification On sign-up, and on login when the last link has expired Welcome After email verification. After a Google sign-up or claim, it also includes the username and generated password. Password reset On POST /forgot-password for an active account

docs.title: 9. Bootstrapping the first admin
docs.text:
npm run bootstrap-admin -- --email <email> --password <password> runs src/scripts/bootstrap-admin.ts:

  1. The super_admin role must already exist, so run npm run seed first.
  2. If any user already has super_admin, the script stops. It prints "already bootstrapped" if that user has the same email, and fails otherwise. This script can only create one super admin. You can add more later with POST /v1/admin/users/:username/roles.
  3. In one transaction, it creates a verified, active user with username system and the given email and password, and gives that user super_admin.

The script does not check the password policy and does not create a subscription.

docs.text: Path What src/identity/auth/auth.controller.ts Auth routes src/identity/auth/auth.service.ts All auth flows, plus token signing and storage src/identity/auth/google/google-oauth.service.ts Google ID token check src/identity/auth/guards/jwt-auth.guard.ts Global auth guard and JwtPayload src/identity/auth/decorators/ @CurrentUser(), @IsStrongPassword() src/common/decorators/public.decorator.ts @Public() src/identity/helpers/ Generated passwords and the placeholder username prefix src/identity/users/users.service.ts User reads and writes used by auth and organizations src/identity/users/admin.controller.ts, admin.service.ts Admin user and role routes src/scripts/bootstrap-admin.ts Creates the first super admin tests/unit/identity/ Unit tests (auth/, users/, helpers/)

docs.title: 11. Known gaps and TODOs
docs.text:
1. The expiry values in .env.example do not work. It has JWT_ACCESS_EXPIRY=15m and JWT_REFRESH_EXPIRY=7d, but the code does +value, which turns 15m into NaN. Use seconds instead, for example 900 and 604800.
  2. There is no endpoint for users to update their profile or change their password. UsersService.update and remove exist, but no controller calls them. A user with mustChangePassword can only change the password through the reset flow.
  3. The API cannot deactivate or delete a user. is_active is checked everywhere, but nothing sets it to false.
  4. Only one refresh token per user (rule 6), so a user cannot stay signed in on several devices.
  5. POST /refresh does not check is_active or is_verified. The guard still rejects the new access token, so the risk is low.
  6. The guard reads the database on every request. Nothing is cached.
  7. request.user.email and request.user.username come from the token. They can be out of date until the token expires.
  8. Sign-up can take over an unverified row with the same email and replace its password. The real owner still has to click the verification link. If they do click it, the password the other person chose stays on the account.
  9. OAuthProvider.GITHUB is in the enum, but there is no GitHub sign-in.
  10. Emails are case-sensitive (rule 13), so A@x.com and a@x.com can be two accounts. The unique index is on the raw value.

docs.title: 1. Purpose
docs.text:
TestFlow never runs user code on the backend host. The code-execution module sends code to an external sandbox and turns the reply into one common result shape.

It sits behind one small interface, CodeRunner, so the rest of the app does not care which sandbox is used. Switching sandbox is a config change (CODE_RUNNER_PROVIDER), not a code change.

The code lives in src/code-execution/.

docs.title: 2. Key concepts
docs.text: Term Meaning CodeRunner The interface every provider implements: provider, supports(language), run(request). CodeRunnerFactory An abstract factory. There is one per provider. It builds a runner from config. CODE_RUNNER The Nest injection token bound to the chosen runner. Callers inject this. Provider The sandbox behind a runner: online-compiler (OnlineCompiler.io, hosted) or piston (self-hosted Piston). Run result How a program ended: success, error, time_limit_exceeded or memory_limit_exceeded. A program that crashes is a result, not an exception. CodeRunnerError Thrown when the run could not happen. The reason is one of not_configured, unsupported_language, busy, unavailable. Judge judgeTestCase compares one run with one test case's expected output.

docs.title: 3. Architecture
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    CR["CodeRunService - live runs over WebSocket"] --> TOKEN
    CE["CodingEvaluator - grading"] --> TOKEN
    GEN["AI coding question generation"] --> TOKEN
    TOKEN["CODE_RUNNER token"] --> RUNNER{"Runner chosen at boot"}
    RUNNER -->|"online-compiler - default"| OC["OnlineCompilerRunner"]
    RUNNER -->|"piston"| PI["PistonRunner"]
    OC -->|"HTTPS POST /api/run-code-sync/"| OCAPI["OnlineCompiler.io"]
    PI -->|"HTTP POST /api/v2/execute"| PAPI["Self-hosted Piston"]
    CR --> JUDGE["judgeTestCase and sameOutput"]
    CE --> JUDGE

How the runner is chosen (code-execution.module.ts):

  1. Both factories (OnlineCompilerRunnerFactory, PistonRunnerFactory) are registered under CODE_RUNNER_FACTORIES.
  2. At boot, CODE_RUNNER is built by selectCodeRunnerFactory(factories, CODE_RUNNER_PROVIDER). An empty value falls back to online-compiler.
  3. An unknown provider name fails the boot with a clear error, so the problem is not found on the first run.
  4. A missing API key does not stop the boot. That runner then refuses every run with not_configured.
  5. The chosen provider is logged: Code runner: <provider>.

To add a provider, write a new CodeRunner and a CodeRunnerFactory, and add the factory to the module's list.

docs.title: 4. Request and response shapes
docs.text:
CodeRunRequest (interfaces/code-runner.interface.ts):

Field Type Notes language python, java or cpp CODING_LANGUAGES in src/ai/interfaces/generated-coding-question.interface.ts code string The full source file stdin string The input fed to the program timeLimitMs number The question's CPU-time limit memoryLimitMb number The question's memory limit

CodeRunResult:

Field Notes status success (exit 0 within limits), error (compile or runtime error, non-zero exit), time_limit_exceeded, memory_limit_exceeded stdout, stderr Program output. When the program left no stderr, stderr is filled with a reason from the provider. exitCode Null if not reported timeMs CPU time of the program, without compilation. Null if not reported. memoryKb Null if not reported outputTruncated True when the provider cut stdout. Truncated output can never pass a test case.

docs.title: 5. Supported languages
docs.text:
Our language OnlineCompiler.io compiler Piston runtime python python-3.14 python 3.12.0 java openjdk-25 java 15.0.2 cpp g++-15 c++ 10.2.0

The Piston versions must match the packages installed on the Piston server (piston.constants.ts). JavaScript is not supported. A coding question may only offer languages from CODING_LANGUAGES. A live run is also refused if the active runner does not supports() the language.

docs.title: 6.1 OnlineCompiler.io (runners/online-compiler/)
docs.text:
• Calls POST {ONLINE_COMPILER_BASE_URL}/api/run-code-sync/ with header Authorization: <api key> and body { compiler, code, input }.
  • Concurrency: an in-process Semaphore allows ONLINE_COMPILER_MAX_CONCURRENCY calls at once (default 4, which is the API's per-key limit). Extra calls wait in order.
  • 429 is retried once after 1 second. A second 429 gives busy.
  • 401 or 403 gives not_configured (bad key). Any other non-2xx, a network error or a timeout gives unavailable.
  • Request timeout: ONLINE_COMPILER_TIMEOUT_MS (default 40 s). The sandbox itself stops a program at 30 s.
  • Payload cap: code and stdin are each at most 100 KB (unavailable if larger).
  • Status mapping: a non-zero exit code maps through ONLINE_COMPILER_EXIT_CODES: 124 is a timeout, 137 is out of memory (the sandbox allows 512 MB), and others are error. The sandbox limits are much higher than a question's, so after a clean exit the runner compares the reported time and memory against the question's limits. Over a limit means TLE or MLE even though the program finished.
  • Output limit: the API cuts output at 999 characters, so outputTruncated is set when stdout.length >= 999.

docs.title: 6.2 Piston (runners/piston/)
docs.text:
• Calls POST {PISTON_BASE_URL}/api/v2/execute with header x-api-key: sha256hex(PISTON_API_KEY). Only the digest is sent, never the raw key.
  • The body has the runtime, files: [{ content: code }], stdin and per-run limits:
    • run_cpu_time = timeLimitMs
    • run_timeout = 2 x timeLimitMs (wall clock, to allow for I/O and start-up)
    • run_memory_limit = memoryLimitMb in bytes
    • each limit is clamped to PISTON_MAX_RUN_TIMEOUT_MS, PISTON_MAX_RUN_CPU_TIME_MS and PISTON_MAX_RUN_MEMORY_MB when set, because Piston answers 400 to anything above its own maximums
  • Concurrency: a Semaphore of PISTON_MAX_CONCURRENCY (default 4). Keep it at or below Piston's PISTON_MAX_CONCURRENT_JOBS divided by the number of backend instances. The request timeout (PISTON_TIMEOUT_MS, default 60 s) starts only once a slot is taken.
  • Compile failure (no run stage) gives error with the compiler's stderr.
  • Status mapping: Piston TO is TLE. OL (output too long) is success with outputTruncated, which the judge treats as a wrong answer. A SIGKILL with memory at 95% or more of the enforced limit is MLE. A non-zero code or another signal is error. Otherwise the reported CPU time and memory are checked against the question's limits.
  • Piston status XX (internal error) or any non-2xx gives unavailable. 401 gives not_configured.

docs.title: 7. Test-case execution and judging
docs.text:
Test cases always run one after another, never in parallel for one submission. The shared semaphore still lets runs from different users overlap.

judgeTestCase(result, expectedOutput) in judge-test-case.ts:

Run status Outcome time_limit_exceeded time_limit_exceeded memory_limit_exceeded memory_limit_exceeded error runtime_error (compile errors land here too) success, output truncated wrong_answer success, output matches passed success, output differs wrong_answer

"Matches" means sameOutput (output-compare.ts): both sides are normalised to LF line endings, trailing spaces on each line are removed, and trailing blank lines are removed. Then they must be exactly equal. This is the exact checker.

How each feature uses it:

Feature Which cases What happens with results Live code run during an attempt visible cases (samples) or one custom stdin (custom) Streamed to the socket. Nothing saved. See attempts. Coding evaluation all cases, hidden included Partial marks and verdict saved on the response. See evaluation. AI coding question generation reference solution on generated inputs Its output becomes the expected output, and generated cases are checked. See assessment generation. The runner is injected @Optional() there.

docs.title: 8. Timeouts, limits and error handling
docs.text:
Limit Value Where Code or stdin size, live run 50,000 characters RunCodeDto (CODE_RUN_MAX_LENGTH) Code or stdin size, OnlineCompiler 100 KB each ONLINE_COMPILER_MAX_PAYLOAD_BYTES Live runs per user 1 in flight, 1 start every 5 s CodeRunService (in memory, per instance) Concurrent provider calls 4 per instance by default *_MAX_CONCURRENCY HTTP timeout 40 s (OnlineCompiler), 60 s (Piston) *_TIMEOUT_MS Program CPU time and memory the question's timeLimitMs and memoryLimitMb from the coding question

How errors flow:

  • A program failure (wrong output, crash, TLE, MLE) is a normal result. The user gets a verdict.
  • A CodeRunnerError means the run did not happen:
    • live run: the socket gets code.run.failed with reason and message. Results already sent still stand.
    • evaluation: the response and its child job are marked failed, and a retry grades them later. It is never scored as wrong.
  • Any other exception in a live run gives code.run.failed with reason: "internal_error".

docs.title: 9. Security notes
docs.text:
1. No local execution. User code is only sent over HTTP to a sandbox. The backend never runs it.
  2. Hidden test cases stay private. Live runs only use visible cases. Graded results shown to the candidate never include a hidden case's input, expected output, stdout or stderr. Reviewers see them.
  3. Secrets: the Piston key is sent as a SHA-256 digest. The OnlineCompiler key is sent as is in Authorization over HTTPS. Both come from env (.env.example).
  4. Third-party exposure: with online-compiler, candidate code and test inputs (hidden ones included, during grading) are sent to OnlineCompiler.io. Use piston to keep them in-house.
  5. Abuse limits: these are the DTO size caps, the per-user cooldown and in-flight limit, and the semaphores. The cooldown is per process, so with N instances a user could run up to N times as often.
  6. Sandbox limits (processes, output size, memory) are enforced by the provider, not by TestFlow.

docs.title: 10. Configuration
docs.text:
Env var Default Used by CODE_RUNNER_PROVIDER online-compiler module (online-compiler or piston) ONLINE_COMPILER_API_KEY none (runs refused) OnlineCompiler ONLINE_COMPILER_BASE_URL https://api.onlinecompiler.io OnlineCompiler ONLINE_COMPILER_MAX_CONCURRENCY 4 OnlineCompiler ONLINE_COMPILER_TIMEOUT_MS 40000 OnlineCompiler PISTON_API_KEY none (runs refused) Piston, the same raw secret as the Piston server's PISTON_BASE_URL http://127.0.0.1:2000 Piston PISTON_MAX_CONCURRENCY 4 Piston PISTON_TIMEOUT_MS 60000 Piston PISTON_MAX_RUN_TIMEOUT_MS, PISTON_MAX_RUN_CPU_TIME_MS, PISTON_MAX_RUN_MEMORY_MB unset (no clamp). .env.example uses 2000 / 2000 / 256 Piston

Values that are not positive integers fall back to the default. See getting started.

docs.title: 11. Where the code lives
docs.text: Path What src/code-execution/code-execution.module.ts Provider selection, exports CODE_RUNNER src/code-execution/code-execution.constants.ts Tokens, provider enum, default src/code-execution/code-runner.factory.ts Abstract factory src/code-execution/interfaces/code-runner.interface.ts CodeRunner, request and result types src/code-execution/code-runner.errors.ts CodeRunnerError and reasons src/code-execution/judge-test-case.ts, output-compare.ts Judging and output normalising src/code-execution/semaphore.ts FIFO concurrency limiter src/code-execution/runners/online-compiler/ OnlineCompiler.io runner, factory, constants src/code-execution/runners/piston/ Piston runner, factory, constants Consumers: src/assessments/attempts/code-run/code-run.service.ts, src/assessments/evaluation/evaluators/coding.evaluator.ts, src/ai/llm/coding-question-generation.graph.ts, src/ai/llm/coding-problem-tool-writer.ts Features that run code

docs.title: 12. Known gaps and TODOs found in code
docs.text:
1. Off-by-one truncation on OnlineCompiler. outputTruncated is stdout.length >= 999 (online-compiler.runner.ts:128). A correct answer that is exactly 999 characters long is treated as truncated and judged wrong_answer.
  2. checkerType is unused. Questions store it, but judging is always exact (judge-test-case.ts:19). There is no float tolerance or custom checker.
  3. Limits are per process. The semaphores and the live-run cooldown do not coordinate across instances. The provider's real concurrency limit is shared, which is why OnlineCompiler retries a 429 once.
  4. Compile errors are reported as runtime_error, because both providers' results are folded into error before judging. There is a compilation_error code verdict, but it is never produced.
  5. Language versions differ between providers (for example Java 25 against 15), so the same code may behave differently after switching provider.

docs.title: 1. What this page covers
docs.text:
"Commerce" is everything to do with money and limits:

  • Plans: what we sell (price, billing cycle, and what you get).
  • Subscriptions: which plan a user or an organization is on right now.
  • Payments: taking money through Razorpay (an Indian payment gateway) and confirming it with a webhook (a server-to-server HTTP call Razorpay makes to us).
  • Usage: counting how much of a limited feature (for example, AI assessment generations) someone has used, and refusing when they run out.
  • Credits: one-time packs of extra usage, spent once a plan's own quota runs out (section 7).
  • Orders: a user's own purchase history (section 8).
  • Admin: endpoints that platform admins use to manage the plan catalog and credit packs, and to look at orders, payments, subscriptions, and usage.

The code is split into three NestJS modules:

Module Folder Owns CommerceModule src/commerce/ Plans, subscriptions, usage, credit packs (src/commerce/credits/), admin endpoints. Exports UsageService, SubscriptionsService and CreditsService to other modules. PaymentsModule src/commerce/payments/ Orders (including GET /v1/orders), payments, the Razorpay client. Imports CommerceModule, because a captured credit payment is granted by CreditsService. Exports PaymentsService and RazorpayService. WebhooksModule src/webhooks/ The public POST /webhooks/razorpay endpoint. Imports PaymentsModule. 
flowchart LR
    auth["Identity / Auth"] -->|"createFreeSubscription"| commerce
    orgs["Organizations"] -->|"createOrgTrialSubscription"| commerce
    assess["Assessment generation"] -->|"consume / release / getFeatureValue"| commerce
    roadmaps["Learning roadmaps"] -->|"consume"| commerce
    ai["AI model selector"] -->|"getFeatureValue"| commerce
    commerce["CommerceModule"]
    webhooks["WebhooksModule"] --> payments["PaymentsModule"]
    payments -.->|"writes Subscription rows directly"| commerce

The dotted arrow is a shortcut: PaymentsService imports the Subscription entity and updates it itself, instead of calling SubscriptionsService. There is a TODO about this in src/commerce/payments/payments.service.ts.

docs.title: 2. Key terms
docs.text: Term Meaning Feature A thing a plan can grant, identified by a fixed FeatureKey (table features). Plan A product we sell, e.g. FREE or PRO (table plans). Has a public code. Plan version One price point of a plan: price, currency, billing cycle (table plan_versions). Plan feature One feature attached to one plan version, with its value and reset period. Entity PlanVersionFeature, but the table is plan_features. Subscription A user's or an organization's link to one plan version, with a status and dates. Order "We expect this much money for this thing." Created at checkout, for a subscription or a credit pack. Payment One attempt to pay an order through a provider (Razorpay). An order can have several payments. Usage row A counter in user_feature_usage: how much of one plan feature was used in the current period. Credit pack A one-time purchase of extra usage of one feature, e.g. "10 AI assessments" (table credit_packs). Credit balance What a user bought and has spent of one feature's credits, per AI model (table user_feature_credits). Never resets or expires. Audience Who can buy a plan: individual (for yourself) or organization.

docs.title: 3.1 How pricing and limits are modelled
docs.text:
erDiagram
    plans ||--o{ plan_versions : "has"
    plan_versions ||--o{ plan_features : "grants"
    features ||--o{ plan_features : "is used in"
    plan_versions ||--o{ subscriptions : "subscribed by"
    plan_features ||--o{ user_feature_usage : "counted in"
  • plans (src/common/entities/plan.entity.ts): name, unique code, description, audience, is_active, is_displayed, sort_order.
    • is_active = false means it cannot be bought.
    • is_displayed = false hides it from the public list, but existing subscribers keep it.
    • sort_order sets the order of the public list (lowest first, then id).
  • plan_versions (plan-version.entity.ts): version number, price (decimal 10,2), currency (3 letters), billing_cycle (MONTHLY, YEARLY, ONE_TIME), is_current, effective_from, effective_until, expiry_days.
    • expiry_days only applies to ONE_TIME versions. null means "never expires". The admin API refuses a value on a recurring version (400).
  • plan_features (plan-version-feature.entity.ts): feature_id, display_name, feature_value (a string), type, reset_period (days, or null). A partial unique index allows one non-deleted row per (version, feature).
  • features (feature.entity.ts): one row per FeatureKey. Seeded, not created through the API.

docs.title: 3.2 Feature types
docs.text:
A plan feature has a type (PlanFeatureType in src/common/enums/commerce.enums.ts) that says how to read feature_value:

Type feature_value means Counted? limit A quota. A number like "2" is the limit. A non-number like "unlimited" means no limit. Yes, by UsageService.consume enum A setting, e.g. a model code or a list of question types. No. consume refuses an enum feature.

docs.title: 3.3 The feature keys today
docs.text:
FeatureKey Type in practice Used by Effect AI_ASSESSMENT limit Assessment generation How many AI assessment generations per period. AI_LEARNING_ROADMAP limit Learning roadmaps How many AI roadmaps per period. AI_MODEL enum src/ai/ai-model-selector.service.ts Which LLM model the user's AI calls use. Missing means the default model. ALLOWED_QUESTION_TYPES enum src/assessments/generation/generation-entitlement.service.ts Comma-separated question types, e.g. mcq,coding. Missing or empty means mcq only (src/commerce/plans/allowed-question-types.ts). AI_ASSESSMENT_SUGGESTION enum src/assessments/attempts/attempt-suggestion.service.ts On/off. Any non-blank value (e.g. enabled) lets the plan's users ask for a next-assessment suggestion after an evaluated attempt. Missing or blank means 403. Personal plan only. Added by migration 20261030000000, attached to no plan by default.

"Number of participants" and "number of assessments" are not metered features. Participant caps live on the assessment itself (see Assessments).

docs.title: 3.4 Why versions exist
docs.text:
Prices change, but people who already paid should keep what they bought. So instead of changing a plan's price in place, an admin adds a new version:

  1. The old current version gets is_current = false, and effective_until is set (if it was empty) to the new version's effective_from.
  2. The new version is inserted with version = old + 1 and is_current = true.

Both steps run in one transaction (CommerceAdminService.createPlanVersion in src/commerce/admin.service.ts). A partial unique index (UQ_plan_versions_plan_id_current, WHERE is_current = true) makes sure a plan has at most one current version.

Existing subscriptions point at a plan_version_id, so they keep their old version's price and features.

Checkout asks for both planCode and version. So a client can buy an older version, as long as its effective_until has not passed.

docs.title: 3.5 Built-in plans and seeding
docs.text:
Two plans are special. Code finds them by name, so they must exist and be active (src/commerce/plans/plan.constants.ts):

Name Code (seeded) Audience Cycle Price Seeded feature Who gets it FREE FREEPLAN individual MONTHLY 0 USD AI_ASSESSMENT = 2, reset every 1 day Every user, when their account is verified ORG_TRIAL ORGTRIAL organization ONE_TIME, 7 days 0 USD AI_ASSESSMENT = 2, reset every 1 day Every new organization
  • npm run seed runs src/seeders/feature.seeder.ts (creates the five features) and then src/seeders/plan.seeder.ts (creates each plan only if no plan with that name exists yet).
  • Because code looks these plans up by name, admins cannot rename or deactivate FREE or ORG_TRIAL (CommerceAdminService.updatePlan returns 409). Hiding, re-describing or re-ordering them is fine.
  • Paid plans (for example PRO) are not seeded. Admins create them through the admin API (section 9).
  • Admin-created plans get a random 10-character code from an alphabet without look-alike characters (no I, O, 0, 1).

docs.title: 4.1 Personal vs organization subscriptions
docs.text:
Both exist, in the same subscriptions table:

Personal Organization organization_id NULL the org's id user_id the owner the purchaser (the org creator for the trial) How it starts FREE at verification, or a paid plan through checkout ORG_TRIAL when the org is created Can be bought? Yes, individual plans via POST /v1/subscriptions/checkout No. There is no org checkout endpoint yet, and checkout refuses organization plans with 422. Usage Counted per user Pooled: one counter per organization and feature, shared by all members

Which subscription applies depends on the x-organization-id request header (see Organizations). With the header, the org's plan is used, and the member's personal plan is never used as a fallback. Without it, the user's personal plan is used.

docs.title: 4.2 How a subscription is created
docs.text:
Trigger Code Result Email verification, new Google sign-in, or claiming an unverified account src/identity/auth/auth.service.ts calls SubscriptionsService.createFreeSubscription FREE current version, ACTIVE, expires_at = start + 1 month A personal user with no active subscription spends usage UsageService.consume calls createFreeSubscription Same as above, created lazily inside the usage transaction Organization created src/organizations/services/organizations.service.ts calls createOrgTrialSubscription ORG_TRIAL, ACTIVE, 7 days (or the version's expiry_days), auto_renew = false User buys a plan SubscriptionsService.checkout PENDING subscription plus a PENDING order. Becomes ACTIVE after payment.

expires_at comes from computeExpiry in src/commerce/subscriptions/subscriptions.service.ts: +1 month for MONTHLY, +1 year for YEARLY, +expiry_days for ONE_TIME (or null when it has no expiry_days).

docs.title: 4.3 Lifecycle
docs.text:
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> PENDING : checkout
    [*] --> ACTIVE : free plan or org trial
    PENDING --> ACTIVE : payment.captured webhook
    ACTIVE --> SUSPENDED : user pays for another personal plan
    note right of SUSPENDED
        PAST_DUE, CANCELLED and EXPIRED
        exist in the enum but no code
        sets them today
    end note

What the code really does today:

  • Upgrade or switch plan: the user checks out a different personal plan. When that payment is captured, every other ACTIVE personal subscription of that user (including FREE) is set to SUSPENDED, and the new one becomes ACTIVE. There is no proration and no refund of the old plan.
  • Downgrade: works the same way. Buying a cheaper plan suspends the more expensive one.
  • Cancel: no endpoint. cancelled_at is never written.
  • Expiry: there is no scheduler or job that expires subscriptions (src/schedulers/ only has the newsletter scheduler). Every "which plan is this user on" query checks status = ACTIVE only and ignores expires_at. So an ACTIVE subscription keeps working after expires_at, including the 7-day org trial.
  • Renewal: auto_renew is stored (true for recurring, false for ONE_TIME and the trial), but nothing reads it. There is no recurring billing.
  • A PENDING subscription whose order expired or failed stays PENDING forever. Nothing cleans it up. To try again, the user checks out again, which makes a new subscription and order.

docs.title: 5.1 Why two steps
docs.text:
Checkout (POST /v1/subscriptions/checkout, or POST /v1/credits/checkout for a credit pack) does not call Razorpay. It only saves our own records: a PENDING order, plus a PENDING subscription for a plan. The Razorpay order is created by a second call, POST /v1/payments/razorpay/create, which works the same for both kinds of order.

This keeps "what is being bought" separate from "which payment provider is used". The order can be checked (owner, status, expiry) before any money is involved, and the provider step can be retried safely.

The order gets a placeholder provider_order_id of chk_<uuid> to fill its unique column. The real Razorpay order id is stored on the payment row, not on the order.

docs.title: 5.2 The full flow
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant C as Client app
    participant S as SubscriptionsController
    participant P as PaymentsController
    participant R as Razorpay
    participant W as WebhooksController
    participant DB as Postgres

    C->>S: POST /v1/subscriptions/checkout with planCode and version
    S->>DB: check plan, version, no ACTIVE sub for this plan
    S->>DB: insert Subscription PENDING and Order PENDING, 30 min expiry
    S-->>C: subscription and order
    C->>P: POST /v1/payments/razorpay/create with orderId
    P->>DB: check owner, status PENDING, not expired, latest payment
    P->>R: orders.create with amount x 100, currency, receipt
    R-->>P: razorpay order id
    P->>DB: insert Payment PENDING with providerOrderId
    P-->>C: razorpayOrderId and razorpayKeyId
    C->>R: open Razorpay Checkout widget and pay
    R->>W: POST /webhooks/razorpay with x-razorpay-signature
    W->>W: verify HMAC of raw body with RAZORPAY_WEBHOOK_SECRET
    W->>DB: look up webhook_events by eventId
    W->>DB: one transaction - Payment SUCCESS, Order PAID, old subs SUSPENDED, new sub ACTIVE, Order FULFILLED
    W->>DB: save webhook_events row, processed true
    W-->>R: 200 OK

Step by step:

  1. Checkout (SubscriptionsService.checkout, one transaction). It checks, in order:

    • plan exists by code, else 404
    • plan is_active, else 422
    • plan audience is individual, else 422 ("can only be bought for an organization")
    • the requested version exists, else 404
    • effective_until has not passed, else 422
    • the user has no ACTIVE personal subscription to this same plan, else 409

    Then it saves the subscription (PENDING) and the order (PENDING, amount = version price, expires after CHECKOUT_ORDER_TTL_MINUTES, default 30). 2. Create the Razorpay payment (PaymentsService.createRazorpayPayment). It checks the order exists (404), belongs to the caller (403), is PENDING (422), and has not expired (422). Then it looks at the latest payment for the order: - SUCCESS: 409 "already been paid". - PENDING with a Razorpay order id: the same payment is returned again. This makes the call safe to retry and avoids duplicate Razorpay orders. - none, or FAILED: a new Razorpay order and a new PENDING payment are created. In practice a failed payment has usually failed its order too (5.3), so the order check above has already returned 422, and the client starts a new checkout instead.

    The amount sent to Razorpay is Math.round(amount * 100) (rupees to paise). If the Razorpay call fails, the API returns 503. 3. Client checkout. The client opens the Razorpay widget with razorpayOrderId and razorpayKeyId (the public key id, never the secret). The backend has no "verify payment signature" endpoint for the client. The webhook is the only source of truth. 4. Webhook (WebhooksService.handleRazorpayWebhook in src/webhooks/webhooks.service.ts), see 5.3.

docs.title: 5.3 Webhook handling
docs.text:
POST /webhooks/razorpay is marked @Public() (Razorpay has no user token) and hidden from Swagger.

Signature check. Razorpay signs the exact bytes it sends. If we parsed the JSON and serialized it again, the bytes could change and the check would fail. So:

  • src/main.ts creates the app with { rawBody: true }, which keeps the original body on req.rawBody.
  • The controller passes req.rawBody (as a UTF-8 string) and the x-razorpay-signature header to the service.
  • RazorpayService.verifyWebhookSignature calls Razorpay.validateWebhookSignature with RAZORPAY_WEBHOOK_SECRET.
  • Missing or wrong signature: 401. This happens before any parsing or database work.

Event filtering. Only payment.captured and payment.failed are handled. Other events are logged and get 200. A body with no payment entity is also logged and ignored.

Dedup with webhook_events. Razorpay can send the same event more than once. We build our own key: eventId = "<event>:<razorpay payment id>", for example payment.captured:pay_ABC123. The column has a unique index (UQ_webhook_events_event_id).

  • If a row with that key exists and processed = true, the webhook does nothing.
  • Otherwise the payment is processed, and then a row is saved with provider = RAZORPAY, the event type, the full JSON payload, processed = true, and processed_at.
  • The row is written after processing, and only on success. If processing throws, nothing is stored, we return an error, and Razorpay retries later.

payment.captured (PaymentsService.markPaymentCaptured, one transaction):

  1. Find the payment by Razorpay order id. Not found: log and stop.
  2. Already SUCCESS: stop. This is a second layer of idempotency.
  3. Set the payment to SUCCESS, and store the Razorpay payment id and paid_at.
  4. Set the order to PAID. It does not check the order's status first, so a capture also wins over an order that was marked FAILED (a retry inside the same Razorpay window).
  5. Fulfil the order, by resource_type:
    • SUBSCRIPTION: suspend the user's other ACTIVE personal subscriptions, set this one to ACTIVE, and set the order to FULFILLED.
    • CREDIT: CreditsService.grant adds the pack's credits to the user's balance and sets the order to FULFILLED (section 7.3).

payment.failed (PaymentsService.markPaymentFailed, one transaction): set the payment to FAILED with Razorpay's error_description, and set the order to FAILED if it is still PENDING. A subscription stays PENDING (see 4.3). Each checkout opens a new order, so a failed order is never paid again through POST /v1/payments/razorpay/create. A later payment.failed never changes a payment that is already FAILED or SUCCESS, so a late failure cannot undo a capture.

docs.title: 5.4 Status values
docs.text: Entity Values Set by code today Order PENDING, PAID, FAILED, FULFILLED All four. PAID moves on to FULFILLED in the same transaction, except for a credit order with no credit metadata. Payment PENDING, SUCCESS, FAILED, REFUNDED PENDING, SUCCESS, FAILED Subscription PENDING, ACTIVE, PAST_DUE, CANCELLED, EXPIRED, SUSPENDED PENDING, ACTIVE, SUSPENDED Order resource type SUBSCRIPTION, CREDIT Both. CREDIT was called AI_CREDITS until migration 20261027000002. Payment provider RAZORPAY, STRIPE Only RAZORPAY

docs.title: 5.5 Refunds
docs.text: There is no refund handling: no endpoint, no refund.* webhook handling, and REFUNDED is never set. Refunds must be done by hand in the Razorpay dashboard, and the database will not show them.

docs.title: 6.1 The three methods
docs.text:
All in src/commerce/usage/usage.service.ts:

Method What it does consume(userId, featureKey, amount = 1, orgId = null) Checks the limit and adds to the counter, in one transaction with a row lock. When the plan's quota runs out, spends purchased credits for the rest (section 7.4). Throws if neither covers it. Returns how the charge was split (fromPlan, fromCredits) and which credit balance it used. release(userId, featureKey, amount, orgId, chargedAt, manager?, credits?) Gives usage back when the work it paid for failed. credits says how much of it came from credits and from which balance; that part goes back to the balance, the rest to the plan counter. Never goes below 0. The plan part does nothing if the period has reset since chargedAt. Pass manager to run inside the caller's transaction. getFeatureValue(userId, featureKey, orgId = null) Reads a feature's value from the active plan without counting anything. Used for enum features. Never creates a free subscription.

docs.title: 6.2 How consume works
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant Caller as Calling service
    participant U as UsageService
    participant DB as Postgres

    Caller->>U: consume userId, featureKey, 1, orgId
    U->>DB: find Feature by key
    U->>DB: BEGIN, find ACTIVE subscriptions for user or org
    alt no personal subscription
        U->>DB: create FREE subscription
    else no org subscription
        U-->>Caller: 422 organization has no active plan
    end
    U->>DB: find the plan feature for these plan versions
    U->>DB: SELECT usage row FOR UPDATE
    U->>U: create the row, or reset it if periodEnd has passed
    alt used + amount is within the limit
        U->>DB: add amount to used, COMMIT
        U-->>Caller: used, limit, remaining, period
    else personal, and a credit balance covers the rest
        U->>DB: add what the plan covers to used, spend the rest from credits, COMMIT
        U-->>Caller: fromPlan, fromCredits, credit balance used
    else no credits cover it
        U-->>Caller: 422 Usage limit exceeded
    end

Details:

  • Reset period. reset_period is a number of days. When a new period starts, period_start = today and period_end = today + reset_period (UTC dates). If reset_period is null, period_end is 9999-12-31, so it never resets.
  • Resets are lazy. The next consume that sees period_end <= now sets used = 0 and starts a new period. There is no reset job.
  • The counter belongs to the plan feature row. When a user moves to a new plan or version, they start a new counter for the new plan feature.
  • Org pooling. For an org, the usage row has organization_id set and user_id = the org subscription's purchaser. All members share it.

docs.text:

Releases it if the transaction fails. Retry a failed generation same file, retry AI_ASSESSMENT Consumes 1 again. Releases it if requeueing fails. Generation ends with failed sections src/assessments/generation/generation-aggregator.service.ts fail AI_ASSESSMENT Releases the charge once (tracked by the usage.refunded flag in the job payload). Question type check src/assessments/generation/generation-entitlement.service.ts ALLOWED_QUESTION_TYPES (read) Not counted. Returns 403 naming the types the plan does not allow. No release on failure. Create a learning roadmap src/learning-roadmaps/learning-roadmaps.service.ts create AI_LEARNING_ROADMAP (personal only) Consumes 1. No release. Pick the LLM src/ai/ai-model-selector.service.ts AI_MODEL (read, personal only) Not counted. Next-assessment suggestion src/assessments/attempts/attempt-suggestion.service.ts suggestNext AI_ASSESSMENT_SUGGESTION and ALLOWED_QUESTION_TYPES (read, personal only) Not counted. 403 without the feature. Starting the suggested assessment is a normal generation and spends AI_ASSESSMENT. docs.title: 6.4 What happens when a limit is hit
docs.text: Situation HTTP status Message Limit reached, and no credit balance has enough left 422 Usage limit exceeded for feature AI_ASSESSMENT: 2/2 used Org request, org has no ACTIVE subscription 422 This organization has no active plan Feature is enum, not limit 422 Feature X is not a usage-limited feature Active plan does not include the feature, and (personally) no credits cover it 404 Feature X is not included in the user's active plan Feature key missing from the features table 404 Feature X not found Plan does not allow a question type 403 Your plan does not include ... questions; it allows: ...

docs.title: 7.1 What credits are
docs.text:
A credit pack is a one-time purchase of extra usage of one feature, for example "10 AI assessments for ₹199". Buying it adds to the user's credit balance for that feature. Credits:

  • work on top of any plan, including FREE and a plan that does not include the feature at all;
  • are spent only after the plan's own quota for the period runs out;
  • never reset and never expire;
  • are personal only for now. user_feature_credits.organization_id exists so organizations can be added later without a schema change, but nothing sells or spends org credits.

Credits are not modelled as a ONE_TIME plan, for two reasons. A paid subscription suspends the user's other personal subscriptions, and plan quotas reset every period. So the catalog and the balances live in their own tables, and only the order → payment → webhook pipeline is shared with subscriptions. Tables: credit_packs and user_feature_credits.

docs.title: 7.2 The catalog
docs.text:
Admins manage packs through /v1/admin/credit-packs (section 9), gated by the plans:* permissions. A pack has a name, a feature, a quantity, a price and currency, an is_active flag and a sort_order.

  • Packs are taken off sale with isActive: false. There is no delete.
  • A pack for a setting feature (AI_MODEL, ALLOWED_QUESTION_TYPES) is refused with 400: there is nothing to count.
  • A pack may name an AI model (ai_model_code, by ai_models.code). It must be an active model when the pack is saved (404 otherwise). No model means the free plan's AI_MODEL. Work paid for with those credits runs on that model (AiModelSelector.forGeneration in src/ai/ai-model-selector.service.ts), and a model removed later falls back to the default.
  • GET /v1/credits/packs is public and lists active packs in sort_order.

docs.title: 7.3 Buying a pack
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant C as Client app
    participant K as CreditsController
    participant P as PaymentsController
    participant W as Razorpay webhook
    participant DB as Postgres

    C->>K: POST /v1/credits/checkout with creditPackId
    K->>DB: check the pack exists and is on sale
    K->>DB: insert Order PENDING, resource_type CREDIT, metadata with the pack's feature, quantity, model
    K-->>C: creditPack and order
    C->>P: POST /v1/payments/razorpay/create with orderId
    Note over C,W: same Razorpay flow as a plan (section 5.2)
    W->>DB: one transaction - Payment SUCCESS, Order PAID
    W->>DB: upsert user_feature_credits, granted += quantity
    W->>DB: Order FULFILLED
  • Checkout (CreditsService.checkout): 404 for an unknown pack, 422 for one not on sale. The order's metadata records { creditPackId, featureId, quantity, aiModelCode } as the pack is now, so an admin editing the pack before the payment settles does not change what this buyer gets.
  • Grant (CreditsService.grant, on the capture transaction): an INSERT ... ON CONFLICT on the balance's partial unique index adds quantity to granted, so two first grants for the same user cannot both insert a row. An order that is already FULFILLED is skipped. An order with no credit metadata is logged and left PAID rather than throwing, because throwing would roll back the payment and make Razorpay retry the webhook forever.

docs.title: 7.4 Spending and refunding
docs.text:
UsageService.consume takes from the plan first, then from credits:

  1. Resolve the plan feature as usual. If the plan lacks the feature, the whole charge is taken from credits (personal only), otherwise 404.
  2. fromPlan = min(amount, plan quota left) (all of it for an unlimited plan) and fromCredits = amount - fromPlan.
  3. If fromCredits > 0, lock the user's balances for the feature and take it all from one balance: the oldest with enough left. One balance means the charged work runs on a single AI model. None has enough: 422, and nothing is spent.
  4. An enum feature is refused before any of this. Credits only apply to limit features.

Assessment generation keeps the split with the charge (GenerationUsageCharge in the job payload), and release sends a refund back to where it came from: the credit part to the same balance (never period-gated), the rest to the plan counter.

docs.title: 8. Reading your subscription, usage, credits and orders
docs.text:
• GET /v1/subscriptions: the current ACTIVE subscription, with plan, version and features. With x-organization-id, the org's subscription (needs the org permission org_billing:read). 404 if there is none.
  • GET /v1/usage/subscriptions/:subscriptionId: every feature of that subscription's plan version, with used, remaining, and the period. A counter whose period has ended shows used = 0. Same org rules as above.
  • GET /v1/plans: public (no login). Active and displayed plans, each with only its current version and features. Paginated, and filterable by name and audience.
  • GET /v1/credits/balance: the user's personal credit balances, one per feature and AI model, with granted, used and remaining.
  • GET /v1/orders: the user's purchase history (OrdersController, served by PaymentsService.listUserOrders). Details below.

docs.title: 8.1 Order history (GET /v1/orders)
docs.text:
The signed-in user's orders, newest first. Cursor paged on the order id with the shared PaginationDto: query cursor?, limit? (1–50, default 20); meta holds nextCursor and total.

  • Which orders. Only those the user placed, including ones bought for an organization (the purchaser is always the user). Only PAID, FULFILLED and FAILED orders are listed. PENDING orders are checkouts that were never paid, so they are left out. The status filter accepts only those three values (400 otherwise); resourceType filters by SUBSCRIPTION or CREDIT.
  • What each order carries. Amount, currency, status, createdAt and expiresAt. plan (name, code, version, billing cycle) for a subscription order, or creditPack (name, feature, and the quantity bought, taken from the order's metadata) for a credit order. Every payment attempt, newest first, with its status, amount, paidAt, failureReason, and reference, Razorpay's payment id, which users quote to support.
  • What it leaves out. The order's raw metadata and our chk_ checkout reference.
  • How it is loaded. One query for the page of orders and one for their payments, rather than a join that would break the page size. Then one lookup per kind for what was bought (loadOrderPurchases in src/commerce/order-purchases.helper.ts, shared with the admin views). Soft-deleted subscriptions and packs still count: the purchase happened either way.

The frontend shows this on the account page (/account) as the Orders card. Each order opens in a details dialog.

docs.title: 9. Admin endpoints
docs.text:
All under /v1/admin, in src/commerce/admin.controller.ts, served by CommerceAdminService. Each needs a platform permission (see RBAC).

Method and path Permission What it does GET /plans plans:read All plans, including hidden and inactive ones. Filters: isActive, isDisplayed, name, audience. GET /plans/:planId plans:read One plan with every version (newest first) and their features. POST /plans plans:create Create a plan and its version 1 (no features yet). PATCH /plans/:planId plans:update Edit name, description, isActive, isDisplayed, sortOrder. Built-in plans cannot be renamed or deactivated. POST /plans/:planId/versions plans:create Add a new version and make it current. PUT /plans/:planId/versions/:versionNo plans:update Edit a version in place. isCurrent: true makes it the current one. POST /plans/:planId/versions/:versionNumber/features plans:create Attach a feature to a version. PUT /plans/:planId/versions/:versionNumber/features/:featureId plans:update Edit a plan feature. :featureId is the plan_features row id. DELETE /plans/:planId/versions/:versionNumber/features/:featureId plans:delete Soft-delete a plan feature. Subscribers lose it at once. Usage history is kept. GET /features features:read List all features (for the "add feature" picker). GET /orders payments:read All orders, with the buyer and what was bought (plan or credit pack). Filters: status, resourceType, provider, user, date range, search (checkout reference, username, email). GET /orders/:orderId payments:read One order with its metadata and every payment attempt, newest first. GET /payments payments:read All payments, with the payer and the plan bought. Filters: status, provider, user, date range, search. GET /payments/:paymentId payments:read One payment, plus the credit pack bought for a credit order. GET /subscriptions subscriptions:read All subscriptions. Filters: status, user, plan, scope (personal or organization), organizationUid, search. GET /subscriptions/:subscriptionId subscriptions:read One subscription (soft-deleted ones too), its orders with their payments, and its owner's usage of the plan's features in the current period. GET /usage usage:read All usage rows. Filters: user, featureKey, current, scope, organizationUid, search. GET /usage/:usageId usage:read One usage row with the plan feature's type, value and reset period, what is left of the limit, and the owner's credit balances for the same feature. GET /credit-packs plans:read Every credit pack, inactive ones included. In CreditPacksAdminController. GET /credit-packs/:creditPackId plans:read One credit pack. POST /credit-packs plans:create Create a pack. Refuses a setting feature (400) and an unknown or inactive AI model (404). PATCH /credit-packs/:creditPackId plans:update Edit a pack, or take it off sale with isActive: false. Orders already placed keep what they bought.

The order endpoints reuse payments:read, as orders and payments are one purchase pipeline. Admin lists are paged by page number (page, limit up to 100), unlike the user's cursor-paged GET /v1/orders.

docs.title: 10. Business rules and edge cases
docs.text:
1. Every verified user should have one ACTIVE personal subscription. If they have none when they spend usage, a FREE one is created on the spot.
  2. Organizations never fall back to a member's personal plan. No ACTIVE org subscription means metered AI features are refused with 422.
  3. Only individual plans can be bought. Organizations stay on ORG_TRIAL because there is no org checkout.
  4. Checkout blocks buying a plan you already have ACTIVE. It does not block a second checkout while one is still PENDING.
  5. Paying for a new personal plan suspends all other ACTIVE personal plans, FREE included. Org subscriptions are not touched.
  6. An order expires 30 minutes after checkout (CHECKOUT_ORDER_TTL_MINUTES). After that, POST /v1/payments/razorpay/create returns 422, and the user must check out again. The same applies to an order whose payment failed.
  7. A payment.captured webhook is still honored if it arrives after the order expired or failed. Expiry and failure only block starting a payment.
  8. Only the webhook updates our database. If the webhook never arrives, the subscription stays PENDING even though the user paid.
  9. A limit value that is not a number (for example unlimited) means unlimited.
  10. Usage resets lazily on the next consume, using UTC dates.
  11. release only refunds into the same period. A charge made before the current period_start is not given back.
  12. A plan version can be bought until its effective_until, even if it is no longer the current one.
  13. Editing a version's price with PUT .../versions/:versionNo changes it in place, so later checkouts of that version charge the new price.
  14. Credits are spent only after the plan's quota for the period runs out, and only for personal requests. An org request never touches a member's credits.
  15. One charge is taken from one credit balance. If a user's credits for a feature are split across AI models and none alone has enough, the charge is refused even though the total would cover it.
  16. A credit order grants what the pack held at checkout (its metadata), not what the pack holds when the payment settles.

docs.title: 13. Known gaps and TODOs
docs.text:
1. No expiry. Nothing moves a subscription to EXPIRED, and lookups ignore expires_at. The 7-day org trial and monthly plans never actually end.
  2. No renewal, cancel, or refund. auto_renew, cancelled_at, CANCELLED, PAST_DUE, and REFUNDED are unused.
  3. No org checkout. Organization plans and organization credits cannot be bought.
  4. Fulfillment is an if per resource type in markPaymentCaptured, with a TODO to move to an event-driven handler per resource type.
  5. Stale checkouts are never cleaned up. Expired PENDING orders and their PENDING subscriptions stay as they are. They are hidden from GET /v1/orders, but not from the admin lists.
  6. The seeded FREE and ORG_TRIAL plans do not include AI_LEARNING_ROADMAP, so creating a roadmap fails with 404 until an admin adds that feature to the plan.
  7. No unique index on user_feature_usage for (user or org, plan feature). Two first-time consume calls at the same moment can create two counter rows.
  8. AI_MODEL is read from the personal plan only, even on org requests.
  9. The webhook does not check the amount. We trust that the captured payment matches the order, because the Razorpay order was created with our amount.
  10. Zero-price plans through checkout would send a 0 amount order to Razorpay, which Razorpay is expected to reject, giving the user 503.

docs.title: 1. Purpose
docs.text:
Evaluation turns a submitted attempt into an evaluated one. It grades every saved response, adds up the marks, and writes the score and counters onto the attempt.

Evaluation is always asynchronous. Nothing is graded during the test or inside the submit request. The submit call only queues a job, and RabbitMQ consumers do the work. This is because:

  • coding answers must run against many test cases on an external code runner, which is slow
  • descriptive answers are graded by an LLM, which is slow and can fail
  • a failure should be retryable without making the user submit again

The code lives in src/assessments/evaluation/.

docs.title: 2. Key concepts
docs.text: Term Meaning Parent job One EVALUATE_ATTEMPT row in jobs per submitted attempt. It tracks the whole evaluation. Child job One job per question type that has answers: EVALUATE_MCQ_RESPONSES, EVALUATE_CODING_RESPONSES, EVALUATE_DESCRIPTIVE_RESPONSES. Each has parentJobId set and a list of responseIds. Orchestrator EvaluationOrchestratorService. It runs the parent: claims the attempt, makes the children and publishes them. Worker ResponseEvaluationWorker. It runs one child: grades its responses one by one. Evaluator A class that implements QuestionEvaluator for one question type: McqEvaluator, CodingEvaluator, DescriptiveEvaluator. Registry EvaluatorRegistry. It maps a question type to its evaluator. Adding a type means adding an evaluator to the EVALUATORS provider list. Aggregator EvaluationAggregatorService. It is called whenever a child settles. When all children are done, it scores the attempt and settles the parent. Snapshot The assessment_questions row the response answers. It holds the answer key, test cases, checkpoints and marks for that assessment. Settled job A job in COMPLETED, FAILED or CANCELLED.

docs.title: 3. Data used
docs.text:
See ERD: Assessment Engine and ERD: Async Jobs.

  • assessment_attempts: status moves submitted -> evaluating -> evaluated. score, attempted_questions, correct_responses and incorrect_responses are written at the end.
  • assessment_attempt_responses: evaluation_status, is_correct, marks_awarded, code_verdict, evaluation_result (jsonb grading detail), evaluated_at.
  • assessment_questions (+ type-specific content): correctMarks, incorrectMarks, MCQ correctOptionId, coding testCases / timeLimitMs / memoryLimitMb, descriptive checkpoints.
  • jobs: the parent and child rows (status, attempts, maxAttempts, statusDescription, result, error, parentJobId).

docs.title: 4. Main flow: submit to result
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant API as AttemptsService
    participant MQ as RabbitMQ
    participant O as Orchestrator
    participant W as ResponseEvaluationWorker
    participant E as Evaluator
    participant A as Aggregator
    participant DB as Postgres
    API->>DB: attempt submitted and parent job PENDING
    API->>MQ: attempt.evaluate
    MQ->>O: AttemptEvaluationConsumer
    O->>DB: TX - lock parent job and attempt rows
    O->>DB: attempt to evaluating, parent to PROCESSING
    O->>DB: group responses by question type and create child jobs
    O->>MQ: publish attempt.evaluate.mcq / coding / descriptive
    MQ->>W: type consumer
    W->>DB: claim child job, check parent PROCESSING and attempt evaluating
    loop each response not yet completed
        W->>DB: response pending to processing
        W->>E: evaluate
        E-->>W: isCorrect, marksAwarded, codeVerdict, details
        W->>DB: response to completed with grade
    end
    W->>DB: child job COMPLETED with tally
    W->>A: onChildSettled
    A->>DB: TX - lock parent, read children
    alt some child still running
        A->>DB: parent statusDescription n of m evaluators done
    else all children completed
        A->>DB: sum marks, write score and counters, attempt to evaluated
        A->>DB: parent COMPLETED with result
    else some child failed
        A->>DB: parent FAILED, attempt stays evaluating
    end

Step by step:

  1. Submit (see attempts) writes the attempt as submitted, creates the parent job (maxAttempts = 3), and publishes { jobId, attemptId, attemptUid, assessmentId, userId } to exchange attempt, key attempt.evaluate.
  2. AttemptEvaluationConsumer calls EvaluationOrchestratorService.start. In one transaction, with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on the parent job and the attempt:
    • It drops the message if the job does not exist, has the wrong type, or is already settled (a redelivery).
    • If the attempt is gone, rejected or already evaluated, it cancels the parent and stops.
    • It moves the attempt submitted -> evaluating (claimEvaluation). An attempt already evaluating stays so, which is how a retry resumes.
    • It moves the parent to PROCESSING and increments attempts.
    • It groups the attempt's responses by question type. No responses at all means the attempt is scored right away (score 0) and the parent completes.
    • It creates one child job per type, or reuses an existing one: a FAILED child is reopened, a PENDING child is republished, and a COMPLETED or PROCESSING child is left alone.
  3. After commit, each child is published to its own queue. A child that cannot be published is marked FAILED on the spot, and the aggregator is told so the parent does not wait forever.
  4. Per-type consumers (McqEvaluationConsumer, CodingEvaluationConsumer, DescriptiveEvaluationConsumer) all call ResponseEvaluationWorker.run. The worker:
    • drops the message if the job does not exist, has the wrong type, is already settled, or its parent is no longer PROCESSING
    • cancels the child if the attempt is no longer evaluating (for example it was rejected), then tells the aggregator
    • grades each response that is not already completed or cancelled. Each grade is saved as soon as it is made, so a retry continues where it stopped
    • writes the child's result { graded, correct, incorrect, marksAwarded } and completes it
  5. EvaluationAggregatorService.onChildSettled locks the parent row, so only one caller finishes the evaluation:
    • any child still running: it only updates the progress text ("1/3 evaluators done")
    • all children COMPLETED: EvaluationService.evaluate sums the grades, writes them onto the attempt, and moves it to evaluated (only if it is still evaluating)
    • any child not completed: the parent becomes FAILED with error.failedChildren, and the attempt stays evaluating
    • attempt rejected meanwhile: the parent is cancelled

Separate queues per type mean slow coding or LLM grading never holds up MCQ grading for other attempts.

docs.title: 5.1 Response evaluation status
docs.text:
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> pending: answer saved
    pending --> processing: worker claims it
    pending --> cancelled
    processing --> completed: graded
    processing --> failed: evaluator threw
    processing --> cancelled
    failed --> pending: parent retried
    completed --> pending: answer changed
    cancelled --> pending: answer changed

A response carries a grade (isCorrect and marksAwarded) only when it is completed. assertGradeMatchesStatus enforces this. A worker that finds a response already processing grades it again. This handles a redelivered message after a worker crashed mid-grade.

docs.title: 5.2 Parent job
docs.text:
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> PENDING: created on submit
    PENDING --> PROCESSING: orchestrator claims
    PENDING --> FAILED: could not be published
    PROCESSING --> COMPLETED: all children completed
    PROCESSING --> FAILED: a child failed
    PROCESSING --> CANCELLED: attempt rejected
    FAILED --> PENDING: retried via the jobs retry endpoint

docs.title: 6. Evaluators and marking rules
docs.text:
All marks are stored as decimal(8,2) and rounded to 2 decimal places. The marks come from the question snapshot (question.correctMarks, question.incorrectMarks).

Type Evaluator How it decides Marks Negative marks MCQ McqEvaluator selected option equals correctOptionId right: correctMarks. Wrong: -abs(incorrectMarks). No option: 0 Yes, only for a wrong pick Coding CodingEvaluator runs code on every test case (hidden included), one after another correctMarks * passed / total (partial credit) Never Descriptive DescriptiveEvaluator an LLM says which checkpoints the answer covers sum of the weightage of completed checkpoints, as a percent of correctMarks (partial credit) Never

A question the user never answered (no response row) is not graded. It earns 0 and is not counted as attempted.

docs.title: 6.1 MCQ
docs.text:
• gradeMcq in src/assessments/domain/response-invariants.ts.
  • isCorrect is true only for the right option.
  • No details are stored (evaluation_result is null).

docs.title: 6.2 Coding
docs.text:
• Uses the shared CODE_RUNNER (see code execution) with the question's timeLimitMs and memoryLimitMb.
  • Empty or missing code: wrong_answer, 0 marks, no runs.
  • Each case is judged by judgeTestCase: passed, wrong_answer, time_limit_exceeded, memory_limit_exceeded, or runtime_error (compile errors count as runtime errors). Output comparison is exact after normalising line endings, trailing spaces and trailing blank lines.
  • isCorrect is true only when all cases pass. codeVerdict is accepted, or the verdict of the first failing case.
  • evaluation_result stores, for each case: pass/fail, verdict, time, memory and, for failed cases, an error message, the input, the expected output and the program's output (clipped to 2,000 characters). The run time and memory stored on the response are the maximum across cases.
  • What the candidate sees (codingEvaluationOf): pass/fail, verdict, time, memory and error per case. For a hidden case the error message never includes their output or stderr, because a program could echo the hidden input. Reviewers see everything.
  • A CodeRunnerError (runner down, busy, not configured, unsupported language) is not a wrong answer. It fails the response and the child job so a retry can grade it later.

docs.title: 6.3 Descriptive (LLM-graded)
docs.text:
• Each descriptive question has checkpoints with integer weightages that sum to 100 (assertCheckpointWeights).
  • A blank answer completes nothing and makes no LLM call.
