  • Otherwise AiService.findCompletedCheckpoints sends the question, the checkpoints and the answer (inside <answer> tags) to the model with structured output, temperature 0, and up to 2 tries. Any checkpoint id the model invents is rejected. See AI.
  • The model is the assessment creator's plan model (AiModelSelector.forUser(createdBy)), and the call is audited against the creator, with the child job id.
  • scoreCheckpoints: scorePercent is the sum of completed weightages. marksAwarded = correctMarks * scorePercent / 100. isCorrect is true when scorePercent >= 60 (DESCRIPTIVE_CORRECT_THRESHOLD_PERCENT).
  • evaluation_result stores each checkpoint (description, weightage, completed, marks) and scorePercent. The candidate sees this after evaluation.

docs.title: 6.4 Attempt totals
docs.text:
EvaluationService.evaluate, run inside the aggregator's transaction:

Field Value score sum of marksAwarded over completed responses (can be negative because of MCQ penalties) attempted_questions number of response rows (a blank descriptive answer still counts) correct_responses completed responses with isCorrect = true incorrect_responses completed responses with isCorrect = false status evaluated, only if the attempt is still evaluating (a conditional update)

docs.title: 7. Failures, retries and re-evaluation
docs.text:
1. Messages are always acked. The consumers catch errors instead of rethrowing them, so a message is not requeued forever on a failure that may repeat (for example the runner being down). Retry is explicit.
  2. A child fails when an evaluator throws. The response being graded becomes failed, and grades already saved in that child stay.
  3. The parent fails once every child has settled and at least one did not complete. The attempt stays evaluating.
  4. The parent cannot start (an error in the claim transaction): the parent is marked FAILED. Nothing else was written.
  5. The publish on submit fails: the parent is FAILED, and the attempt stays submitted.
  6. Retry is POST /v1/jobs/:id/retry on the parent job, by its owner. Retrying a child directly gives 409 "retry its parent job instead". The parent may run at most 3 times, and each child job also has maxAttempts = 3. On retry, the orchestrator keeps completed children, reopens failed ones (their failed responses go back to pending), and grades only what is left.
  7. Redelivery is safe. Settled jobs are dropped, an evaluating attempt and processing responses are picked up again, and every status write is conditional on the status last read.
  8. Rejection during evaluation: children cancel themselves, the parent is cancelled, and the attempt keeps rejected. If the rejection lands between the last grade and the final update, the conditional update leaves the attempt rejected and the parent completes with "Attempt was no longer evaluating".
  9. There is no re-evaluation of an evaluated attempt. There is no endpoint or job type that re-grades a finished attempt (for example after a question fix). Only failed evaluations can be retried.

docs.title: 8. Async events, queues and notifications
docs.text:
All on exchange attempt (src/config/rabbitmq/rabbitmq.constants.ts). Routes for retries come from src/jobs/job-routes.ts.

Routing key Queue Consumer Job type attempt.evaluate attempt-evaluation-queue AttemptEvaluationConsumer EVALUATE_ATTEMPT (parent) attempt.evaluate.mcq attempt-evaluation-mcq-queue McqEvaluationConsumer EVALUATE_MCQ_RESPONSES attempt.evaluate.coding attempt-evaluation-coding-queue CodingEvaluationConsumer EVALUATE_CODING_RESPONSES attempt.evaluate.descriptive attempt-evaluation-descriptive-queue DescriptiveEvaluationConsumer EVALUATE_DESCRIPTIVE_RESPONSES

Every message is { jobId, ...job.payload }, so a retry can rebuild it from the job row. All consumers are marked @Public() so the global JWT guard skips them.

Announcing results: no WebSocket event and no email are sent when evaluation finishes or fails. Progress is visible only by polling:

  • GET /v1/attempts/:uid/result: 400 until evaluated.
  • GET /v1/jobs/:id: the parent job with its children (statusDescription such as "2/3 evaluators done"). The job id is not returned by submit, though.

See realtime events and notifications.

docs.title: 9. Where the code lives
docs.text: Path What src/assessments/evaluation/evaluation.module.ts Wires evaluators, registry, services and consumers src/assessments/evaluation/evaluation-orchestrator.service.ts Parent job: claim, fan-out, publish src/assessments/evaluation/response-evaluation.worker.ts Child job: claim, grade, complete src/assessments/evaluation/evaluation-aggregator.service.ts Settles the parent once all children settle src/assessments/evaluation/evaluation.service.ts Sums grades onto the attempt src/assessments/evaluation/evaluators/*.evaluator.ts MCQ, coding, descriptive grading src/assessments/evaluation/evaluator.registry.ts, evaluation.constants.ts Type-to-evaluator and type-to-job mapping, max attempts src/assessments/evaluation/consumers/ RabbitMQ subscribers src/assessments/evaluation/interfaces/ QuestionEvaluator, job payload and result shapes src/assessments/domain/response-*.ts, attempt-transitions.ts, descriptive-invariants.ts Status rules and scoring helpers src/jobs/ Job rows, retry endpoint, child-outcome.ts, job-routes.ts

docs.title: 10. Known gaps and TODOs found in code
docs.text:
1. No completion notification. Nothing pushes or emails the result. Clients must poll.
  2. The job id is hard to find. submitAttempt returns true, not the job id, and there is no "list my jobs" endpoint. So a candidate cannot easily retry a failed evaluation through POST /v1/jobs/:id/retry.
  3. No automatic recovery. No scheduler sweeps attempts stuck in submitted or evaluating after a failure. They stay there until someone retries the parent job by hand.
  4. Retry is billed like AI work. POST /v1/jobs/:id/retry is rate-limited under the AI_GENERATION scope with cost 5 (src/jobs/jobs.controller.ts:76), even for an MCQ-only evaluation.
  5. No re-grading of evaluated attempts (for example after an answer key fix).
  6. checkerType is ignored. Coding questions store a checkerType (default exact), but grading always uses the exact comparison (src/code-execution/judge-test-case.ts:19).
  7. Descriptive grading is tied to the creator. It runs on the assessment creator's plan model (AI_MODEL feature) and the LLM call is audited against the creator, not the candidate (descriptive.evaluator.ts:43-57). Keep this in mind when reading AI usage and audit data.

docs.title: 1. Purpose
docs.text:
Some work is too slow for an HTTP request: asking an LLM for questions, grading an attempt, building a roadmap, or importing a CSV of invitations. TestFlow does this work in the background:

  1. The API saves a job row in Postgres.
  2. It publishes a message to RabbitMQ.
  3. A consumer (a worker) picks the message up, does the work, and updates the job row.
  4. The client polls the job through GET /v1/jobs/:id.

The jobs module (src/jobs/) owns the job record, its state rules, and the polling and retry API. It does not own any worker. Workers live in the feature modules.

The schedulers module (src/schedulers/) owns every timed (cron) task. Today there is one.

docs.title: 2. Key concepts
docs.text: Term Meaning Job One row in jobs. It tracks one unit of background work from start to finish. Producer Code that creates a job row and publishes its message (for example LearningRoadmapsService.create). Consumer / worker A class with a @RabbitSubscribe handler that does the work and settles the job. Settled A job that is completed, failed or cancelled. It will not change on its own. Claimable A job that is pending or processing. A worker may still pick it up. Parent job A job that only tracks child jobs (GENERATE_ASSESSMENT, EVALUATE_ATTEMPT). Children point to it with parent_job_id. Attempts How many times a worker has picked the job up. max_attempts is the budget for manual retries. CONSUMER env var When false, the instance only publishes messages and does not run consumers. Use this to split API and worker instances.

docs.title: 3. Data
docs.text:
The table is jobs. See ERD for the full definition. The important columns are:

Column Meaning id bigint. Returned to clients as a string. type A JobType value (stored as varchar). queue A label for the job family, for example roadmap, assessment-generation, attempt-evaluation, organization-invitations. It is not the RabbitMQ queue name. status JobStatus enum. payload The message body, without jobId. Must include userId (see section 6). Never returned to clients. result / error JSON set when the job settles. status_description A short progress text for the UI, for example "Saving roadmap nodes and links". attempts / max_attempts Pick-up count and retry budget. parent_job_id Link to a parent job. Deleting the parent deletes the children (CASCADE). idempotency_key Optional. Unique per created_by. Used by assessment generation to make repeated create requests safe. Never returned to clients. created_by The user. SET NULL if the user is deleted, so the job stays as an audit record. started_at / completed_at Timestamps.

docs.title: Job types
docs.text:
JobType Created by Parent? Retry through CREATE_ASSESSMENT Prompt-based generation, AssessmentsService.generate (also used for roadmap practice nodes). Consumed by QuestionGenerationConsumer. No POST /v1/jobs/:id/retry GENERATE_ASSESSMENT Assessment generation Yes, of the three section types POST /v1/assessments/:id/generation/retry GENERATE_MCQ_SECTION / GENERATE_CODING_SECTION / GENERATE_DESCRIPTIVE_SECTION Assessment generation, one per section Child Through the assessment EVALUATE_ATTEMPT Attempt submit Yes, of the three evaluate types POST /v1/jobs/:id/retry on the parent EVALUATE_MCQ_RESPONSES / EVALUATE_CODING_RESPONSES / EVALUATE_DESCRIPTIVE_RESPONSES Evaluation fan-out Child Through the parent ANALYZE_ROADMAP_INTENT / GENERATE_ROADMAP / MODIFY_ROADMAP_GRAPH Learning roadmaps No POST /v1/jobs/:id/retry IMPORT_ORG_INVITATIONS Organization CSV invitation import No POST /v1/jobs/:id/retry

See Assessment Generation, Evaluation, Learning Roadmaps and Organizations for each flow.

docs.title: 4. Lifecycle
docs.text:
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> pending: producer saves job
    pending --> processing: worker picks it up
    pending --> failed: publish to RabbitMQ failed
    pending --> cancelled: abandoned before start
    processing --> completed: work done
    processing --> failed: work failed
    processing --> cancelled: abandoned mid-run
    processing --> pending: requeued
    failed --> pending: POST retry
    failed --> processing: generation parent reopened for retried sections
    completed --> [*]
    cancelled --> [*]

These rules live in src/jobs/domain/job-transitions.ts (JOB_TRANSITIONS). Helper functions (startJob, completeJob, failJob, cancelJob, requeueJob, reopenJob) throw a conflict error if a move is not allowed.

Other domain helpers:

  • claimJob(status): pending → processing. If the job is already processing, it stays so. This is how a worker recovers a message that was redelivered after another worker crashed.
  • isClaimable(status): true for pending and processing. Workers use it to drop redelivered messages for jobs that are already settled.
  • assertRetryable(status, budget): only a failed job with attempts < max_attempts can be retried.
  • childOutcome(statuses) in src/jobs/domain/child-outcome.ts: a parent is running while any child is unsettled, completed when all children completed, and failed otherwise. childrenToRetry returns the children that did not complete, so a retry only re-runs those.

docs.title: 5.1 Produce, consume, poll
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant C as Client
    participant API as Feature service
    participant DB as Postgres jobs
    participant MQ as RabbitMQ
    participant W as Consumer
    participant J as JobsService

    C->>API: POST some slow action
    API->>DB: insert job PENDING in the same transaction as the feature row
    API->>MQ: publish jobId plus payload after commit
    API-->>C: 202 with jobId
    MQ->>W: message
    W->>J: markProcessing, attempts + 1
    W->>J: updateProgress with status text
    alt success
        W->>J: markCompleted with result
    else error
        W->>J: markFailed with reason
    end
    W-->>MQ: ack
    loop until settled
        C->>API: GET /v1/jobs/jobId
        API-->>C: status, statusDescription, result or error
    end

The pattern every producer follows:

  1. Write first, publish second. The job row is saved in the same transaction as the feature's own rows. The message is published only after the commit. If it were published first, a fast worker could read the job before it exists.
  2. The message is { jobId, ...payload }. Nothing else is stored. This is what makes generic retry possible (section 5.2).
  3. If publish fails, the producer marks the job failed, walks the feature row back to a safe status, and returns 503.

The pattern every worker follows:

  1. Mark the job processing (markProcessing also adds 1 to attempts).
  2. Write short progress text with updateProgress.
  3. Settle with markCompleted(result) or markFailed(reason).
  4. Catch errors instead of re-throwing them. The message is acked either way. A failure that will happen again (a bad LLM output, a malformed file) would otherwise loop forever.

docs.title: 5.2 Manual retry
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant C as Client
    participant J as JobsService
    participant DB as Postgres
    participant MQ as RabbitMQ

    C->>J: POST /v1/jobs/id/retry
    J->>DB: load job, check owner
    J->>J: must be FAILED with attempts left
    J->>J: reject generation and evaluation child types
    J->>J: look up exchange and routing key in JOB_ROUTES
    J->>DB: status PENDING, clear error and result
    J->>MQ: publish jobId plus payload
    alt publish fails
        J->>DB: back to FAILED with the old error
        J-->>C: 503
    else ok
        J-->>C: 200 with job
    end
  • The route for each type is in src/jobs/job-routes.ts (JOB_ROUTES). The map is typed so that adding a new job type without a route is a compile error.
  • attempts is not increased by retry. It goes up only when a worker actually picks the message up.
  • Generation jobs are refused here and must use POST /v1/assessments/:id/generation/retry. Evaluation child jobs are refused here, and the caller must retry the EVALUATE_ATTEMPT parent.
  • Retry uses the same rate limit as creating AI work (CLASS_B, scope AI_GENERATION, cost 5). A retry should not be a cheaper way to run the LLM.

docs.title: 6. Rules and edge cases
docs.text:
Situation Behaviour Job id is not numeric 400 "Invalid job id" Job not found 404 payload.userId is not the caller 403 payload.userId is missing No ownership check. Any logged-in user can read the job. This is why every producer must put userId in the payload. Retry a job that is not failed 409 Retry with no attempts left 409 Retry a job with an unknown type or no payload 409

The response leaves out payload and idempotency_key. For GENERATE_ASSESSMENT and EVALUATE_ATTEMPT parents, it adds a sections array. Each item has the child jobId, sectionId, questionType, status, statusDescription, attempts and error. One poll shows the progress of every child.

docs.title: 7. RabbitMQ setup, retry and dead letters
docs.text:
Configured in src/config/rabbitmq/rabbitmq.module.ts with @golevelup/nestjs-rabbitmq.

Exchange (topic) Routing key → queue question.generation question.generate → question-generation-queue; question.section.mcq / .coding / .descriptive → question-section-<type>-queue attempt attempt.evaluate → attempt-evaluation-queue; attempt.evaluate.mcq / .coding / .descriptive → attempt-evaluation-<type>-queue roadmap roadmap.analyze / .generate / .modify → roadmap-analysis-queue / roadmap-generation-queue / roadmap-modification-queue organization organization.invitations.import → organization-invitation-import-queue

Each question type has its own queue, so slow coding work never holds up MCQ work.

Retry and dead-letter behaviour:

  • No dead-letter exchange is configured. No queue sets x-dead-letter-exchange, and there is no retry queue with a delay.
  • No automatic retry. The library's default on a thrown error is to nack and requeue the message. Because workers catch their errors and mark the job failed, messages are acked and not requeued. Failed jobs stay failed until someone calls the retry endpoint.
  • Redelivery after a crash. If a worker process dies before it acks, RabbitMQ redelivers the message. Workers that use isClaimable / claimJob (evaluation, invitation import) handle this safely. The roadmap consumers do not check this (see section 10).
  • connectionInitOptions: { wait: false } means the app starts even when RabbitMQ is down. The health check reports rabbitmq: down until it connects.
  • RabbitMQ handlers run through the same global guards as HTTP. Each consumer class is marked @Public() so JwtAuthGuard lets it through, and RateLimitGuard skips non-HTTP contexts.

docs.title: 8. Schedulers
docs.text:
All cron tasks are registered in src/schedulers/, and nowhere else. A feature module owns the work. The scheduler only calls an exported service at the right time. ScheduleModule.forRoot() from @nestjs/schedule is imported only in SchedulersModule.

Name Schedule Class What it does newsletter-dispatch Every minute (CronExpression.EVERY_MINUTE) NewsletterScheduler.dispatchDueNewsletters Calls NewslettersDispatchService.dispatchDue(), which claims newsletters whose scheduled_at has passed and emails all subscribers. See Platform Services.

Details:

  • Off switch: set NEWSLETTER_SCHEDULER_ENABLED=false on machines that share a database but must not send mail (a dev laptop, a restored production snapshot).
  • Errors are caught and logged, so a failed tick does not become an unhandled rejection. The next tick runs as normal.
  • Multiple instances. Every instance runs the cron. This is safe because claiming uses FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED. Two instances never claim the same newsletter. Inside one instance, a dispatchInFlight flag stops overlapping ticks.
  • Newsletters are not jobs rows. They keep their own status on the newsletters table.

docs.title: 9. Endpoints summary
docs.text:
Full details are in API v1.

Method and path Purpose Rate limit GET /v1/jobs/:id Job status, result or error, plus sections for parents CLASS_C POST /v1/jobs/:id/retry Requeue a failed job CLASS_B, scope AI_GENERATION, cost 5

Both need login. Ownership is checked through payload.userId.

docs.title: 10. Where the code lives
docs.text: Path What it does src/jobs/jobs.controller.ts Poll and retry endpoints src/jobs/jobs.service.ts markProcessing, updateProgress, markCompleted, markFailed, findOne, findSections, retry src/jobs/job-routes.ts Job type → exchange and routing key src/jobs/domain/ States, allowed transitions, invariants, parent/child outcome src/jobs/serializers/jobs.serializer.ts Response shape (hides payload) src/common/entities/job.entity.ts Job entity src/common/enums/jobs.enums.ts JobType, pipeline type groups src/config/rabbitmq/ Exchanges, queues, routing keys src/schedulers/ SchedulersModule and NewsletterScheduler

docs.title: 11. Known gaps and TODOs
docs.text:
• No dead-letter queue and no automatic retry with backoff. Transient errors (an LLM timeout, a short network blip) fail the job at once. A person must retry it.
  • Ownership depends on the payload. A job without payload.userId can be read by any logged-in user. A check on created_by would be safer.
  • markProcessing does not check transitions. It writes processing without reading the row. The roadmap consumers call it without first checking isClaimable, so a redelivered message for a settled roadmap job would reopen it.
  • cancelled has no API. Only internal evaluation code cancels jobs. There is no user-facing cancel endpoint.
  • No cleanup. Old job rows are never deleted or archived.
  • No stuck-job sweeper. A job left in processing (for example, after a worker crash with no redelivery) stays that way. No scheduler finds or fails it.

docs.title: 1. Purpose
docs.text:
A learning roadmap is a personal study plan. The learner types a goal in plain words, for example "I want to become a backend engineer". The system then:

  1. Asks the AI to understand the goal and come up with a few requirement questions (for example "How much time can you spend per week?").
  2. Takes the learner's answers and asks the AI to build a graph of study steps.
  3. Lets the learner mark steps as done, revise the graph in natural language, and generate a practice assessment for practice steps.

Each roadmap belongs to exactly one user. Roadmaps are not shared and are not tied to an organization.

All AI work runs in the background through RabbitMQ. HTTP calls return quickly with a job id, and the client polls GET /v1/jobs/:id (see Jobs and Schedulers).

docs.title: 2. Key concepts
docs.text: Term Meaning Roadmap One learner's plan. Has a status, a title, a description, a meta JSON blob, and a free-text notepad. Node One step in the plan. A node is either a knowledge node (something to learn) or a practice node (a check on what was learned). Edge A directed link from → to between two nodes. It means "do this before that". Entry node The single node with no incoming edge. This is where the learner starts. Cursor current_node_id on the roadmap. It points at the step the learner is working on. Requirement questions Questions the AI asks after reading the goal. Stored in roadmap.meta.requirementQuestions. Resolved node A node whose status is completed or skipped. Both count as "done" (RESOLVED_NODE_STATUSES). Template A ready-made goal text (name, description, goal) that a client can show as a starting point. Scoped modification A revision request that names affectedNodes. Only those nodes (and new nodes next to them) may change.

docs.title: Graph rules
docs.text:
The roadmap is a DAG (directed acyclic graph). Before anything from the AI is saved, RoadmapGraphService.assertValidGraph checks that:

  • There is at least one node.
  • Every node has a known type (knowledge or practice) and a non-empty title.
  • Every positionIndex is a whole number of 0 or more, and no two nodes share one.
  • Every edge points at nodes that exist, with no self-loops and no duplicate edges.
  • There are no cycles (checked with Kahn's algorithm).
  • There is exactly one entry node, and every node can be reached from it.

If any rule fails, the job fails with a 422-style message: "The generated roadmap was not usable: ...". Nothing is written.

docs.title: Node meta
docs.text:
Node type Useful meta fields knowledge resources (title, url, kind), estimatedMinutes, concepts practice coversNodeIds (the knowledge nodes this step checks), questionCount, assessmentId (set once an assessment is generated)

Edges may carry meta.label and an optional meta.condition (for example "score >= 70"). The condition is stored but not enforced by the backend today.

docs.title: 3. Data
docs.text:
Tables: learning_roadmaps, learning_roadmap_nodes, learning_node_edges, learning_roadmap_templates. See ERD for columns and keys.

A few points worth knowing:

  • learning_roadmaps.meta is always merged, never replaced. It keeps rawDescription (what the user typed), all job ids, the requirement answers, and an audit trail of each LLM run (analysis, generation, modifications[] with model, prompt version, and diff counts).
  • notepad is select: false. Only the two notepad endpoints load it.
  • current_node_id is ON DELETE SET NULL. The modification code re-anchors it so the learner does not lose their place (see section 6).
  • learning_roadmaps.job_id holds the id of the most recent job for that roadmap.

docs.title: 4.1 Create, analyse, answer, generate
docs.text:
This is the main flow. It has two AI stages with a human step in between.

sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant C as Client
    participant API as LearningRoadmapsController
    participant S as LearningRoadmapsService
    participant DB as Postgres
    participant MQ as RabbitMQ roadmap exchange
    participant AC as RoadmapAnalysisConsumer
    participant GC as RoadmapGenerationConsumer
    participant AI as RoadmapAiService

    C->>API: POST /v1/roadmaps with description
    API->>S: create
    S->>S: usageService.consume AI_LEARNING_ROADMAP
    S->>DB: insert roadmap status ANALYZING and job PENDING
    S->>MQ: publish roadmap.analyze after commit
    API-->>C: 202 with roadmapId and jobId
    MQ->>AC: AnalyzeRoadmapIntentJob
    AC->>DB: job PROCESSING, roadmap ANALYZING
    AC->>AI: analyzeRoadmapIntent
    AI-->>AC: title, description, requirement questions
    AC->>DB: roadmap DRAFT with questions, job COMPLETED
    C->>API: GET /v1/jobs/jobId until completed
    C->>API: POST /v1/roadmaps/id/requirement-collection with answers
    API->>S: submitRequirements
    S->>DB: merge answers, roadmap GENERATING, new job PENDING
    S->>MQ: publish roadmap.generate
    API-->>C: 202 with new jobId
    MQ->>GC: GenerateRoadmapJob
    GC->>AI: generateRoadmap
    AI-->>GC: nodes and edges
    GC->>DB: validate graph, replace nodes and edges, roadmap ACTIVE
    GC->>DB: job COMPLETED with graph
    C->>API: GET /v1/roadmaps/id/graph

Step by step:

  1. Create. POST /v1/roadmaps first spends one unit of the AI_LEARNING_ROADMAP plan quota (see Commerce). It then saves the roadmap in analyzing status and a jobs row of type ANALYZE_ROADMAP_INTENT in one transaction.
  2. Publish after commit. The RabbitMQ message is sent only after the transaction commits. If the publish fails, the job is marked failed, the roadmap is set to failed, and the API returns 503.
  3. Analyse. The consumer calls the LLM. The model is chosen per user by AiModelSelector.forUser. On success the roadmap gets its title, description and questions, and moves to draft.
  4. Answer. The client sends answers keyed by question id. Unknown ids are rejected with 400. Answers are trimmed and merged into the stored questions. The client cannot change the original description.
  5. Generate. The consumer asks the LLM for a graph, validates it, deletes any old nodes and edges, and inserts the new ones. The cursor is set to the entry node, and the roadmap becomes active.

For LLM graph and prompt details, see AI.

docs.title: 4.2 Revise the graph in natural language
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant C as Client
    participant S as LearningRoadmapsService
    participant MQ as RabbitMQ
    participant MC as RoadmapModificationConsumer
    participant AI as RoadmapAiService
    participant G as RoadmapGraphService

    C->>S: POST /v1/roadmaps/id/graph/modify with description and affectedNodes
    S->>S: check status is ACTIVE and affectedNodes belong to roadmap
    S->>MQ: roadmap MODIFYING, publish roadmap.modify
    S-->>C: 202 with jobId
    MQ->>MC: ModifyRoadmapGraphJob
    MC->>G: loadGraph
    MC->>AI: modifyRoadmapGraph with full graph as context
    AI-->>MC: diff with added, updated, removed, edges
    MC->>G: applyModification
    G->>G: check diff only names nodes of this roadmap
    G->>G: in scoped mode check nothing outside scope changes
    G->>G: validate resulting graph
    G-->>MC: new graph and diff
    MC->>MC: job COMPLETED with graph and diff, roadmap ACTIVE

Key points:

  • The AI returns a diff, not a full new graph. Surviving nodes are updated in place, so they keep their ids and the learner's progress.
  • Nodes are removed only when the diff lists them in removed.
  • Edges are fully replaced by the diff's edges list.
  • Even in scoped mode, the AI sees the whole graph. Otherwise a local edit could break the path around it.
  • The job result contains both the new graph and a diff (added, updated, removed node summaries). The client should show the diff, so a revision never changes the plan silently.
  • Each revision is logged in roadmap.meta.modifications[].

docs.title: 4.3 Track progress
docs.text:
PUT /v1/roadmaps/:id/nodes/:nodeId/progress with { status } is the only way a learner changes a node. In one transaction it:

  1. Sets the node status. completed_at is stamped when entering completed and cleared when leaving it.
  2. If the new status is in_progress, moves the roadmap cursor to this node.
  3. Re-counts nodes. If every node is resolved, the roadmap becomes completed. If not, it goes back to (or stays) active.

Progress can only be written while the roadmap is active or completed. During modifying it returns 409, because the revision may be rewriting the same rows.

docs.title: 4.4 Generate a practice assessment for a node
docs.text:
This is the link between roadmaps and Assessments.

sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant C as Client
    participant R as LearningRoadmapAssessmentService
    participant DB as Postgres
    participant A as AssessmentsService

    C->>R: POST /v1/roadmaps/id/nodes/nodeId/assessments
    R->>DB: load roadmap, must be ACTIVE or COMPLETED
    R->>DB: load node, must be PRACTICE with no assessmentId
    R->>DB: load covered knowledge nodes that are resolved
    R->>R: build prompt from roadmap, step and covered topics
    R->>A: generate with maxParticipants 1
    A-->>R: assessmentId and jobId
    R->>DB: set node.meta.assessmentId only if still empty
    R-->>C: 202 with assessmentId and jobId

Rules:

  • Only practice nodes can have an assessment (400 otherwise).
  • A node gets at most one assessment. A second call returns 409. The final link uses a conditional UPDATE ... WHERE meta->>'assessmentId' IS NULL, so two parallel calls cannot both win.
  • Covered topics are the knowledge nodes in meta.coversNodeIds. If that list is empty, it uses every knowledge node with a lower positionIndex. Only resolved nodes are used, so the test never covers material the learner has not reached.
  • If no covered node is resolved yet, the call returns 409 ("Complete at least one knowledge node...").
  • Skipped topics are marked "(self-declared)" in the prompt, so the AI checks them instead of assuming them.
  • The prompt is capped at 5,000 characters. Topics that do not fit are dropped, and a warning is logged.
  • The assessment is a normal solo assessment (maxParticipants = 1). Its question generation follows Assessment Generation.

docs.title: 4.5 Notepad
docs.text: GET and PUT /v1/roadmaps/:id/notepad read and overwrite one free-text note per roadmap (up to 20,000 characters). The notepad can be written in any roadmap status.

docs.title: 4.6 Templates
docs.text:
A template is a reusable starting goal. It has uid (a public 8-character id), slug, name, description, goal, visibility (public or private), and isActive.

  • GET /v1/roadmap-templates is public (no login). It lists only active public templates, with cursor paging and an optional search on name and description.
  • Any logged-in user can create a template. It is private by default, and the caller owns it.
  • Only the owner can update or delete it. Delete is a soft delete.
  • The slug comes from the name unless one is given. It must be unique (409 otherwise).
  • A template does not create a roadmap by itself. The client takes the template's goal text and sends it to POST /v1/roadmaps.

Seeding: npm run seed:roadmap-templates runs src/scripts/seed-learning-roadmap-templates.ts. It reads the seed list from src/config/database/dummy-data/learning-roadmap-templates. It is idempotent by slug: existing templates are skipped and never changed. Flags: --owner-email <email> (defaults to the system user) and --dry-run.

docs.title: 5. Lifecycle
docs.text:
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> analyzing: POST /v1/roadmaps
    analyzing --> draft: analysis job completed
    analyzing --> failed: analysis failed or publish failed
    draft --> generating: requirement answers submitted
    generating --> active: graph saved
    generating --> failed: generation failed or publish failed
    active --> modifying: graph modify requested
    modifying --> active: revision applied
    modifying --> active: revision failed, old graph kept
    active --> completed: last node resolved
    completed --> active: a node is un-resolved
    failed --> analyzing: analysis job retried
    failed --> generating: generation job retried

Notes:

  • A failed modification returns the roadmap to active, never failed. The old graph is still there because the database transaction rolled back.
  • A completed roadmap cannot be revised. A modify request returns 409.
  • archived exists in the enum and blocks modification, but no code path sets it today.
  • A failed roadmap can recover only by retrying its failed job with POST /v1/jobs/:id/retry. The consumer sets the in-flight status again when it picks up the retried message.

Node status: not_started → in_progress → completed or skipped. The learner may set any of the four at any time.

docs.title: 6. Rules and edge cases
docs.text:
Situation Behaviour Read a roadmap that belongs to someone else 404. The userId filter is part of the query, so the API does not reveal that it exists. Write (answers, modify) to someone else's roadmap 404 if missing, 403 if it belongs to another user. Submit answers while still analyzing 409 "Analysis still in progress". Submit answers after generation started 409 "Generation already started". Modify when status is not active 409 with a reason (no graph yet, already modifying, archived, completed). affectedNodes includes a node from another roadmap 400. AI title longer than 255 characters Cut to 255 before saving. Revision removes the learner's current node The cursor moves to the nearest surviving ancestor in the old graph. If none exists, it moves to the new entry node. Regeneration applyGeneration deletes all old nodes and edges first, so graphs never stack. GET /:id/graph before generation 200 with empty nodes and edges and the current status, so the client can show a "pending" state. Client lost the job id GET /v1/roadmaps/:id returns the roadmap with its job ids in meta.

Every roadmap job payload includes userId. This matters because JobsService.findOne uses payload.userId to decide who may poll a job.

docs.title: 7. Endpoints summary
docs.text:
Full details are in API v1.

Method and path Purpose Rate limit POST /v1/roadmaps Create and start analysis (202) CLASS_B, scope AI_GENERATION, cost 3 POST /v1/roadmaps/:id/requirement-collection Submit answers, start generation (202) CLASS_B, AI_GENERATION, cost 5 POST /v1/roadmaps/:id/graph/modify Natural-language revision (202) CLASS_B, AI_GENERATION, cost 5 GET /v1/roadmaps List own roadmaps (cursor paging, status filter, progress counts) CLASS_B GET /v1/roadmaps/:id Detail, questions, job ids CLASS_B GET /v1/roadmaps/:id/graph Full graph CLASS_B GET /v1/roadmaps/:id/nodes/:nodeId One node with incoming and outgoing node ids CLASS_B PUT /v1/roadmaps/:id/nodes/:nodeId/progress Set node status CLASS_B POST /v1/roadmaps/:id/nodes/:nodeId/assessments Generate practice assessment (202) CLASS_B, AI_GENERATION, cost 5 GET / PUT /v1/roadmaps/:id/notepad Read or replace notepad CLASS_B GET /v1/roadmap-templates Public list of templates CLASS_B (by IP when not logged in) POST /v1/roadmap-templates Create template CLASS_B PATCH / DELETE /v1/roadmap-templates/:uid Owner updates or deletes CLASS_B

The AI assistant can also read roadmaps through three tools (LIST_ROADMAPS, GET_ROADMAP, GET_ROADMAP_NODE) in src/ai/tools/roadmap.tools.ts. See AI Assistant.

docs.title: 8. Async events
docs.text:
All three stages share the roadmap topic exchange, but each has its own queue. They fail in different ways, so they do not share a consumer.

Job type Routing key Queue Consumer On failure ANALYZE_ROADMAP_INTENT roadmap.analyze roadmap-analysis-queue RoadmapAnalysisConsumer roadmap failed GENERATE_ROADMAP roadmap.generate roadmap-generation-queue RoadmapGenerationConsumer roadmap failed MODIFY_ROADMAP_GRAPH roadmap.modify roadmap-modification-queue RoadmapModificationConsumer roadmap back to active
  • jobs.queue is roadmap for all three. maxAttempts is 3.
  • Each consumer catches every error, marks the job failed, and acks the message. RabbitMQ does not redeliver it. A retry is always manual through POST /v1/jobs/:id/retry.
  • Progress text for the client is written to jobs.status_description (for example "Analyzing learning intent", then "Saving requirement questions").
  • No Socket.IO events are sent for roadmaps. Clients poll the job.

docs.title: 9. Where the code lives
docs.text: Path What it does src/learning-roadmaps/learning-roadmaps.controller.ts Roadmap HTTP endpoints src/learning-roadmaps/learning-roadmaps.service.ts Create, answers, modify (job producers), reads, progress, notepad, assistant reads src/learning-roadmaps/roadmap-graph.service.ts Graph validation, apply generation, apply diff, cursor re-anchoring, graph response building src/learning-roadmaps/learning-roadmap-assessment.service.ts Practice-node assessment generation src/learning-roadmaps/learning-roadmap-templates.controller.ts and .service.ts Templates src/learning-roadmaps/consumers/ The three RabbitMQ consumers src/learning-roadmaps/interfaces/ Job payloads, RoadmapMeta, planned-graph types src/learning-roadmaps/serializers/learning-roadmaps.serializer.ts Response shapes src/learning-roadmaps/tdd.md The original technical design (referenced as "TDD §x" in code comments) src/ai/roadmap-ai.service.ts LLM calls for analyse, generate, modify src/common/enums/learning-roadmaps.enums.ts RoadmapStatus, NodeStatus, NodeType, RoadmapTemplateVisibility src/scripts/seed-learning-roadmap-templates.ts Template seeder

docs.title: 10. Known gaps and TODOs
docs.text:
• No archived transition. The status exists and is checked, but no endpoint archives a roadmap. There is also no delete endpoint for roadmaps.
  • Quota is not refunded on failure. create spends AI_LEARNING_ROADMAP before the job runs. If publishing or analysis fails, the unit is not given back. (Assessment generation does refund through usageService.release.)
  • Consumers do not check if a job is still claimable. Unlike the evaluation and invitation-import workers, the roadmap consumers call markProcessing without isClaimable. A redelivered message for a settled job would be processed again.
  • Edge conditions are not enforced. meta.condition on edges (for example a minimum score) is stored, but nothing reads it.
  • getResolvedNodes is unused. It exists in LearningRoadmapsService but no controller or tool calls it.
  • Feature flag is UI-only. The learning_roadmaps flag hides the section in the client, but these endpoints do not check it (see Platform Services).
  • Debug logging. Both the analysis and generation consumers contain a leftover console.log of the full LLM output.

docs.title: 1. Purpose
docs.text:
The notifications module sends every email the platform sends. Today email is the only channel. There is no SMS, push or in-app inbox. (For live browser updates, see Realtime Events.)

The module has three jobs:

  1. Send email through SMTP (EmailService).
  2. Render emails from typed, code-based templates that share one layout.
  3. Preview those templates for admins, without sending anything (EmailPreviewService and the admin controller).

The emails carry the product brand RealPrep in subjects, header and footer.

docs.title: 2. Key concepts
docs.text: Term Meaning Transport The SMTP connection made with nodemailer. One is created when the app starts. Template A TypeScript function such as buildVerificationEmail(data) that returns { subject, html, text }. Templates are code, not database rows. Content What a template produces before the layout is added: subject, preheader, category, footnote, a list of blocks, and plain-text lines. Block A reusable body piece from email-blocks.ts: intro, paragraph, primaryAction (button), divider, linkFallback, callout, steps, detailPanel, prose. Layout renderEmail() wraps content in the shared page, header (wordmark plus category) and footer, for both HTML and plain text. Theme email-theme.ts copies the frontend design tokens as literal values, because CSS variables do not work in most mail clients. Fire-and-forget The caller starts the send but does not wait for it. A failure is logged and never fails the user's request.

docs.title: 3. Data
docs.text:
The module has no tables of its own. Templates live in code under src/notifications/email/templates/. There are no database-stored email templates. The "email templates" admin API only lists and previews the code templates.

Related data owned by other modules:

  • users.is_newsletter_subscribe decides who gets newsletters.
  • users.last_verification_email_sent_at throttles verification resends.
  • The newsletters table holds newsletter content and delivery counts (see Platform Services).

See ERD.

docs.title: 4. Configuration
docs.text:
Env var Required Default Use SMTP_HOST Yes – SMTP server SMTP_PORT No 587 SMTP port SMTP_SECURE No false true for implicit TLS (port 465) SMTP_USER / SMTP_PASSWORD Yes – SMTP login EMAIL_FROM Yes – The From address on every email FRONTEND_URL No https://app.testflow.com Base for every link in emails

The provider is whatever SMTP server these point to. No provider-specific SDK is used. If a required value is missing, the app fails at startup because EmailService uses getOrThrow.

docs.title: 5. The template system
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    Caller["Caller, for example AuthService"] --> ES["EmailService.sendXxxEmail"]
    ES --> Build["buildXxxEmail data"]
    Build --> Content["EmailContent: subject, blocks, textLines"]
    Content --> Layout["renderEmail: header, body, footer"]
    Layout --> Rendered["subject, html, text"]
    Rendered --> Send["EmailService.sendEmail"]
    Send --> SMTP["nodemailer SMTP transport"]

How to read the files:

  • templates/<name>-email.template.ts: one file per email. Each exports a build<Name>EmailContent (content only) and a build<Name>Email (content plus layout).
  • templates/email-blocks.ts: body building blocks. Everything is table-based HTML with inline styles, because that is the only thing every mail client renders the same way. User-supplied text is passed through escapeHtml.
  • templates/layout/: email-layout.ts (renderEmail), email-header.ts, email-footer.ts, email-styles.ts (one <style> block for dark mode and small screens) and email-layout.constants.ts.
  • templates/email-theme.ts: colours, fonts and spacing.
  • email-template-previews.ts: sample data for each template, used only by the preview API.

To add a new email:

  1. Create templates/<name>-email.template.ts using blocks and renderEmail.
  2. Add a send<Name>Email method to EmailService that builds the links and calls sendEmail.
  3. Add an entry to EMAIL_TEMPLATE_PREVIEWS so admins can preview it.

docs.title: 6. Every email the system sends
docs.text:
Found by searching every caller of EmailService in src/.

Email Trigger Template Recipient Sync or async On failure Email verification Signup (AuthService.signup). Also on login with correct credentials while unverified, if the last link has expired (resendVerificationEmailIfDue). verification-email.template.ts. Link: FRONTEND_URL/verify-email?token=... The new user Fire-and-forget Logged. The send time is still recorded, so a broken mailer is not retried on every login. Welcome Email verified for the first time (AuthService.verifyEmail) welcome-email.template.ts. Link: FRONTEND_URL The user Fire-and-forget Logged Welcome with credentials First Google sign-in that creates a new account (AuthService.googleLogin). Includes the generated username and password. welcome-email.template.ts (credentials variant) The new user Fire-and-forget Logged Password reset POST forgot-password, only if the user exists and is active (AuthService.requestPasswordReset) password-reset-email.template.ts. Link: FRONTEND_URL/reset-password?token=... and expiry in minutes The user Fire-and-forget Logged by user id. The API always returns the same message, so it does not reveal whether the email exists. Assessment invitation Owner invites participants to a personal assessment (AssessmentInvitationsService, src/assessments/assessment-invitations.service.ts) assessment-invitation-email.template.ts. New users go to /signup?email=..., others to /assessments/:id. Each invitee Fire-and-forget, one per invitee Logged by assessment id. The invitation stays. Organization invitation Admin invites members by list (OrganizationMembersService.inviteMany) or by CSV import (background job) organization-invitation-email.template.ts. New users go to /signup?email=..., others to /invitations. Each invitee Awaited, 10 at a time (OrganizationInvitationMailer) Collected and returned as emailsFailed in the API or job result. The invitation stays. Newsletter Newsletter scheduler tick or "send now" (NewslettersDispatchService) newsletter-email.template.ts with the admin's HTML body All active, subscribed, not-deleted users, in pages of 100 by BCC Background (cron) A failed page counts all its recipients as failed. If every recipient fails, the newsletter is marked FAILED.

Notes:

  • Auth flows are covered in Auth. Invitations are covered in Assessments and Organizations.
  • Signup without a later verification gives a user only the verification email. The welcome email is sent after verification.

docs.title: 7.1 Fire-and-forget send (most emails)
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant U as User
    participant A as AuthService
    participant E as EmailService
    participant S as SMTP server

    U->>A: POST signup
    A->>A: create user and tokens
    A->>E: sendVerificationEmail, not awaited
    A-->>U: 201 with tokens
    E->>E: build template and layout
    E->>S: sendMail
    alt SMTP error
        E->>E: log error, throw 503
        Note over A,E: the caller only logs the error
    else ok
        S-->>E: messageId
    end

docs.title: 7.2 Awaited batch send (organization invitations)
docs.text: OrganizationInvitationMailer.sendInvitations sends invitations in batches of 10 with Promise.allSettled. It waits for each batch. Failed addresses are returned to the caller, and a failed email never undoes the invitation. For the CSV import, these counts go into the job result and the org.invitations.import.settled socket event.

docs.title: 7.3 Newsletter batches
docs.text: NewslettersDispatchService loads subscribers 100 at a time (NEWSLETTER_RECIPIENT_BATCH_SIZE). For each page it sends one email with every address in bcc, so recipients never see each other. See Platform Services for the full lifecycle.

docs.title: 8. Sync vs queued sending
docs.text:
There is no email queue. Nothing goes through RabbitMQ just to send email, and there is no outbox table.

Style Used by What it means Fire-and-forget in the request Verification, welcome, password reset, assessment invitation The HTTP response does not wait. If the process dies, the email is lost. Awaited in the request Organization invitations from the HTTP endpoint The response waits for all sends and reports failures. Awaited in a background worker Organization invitations from CSV import (RabbitMQ job), newsletters (cron) Slow sends do not block any user request.

docs.title: 9. Failure handling
docs.text:
• EmailService.sendEmail logs every attempt and its messageId. On any SMTP error, it logs the stack and throws ServiceUnavailableException('Email delivery is temporarily unavailable').
  • Callers decide what a failure means. Every caller treats email as best-effort. The main action (signup, invitation) is never rolled back because an email failed.
  • There is no automatic retry of a failed email. Users can trigger some again themselves: log in again to get a new verification link after the old one expires, or request another password reset.
  • Logging rules: newer code logs user ids or assessment ids, not addresses (logging conventions keep email addresses out of logs).

docs.title: 10. Endpoints summary
docs.text:
Admin-only. Full details are in API v1.

Method and path Permission Purpose GET /v1/admin/email-templates newsletters:read List previewable templates: key, name, description GET /v1/admin/email-templates/:key/preview newsletters:read Render one template with sample data. Returns subject, html, text. POST /v1/admin/newsletters/preview newsletters:create Render a newsletter draft (see Platform Services) GET /v1/admin/newsletters/:id/preview newsletters:read Render a saved newsletter

Template keys: welcome, welcome-google, verification, password-reset, assessment-invitation, assessment-invitation-signup, organization-invitation, organization-invitation-signup, newsletter.

Previews need no SMTP settings. EmailPreviewService is separate from EmailService for this reason. All these routes use the CLASS_C rate limit.

docs.title: 11. Async events
docs.text: The module publishes and consumes no RabbitMQ messages and emits no socket events. It is called directly by other services.

docs.title: 12. Where the code lives
docs.text: Path What it does src/notifications/notifications.module.ts Exports EmailService and EmailPreviewService src/notifications/email/email.service.ts SMTP transport and one send...Email method per email src/notifications/email/email-preview.service.ts Renders previews src/notifications/email/email-template-previews.ts Sample data per template key src/notifications/email/templates/ Templates, blocks, theme, layout src/notifications/email-templates-admin.controller.ts Admin preview endpoints src/organizations/services/organization-invitation-mailer.service.ts Batched organization invitation sends src/newsletters/newsletters-dispatch.service.ts Newsletter sending

docs.title: 13. Known gaps and TODOs
docs.text:
• No queue or outbox. Fire-and-forget emails are lost if the process restarts mid-send, and nothing retries them.
  • No delivery tracking. Bounces, complaints and opens are not recorded. A "sent" status only means the SMTP server accepted it.
  • Users cannot opt out of newsletters. users.is_newsletter_subscribe defaults to true, and no endpoint or service ever changes it (src/common/entities/user.entity.ts:76). There is also no unsubscribe link in the newsletter email.
  • Email addresses in some logs. AuthService still logs the address when welcome and verification emails fail (src/identity/auth/auth.service.ts:276 and :374). This goes against the logging conventions that newer code follows.
  • Brand naming. Templates say "RealPrep" while the code base and docs say "TestFlow". The default FRONTEND_URL is app.testflow.com.
  • Newsletter HTML is not sanitised. The admin's bodyHtml is inserted as-is (prose(bodyHtml)). This is fine while only trusted admins can write newsletters.

docs.title: 1. Purpose
docs.text:
An organization ("org") is a group of users who work together. Examples are a company, a college or a coaching class. Inside an org:

  • Each member has an org role (org_owner, org_admin or org_member) that decides what they may do there.
  • Members can create org assessments, which belong to the org and not to one person.
  • The org has its own subscription (it starts on a 7-day trial). See Commerce.

The same user can use TestFlow personally and also act in one or more orgs. Each request says which one it is acting in. That choice is called the org context.

docs.title: 2. Key terms
docs.text: Term Meaning uid Public 8-character id of an org (for example a7Kq2Xb9). Clients always use the uid, never the numeric id. slug URL-safe name made from the org name, for example acme-labs. Unique among live orgs. Owner The user who created the org. Stored in organizations.owner_user_id, and as an org_owner membership row. Membership One row in organization_members for one user in one org, with a role and a status. Invitation A membership row with status invited. Accepting it changes the same row to active. There is no separate invitations table. Placeholder account An unverified user account created for an invitee who has no account yet. Its username starts with invited_. When the person later signs up (or uses Google) with that email, they take over this row. See Auth. Org context request.org = { orgId, memberId, roleId }. OrgContextGuard sets it when a request acts in an org. Org-scoped route A route under /v1/orgs/:orgUid/... marked @OrgScoped(). It always acts in that org. Header-scoped route A route marked @OrgHeaderScoped(). It acts in an org only if the x-organization-id header is sent. Otherwise it is personal.

docs.title: 3. Data it uses
docs.text:
See the ERD for full definitions.

Table Notes organizations uid, slug, name, owner_user_id, status (active or suspended), soft delete. uid and slug are unique among live rows. organization_members organization_id, user_id, role_id, status (invited, active, suspended), invited_by, joined_at, soft delete. One live row per user per org. A soft-deleted row does not block a new invite. roles The built-in org roles. See RBAC. jobs One row per bulk CSV import (type = IMPORT_ORG_INVITATIONS). See Jobs and schedulers. subscriptions The org's trial subscription is created with the org. See Commerce. assessments.organization_id Set for org assessments. NULL for personal ones. See Assessments.

The uploaded CSV files are stored in S3 (or MinIO or LocalStack in development) under org-invitations/<orgId>/<uuid>.csv, by StorageService in src/storage/storage.service.ts.

docs.title: 4. Creating an organization
docs.text:
1. A signed-in user calls POST /v1/orgs with { name, slug? }.
  2. Org limit: a user can own at most 1 org (OrganizationLimit.ORG_LIMIT). Otherwise the server returns 409.
  3. The slug is the one given, or it is made from the name (slugify). If the slug is already taken, the server returns 409.
  4. In one transaction, the server:
    • inserts the org with a new random uid and status active
    • inserts an active org_owner membership for the creator
    • creates the org's 7-day trial subscription (SubscriptionsService.createOrgTrialSubscription)
  5. If the random uid collides with an existing one, the whole transaction is retried, up to 5 times.

A platform admin can do the same thing for another user with POST /v1/admin/organizations and { name, slug?, ownerEmail }. The owner must have an account and must be active. The result is the same as if that user had created the org.

Updating (PATCH /v1/orgs/:orgUid, needs org_settings:update): you can change name and slug. If you change the name and do not send a slug, the slug is made again from the new name.

docs.title: 5. Invitations
docs.text:
There is one invite endpoint. It takes a list of 1 to 50 people. Inviting one person means sending a list with one entry. (A separate single-invite route was removed on branch feat/bulk-invite in commit c289b17.) For larger lists there is a CSV import that runs as a background job.

Both paths end in the same method, OrganizationMembersService.inviteMany.

docs.title: 5.1 What inviteMany does
docs.text:
Input: { invitees: [{ name, email }, ...] }. Names and emails are trimmed.

  1. Every invitee gets the role org_member. You cannot pick another role at invite time.
  2. Duplicate emails in the list are merged, ignoring case. The first spelling wins.
  3. The server finds existing accounts by email, ignoring case.
  4. For each person:
    • Already an active or suspended member: skipped with reason already_member.
    • Already invited: skipped with reason already_invited.
    • Has an account (verified or not): invited as they are.
    • Has no account: a placeholder account is created. It is unverified, the username is invited_<random>, the password is a random 24-character one that nobody sees, and the name comes from the invite.
  5. In one transaction, the server creates the placeholder accounts and inserts the invited membership rows (invited_by = the caller).
  6. If someone else invited or signed up one of these people at the same moment, a unique index fails and the server returns 409 ... please retry. Nothing is saved.
  7. After the commit, the server sends one email per new invitation, 10 at a time (OrganizationInvitationMailer). A failed email does not undo the invitation. It is listed in emailsFailed.

The response has invited (member rows), accountsCreated (emails), skipped (email and reason) and emailsFailed.

docs.title: 5.2 Invite and accept
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant A as Org admin
    participant API as OrganizationInvitationsController
    participant MS as OrganizationMembersService
    participant DB as Postgres
    participant ML as InvitationMailer
    participant I as Invitee
    A->>API: POST /v1/orgs/:orgUid/invitations with invitees
    Note over API: OrgContextGuard and the org_members create permission run first
    API->>MS: inviteMany(org, actorId, dto)
    MS->>DB: find users by email, find existing memberships
    MS->>DB: BEGIN, create placeholder users, insert invited rows, COMMIT
    MS->>ML: sendInvitations
    ML-->>I: email with sign up link or view invitation link
    MS-->>A: 201 invited, accountsCreated, skipped, emailsFailed
    opt invitee has no usable account
        I->>API: sign up or Google sign-in with the same email, then verify
        Note over I: Takes over the placeholder row, so the invite is kept
    end
    I->>API: GET /v1/orgs/invitations
    API-->>I: pending invitations
    alt accept
        I->>API: POST /v1/orgs/:orgUid/invitation/accept
        API->>DB: status active, joined_at now
        API-->>I: 204
    else decline
        I->>API: DELETE /v1/orgs/:orgUid/invitation
        API->>DB: soft delete the row
        API-->>I: 204
    end

The email link depends on whether an account was just created for the invitee:

  • Account created now: "Sign up to accept" → FRONTEND_URL/signup?email=...
  • Account already existed: "View invitation" → FRONTEND_URL/invitations

The invitee must be verified to call the accept or decline routes, because the auth guard rejects unverified accounts (see Auth).

docs.title: 5.3 Bulk invite by CSV
docs.text:
1. GET /v1/orgs/:orgUid/invitations/import/sample downloads a sample file. Its contents are just the header name,email.
  2. POST /v1/orgs/:orgUid/invitations/import with a multipart field file:
    • at most 1 MB
    • type text/csv, application/csv, text/plain or application/vnd.ms-excel (CSV has no magic bytes, so only the MIME type is checked)
  3. The server stores the file in S3, creates a jobs row (status PENDING, maxAttempts 3, createdBy = the caller) and publishes a message to RabbitMQ. It returns 202 Accepted with the job.
  4. If publishing fails, the job is marked failed and the server returns 503.
  5. OrganizationInvitationImportConsumer receives the message and calls OrganizationInvitationImportService.run:
    1. Claim the job. Drop the message if the job is missing, has the wrong type, or is already finished (a redelivery).
    2. Re-check the uploader with resolveContext. They must still be an active member, and the org must not be suspended.
    3. Read and parse the file (parseInvitationCsv):
      • The header row must have name and email, in any case. Other columns are ignored.
      • At most 5000 data rows. An empty file or a file without the right header fails the whole job.
      • A bad row (it fails InviteeDto validation) goes to failed with its line number.
      • A repeated email goes to skipped as duplicate_in_file.
    4. Invite in chunks of 50 through inviteMany. After each chunk, the job's progress text is updated ("Invited 50 of 320"). If a chunk hits a 409 conflict, it is tried once more. If it fails again, its rows go to failed.
    5. Mark the job completed with a result: totalRows, invited, accountsCreated, skipped[], failed[], emailsFailed[].
    6. Emit the socket event org.invitations.import.settled to the uploader.
  6. Any other error marks the job failed and emits the same event with status: failed. The message is still acknowledged, so it is not redelivered forever. To retry, call POST /v1/jobs/:id/retry. Re-running is safe, because people already invited are skipped and are not emailed again.
  7. The client polls GET /v1/jobs/:id, or listens for the socket event.
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant A as Org admin
    participant API as InvitationsController
    participant IS as ImportService
    participant S3 as S3 storage
    participant DB as Postgres
    participant MQ as RabbitMQ
    participant CO as ImportConsumer
    participant MS as MembersService
    participant WS as EventsGateway
    A->>API: POST /v1/orgs/:orgUid/invitations/import with CSV file
    API->>IS: enqueue
    IS->>S3: putObject org-invitations/orgId/uuid.csv
    IS->>DB: insert job IMPORT_ORG_INVITATIONS, PENDING
    IS->>MQ: publish to organization exchange
    API-->>A: 202 job
    MQ->>CO: organization.invitations.import message
    CO->>IS: run(message)
    IS->>DB: claim job, mark PROCESSING
    IS->>MS: resolveContext for uploader
    IS->>S3: getObject
    IS->>IS: parse CSV, split into valid, invalid, duplicate rows
    loop each chunk of 50 rows
        IS->>MS: inviteMany(chunk)
        MS->>DB: placeholder users and invited rows
        MS-->>MS: send invitation emails
        IS->>DB: update job progress
    end
    IS->>DB: mark job COMPLETED with result
    IS->>WS: org.invitations.import.settled to uploader
    A->>API: GET /v1/jobs/:id
    API-->>A: job status, progress and result

RabbitMQ wiring (src/config/rabbitmq/rabbitmq.constants.ts):

Item Value Exchange organization (topic) Routing key organization.invitations.import Queue organization-invitation-import-queue Job queue name stored on the job row organization-invitations Job type IMPORT_ORG_INVITATIONS

docs.title: 6. Members
docs.text:
Action Route Permission Rules List GET /v1/orgs/:orgUid/members org_members:read Cursor-paged, newest first. Optional status filter. Includes pending invitations. meta has nextCursor and total. Change role or status PATCH /v1/orgs/:orgUid/members/:userId org_members:update roleKey can be any built-in org role except org_owner. status can be active or suspended. An invitation cannot be activated this way, only by the invitee accepting it. Remove member or revoke invite DELETE /v1/orgs/:orgUid/members/:userId org_members:delete Soft-deletes the row. Leave DELETE /v1/orgs/:orgUid/membership none (active member) The owner cannot leave.

For both PATCH and DELETE, you cannot target yourself, and you cannot target the owner (403).

A suspended member stays in the list, but cannot act in the org at all, because OrgContextGuard requires status active.

docs.title: 7. Org context: how a request picks its organization
docs.text:
OrgContextGuard (src/organizations/guards/org-context.guard.ts) runs after JwtAuthGuard, RateLimitGuard and RolesGuard, and before PermissionGuard. So the permission check can already see request.org.

There are two ways a route can ask for an org:

Decorator Where the org uid comes from If it is missing @OrgScoped() Route param :orgUid Not possible, because it is part of the path @OrgHeaderScoped() Header x-organization-id The request stays personal. request.org is not set.

Steps:

  1. If the route has neither decorator, do nothing.
  2. Read the uid from the param or the header. A header-scoped route with no header (or an empty one) continues as personal.
  3. Call OrganizationMembersService.resolveContext(uid, userId). It looks for an active membership of this user in the org with this uid.
    • No such membership (not a member, only invited, suspended member, or no such org): 404 Organization not found. It is 404 and not 403 so that outsiders cannot find out which orgs exist.
    • The org is suspended: 403 This organization has been suspended.
  4. Set request.org = { orgId, memberId, roleId }.

Handlers read it with:

  • @CurrentOrg(): returns the context. It throws a 500 if used on a route that is not org-scoped (a programming error).
  • @OptionalOrg(): returns the context or null. Used on header-scoped routes.
flowchart TD
    A["Request after JwtAuthGuard"] --> B{"OrgScoped or OrgHeaderScoped?"}
    B -- neither --> P["Personal request, continue"]
    B -- OrgScoped --> C["uid from path param orgUid"]
    B -- OrgHeaderScoped --> D{"x-organization-id header sent?"}
    D -- no --> P
    D -- yes --> E["uid from header"]
    C --> F["resolveContext: find ACTIVE membership by uid and user"]
    E --> F
    F --> G{"Active membership found?"}
    G -- no --> N["404 Organization not found"]
    G -- yes --> H{"Org suspended?"}
    H -- yes --> S["403 Organization suspended"]
    H -- no --> R["Set request.org to orgId, memberId, roleId"]
    R --> PG["PermissionGuard checks the org role"]

docs.title: 7.1 Org-scoped permissions
docs.text:
When request.org is set, PermissionGuard checks permissions against the member's org role only. Platform roles, including super_admin, give nothing inside an org. @OrgPermissions(...) adds keys that are checked only in org mode. The full logic and the default grants for each org role are in RBAC.

Routes that use the header today:

  • Assessments: create, generate, list, invite, participants, register, and more. They use @OrgPermissions('org_assessments:read' or 'create'). See Assessments.
  • Attempt review and leaderboard. See Attempts.
  • Billing: GET /v1/subscriptions and GET /v1/usage/subscriptions/:subscriptionId, with @OrgPermissions('org_billing:read'). See Commerce.

docs.title: 8. Org assessments and participants
docs.text:
The assessment side is covered in Assessments. These are the points that matter for orgs:

  1. An assessment created with the x-organization-id header gets organization_id set, and belongs to the org.
  2. Schedule: an org assessment has two windows, added on branch feat/bulk-invite (commit 514f2bd, migration add-registration-window-to-assessments):
    • Registration window (registrationStartTime to registrationEndTime): when people can register or be invited. If not given, it opens now and closes when the attempt window closes.
    • Attempt window (attemptStartTime to attemptEndTime): required for org assessments.
    • Rules: each window must end after it starts, and registration cannot close after the attempt window ends.
    • A personal assessment ignores these inputs. Both of its windows are "now plus 30 days".
  3. Only active org members can be invited to an org assessment. Others come back as skipped.
  4. Participant details (GET /v1/assessments/:id/participants, added in commits d442e37 and cc7ffd0) list everyone invited, active or revoked. Each row has the account details, isCreator, invitedBy, invitedAt, inviteAcceptedAt and revokedAt. There are status and search filters, and meta.counts gives the number in each status. Only the creator, or a member whose org role has org_assessments:update, may see it.
  5. DELETE /v1/assessments/:id/participants/:userId removes a participant or revokes an invite. The creator cannot be removed.

docs.title: 9.1 Organization
docs.text:
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> active: POST /v1/orgs or admin create
    active --> suspended: admin PATCH status
    suspended --> active: admin PATCH status

When an org is suspended:

  • Every org-scoped or header-scoped request for it returns 403.
  • Its pending invitations are hidden from GET /v1/orgs/invitations and cannot be accepted.
  • It still shows in GET /v1/orgs, with an empty permissions list.

There is no delete endpoint for organizations.

docs.title: 9.2 Membership
docs.text:
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> invited: inviteMany
    [*] --> active: owner row at org creation
    invited --> active: invitee accepts
    invited --> removed: invitee declines or admin revokes
    active --> suspended: admin PATCH status
    suspended --> active: admin PATCH status
    active --> removed: admin removes or member leaves
    suspended --> removed: admin removes
    removed --> [*]
    note right of removed
        Soft deleted row.
        The person can be invited again.
    end note

docs.title: 10. Business rules and edge cases
docs.text:
1. A user can own at most one org. They can be a member of any number.
  2. Each org has exactly one owner. org_owner can never be granted through the API, and the owner's membership can never be changed or removed. There is no ownership transfer endpoint.
  3. Invites always use the role org_member. Promote people afterwards with PATCH .../members/:userId.
  4. An org_admin can change or remove another org_admin. There is no rank check between admins.
  5. Emails are matched ignoring case when inviting, but login and sign-up match them exactly (see Auth).
  6. A person with an account who has never verified it (for example, a placeholder from another org's invite) gets the "View invitation" email, not the "Sign up" one.
  7. Re-inviting after a decline, revoke, removal or leave works, because the unique index ignores soft-deleted rows.
  8. The import job re-checks only that the uploader is still an active member. It does not re-check that they still have org_members:create.
  9. Each invite request is limited to 50 people. Each CSV is limited to 5000 rows and 1 MB.
  10. A failed invitation email never fails the invite.
  11. There is no limit on how many members an org can have.

docs.title: 11. Endpoints summary
docs.text: The API reference has the full details.

docs.text:
Method and path Permission Purpose POST /v1/admin/organizations organizations:create Create an org for the user with ownerEmail GET /v1/admin/organizations organizations:read Cursor-paged list. Filters: search (name, slug), status. GET /v1/admin/organizations/:orgUid organizations:read One org PATCH /v1/admin/organizations/:orgUid/status organizations:update Suspend or reactivate

Admin routes are personal requests. They use platform permissions, and the admin does not need to be a member of the org.

docs.text: Kind Name When RabbitMQ consumer OrganizationInvitationImportConsumer (src/organizations/consumers/organization-invitation-import.consumer.ts) A CSV import is queued Job IMPORT_ORG_INVITATIONS One per CSV upload. Poll GET /v1/jobs/:id, retry with POST /v1/jobs/:id/retry. docs.title: 13. Where the code lives
