docs.title: 14. Known gaps and TODOs
docs.text:
1. No ownership transfer and no org delete. The owner can never leave.
  2. Uploaded CSV files are never deleted from S3 after the import finishes.
  3. The maxAttempts: 3 on import jobs is not used for automatic retries. A failure is final until someone calls the retry endpoint.
  4. No member limit and no seat billing for orgs.
  5. The wrong email for existing unverified accounts (rule 6). Those people get "View invitation" but cannot log in until they sign up.
  6. The import does not re-check permission (rule 8).
  7. No rank check between admins (rule 4).
  8. A suspended member cannot leave the org, because leave is org-scoped and needs an active membership.
  9. Changing the name changes the slug unless a slug is also sent. This may break saved links that use the slug.
  10. Admin org creation does not check that the owner is verified.

docs.title: Platform Services
docs.text:
This page covers the small modules that support the rest of the platform. Each section follows the same shape: what it is for, how it works, its endpoints, and its known gaps.

Module Folder One-line summary Feature flags src/feature-flags/ Admin-controlled on/off switches, optionally limited to platform roles Rate limiter src/rate-limiter/ Redis token bucket, applied per route with @RateLimit() Stats src/stats/ One admin endpoint with platform-wide numbers Newsletters src/newsletters/ Admins write and schedule an email to all subscribers Support tickets src/support-tickets/ Users open tickets, admins change their status Health src/health/ Checks Postgres, Redis and RabbitMQ Storage src/storage/ Thin S3 wrapper App controller src/app.controller.ts GET /ping

All admin routes live under /v1/admin/... and are protected by @Permissions('<resource>:<action>'). The global PermissionGuard checks these. See RBAC.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: A feature flag is a switch that turns a product feature on or off without a deploy. Admins can turn a flag off for everyone (a kill switch) or limit it to some platform roles (for example, only super_admin while testing).

docs.title: Model
docs.text:
• Flags are defined in code. FeatureFlagKey and FEATURE_FLAG_DEFINITIONS in src/feature-flags/feature-flag.constants.ts list every flag with its description, defaultEnabled and defaultRoles.
  • State is stored in the database. feature_flags has one row per flag (key, description, enabled, updated_by). feature_flag_roles links a flag to the platform roles it is limited to. See ERD.
  • No row means the code default applies. The seeder (src/seeders/feature-flag.seeder.ts) adds missing rows in their default state and never changes rows that already exist.
Key Controls Default coding_questions Coding question types in the composer and templates. A kill switch for coding generation. On for everyone learning_roadmaps The learning roadmaps section: pages and navigation On for everyone

docs.title: Evaluation rules
docs.text:
isFlagOn(state, userRoleKeys):

  1. If enabled is false → off for everyone.
  2. If the flag has no roles → on for everyone.
  3. Otherwise → on only if the user holds any of the flag's roles.

Only platform roles can be used. Organization roles are rejected with 400. A soft-deleted role is ignored.

docs.title: How code checks a flag
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant C as Client
    participant A as AuthService.getMe
    participant F as FeatureFlagsService
    participant R as AccessControlService
    participant DB as Postgres

    C->>A: GET /v1/auth/me
    A->>F: enabledFor userId
    F->>DB: load all flag rows with roles
    F->>R: getUserRoleKeys userId
    F-->>A: list of flag keys that are on
    A-->>C: profile with featureFlags array
    Note over A,F: if the read fails, code defaults are returned instead

The only consumer is GET /me, which returns featureFlags: FeatureFlagKey[]. The client hides or shows features from that list. No server endpoint checks a flag today. There is no guard or decorator for flags.

docs.title: Admin API
docs.text: Method and path Permission Purpose GET /v1/admin/feature-flags feature_flags:read Every flag in code with its current state GET /v1/admin/feature-flags/:key feature_flags:read One flag (404 for unknown keys) PATCH /v1/admin/feature-flags/:key feature_flags:update Body { enabled?, roleKeys? }. Creates the row if missing. roleKeys replaces the whole role list. [] means everyone.

docs.title: Gaps
docs.text:
• Flags are not enforced on the server. Turning off learning_roadmaps or coding_questions hides the UI, but the API endpoints still work for a client that calls them directly.
  • No caching. Every GET /me reads the flag tables.
  • No per-user or percentage rollout. Targeting is by platform role only.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: The rate limiter stops abuse and runaway clients. It protects login from password guessing and stops one user from spending too much on AI calls.

docs.title: Algorithm
docs.text:
It uses a token bucket:

  • Each bucket holds up to limit tokens and starts full.
  • Tokens refill smoothly at limit / windowSeconds per second.
  • Each request takes cost tokens (default 1). If not enough are left, the request is rejected.

The whole read-refill-decide-write step runs as one Lua script inside Redis (TOKEN_BUCKET_LUA in src/rate-limiter/algorithms.ts). Because it is atomic, two parallel requests can never both spend the same token, even across app instances. The script is registered once with defineCommand and called with EVALSHA.

The caller passes the current time, so app servers need synced clocks (NTP).

docs.title: Policies (default limits)
docs.text:
From src/rate-limiter/policies.ts:

Policy Limit Keyed by Meant for CLASS_A 10 per 5 minutes (1 token every 30s) IP Auth: login, signup, refresh, password reset CLASS_B 30 per minute User Writes: create, update, submit, AI generation CLASS_C 120 per minute User Reads, lists, polling

docs.title: Redis keys
docs.text:
rl:v1:<identifier>:<identity>:<scope>
  • identifier is user or ip.
  • identity is the user id or IP address.
  • scope is the policy name by default, so all routes with that policy share one bucket. A route can pass its own scope (for example AI_GENERATION) to get a separate bucket.
  • Each key is a hash with tokens and updatedAt. It expires once it would have refilled to full, so idle keys clean themselves up.
  • Bump v1 in RATE_LIMIT_KEY_PREFIX if the stored shape changes.

The limiter uses its own Redis client (src/rate-limiter/redis.provider.ts). It fails fast: no offline queue, 1 retry, and a 200 ms command timeout (REDIS_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_MS).

docs.title: The decorator
docs.text:
@RateLimit(POLICIES.CLASS_B, { scope: 'AI_GENERATION', cost: 5 })
  • A route with no @RateLimit is not limited. The global guard skips it.
  • The decorator can go on a controller (all routes) or on a method. The method wins.
  • AI endpoints share the AI_GENERATION scope with different costs. For example, creating a roadmap costs 3, while submitting roadmap answers, revising a roadmap or retrying a job costs 5. They all draw from the same 30-token bucket per minute.

docs.title: Request flow
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant C as Client
    participant G as RateLimitGuard
    participant P as PolicyResolver
    participant S as RateLimiterService
    participant R as Redis

    C->>G: HTTP request
    G->>G: read @RateLimit metadata, skip if none or not HTTP
    G->>P: resolve policy, request, scope
    P-->>G: policy and key
    G->>S: check with cost
    S->>R: run token bucket script
    R-->>S: allowed, remaining, retryAfterMs
    S-->>G: decision
    G->>G: set X-RateLimit-Limit and X-RateLimit-Remaining
    alt not allowed
        G-->>C: 429 with Retry-After header
    else allowed
        G->>G: continue to RolesGuard
    end

The guard runs after JwtAuthGuard, so it can key by user. If a USER policy runs on a request with no user (a @Public route), it falls back to the IP and logs a warning.

docs.title: Response on limit
docs.text:
• Status 429 Too Many Requests.
  • Body (through the global exception filter): { success: false, message: 'Rate limit exceeded. Please retry later.' }.
  • Headers on every limited response: X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining. On a 429 also: Retry-After (seconds).

docs.title: Gaps
docs.text:
• Fails open. If Redis is down, every request is allowed and an error is logged. This is a deliberate choice: a Redis outage should not take down the API.
  • IP behind a proxy. request.ip is only correct if Express trust proxy matches the deployment. Otherwise every user behind the load balancer shares one IP bucket. main.ts does not set trust proxy today.
  • Not used for WebSockets. Socket messages do not go through this guard. Code runs have their own in-memory cooldown (see Realtime Events).

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: One endpoint that feeds the admin overview page with platform-wide numbers.

docs.title: What it shows
docs.text:
GET /v1/admin/stats?days=30 (days from 7 to 90, default 30). Needs stats:read.

Section Figures range days, from, to (UTC dates, today included) users total, verified, new in period organizations total, active, suspended, new in period assessments total, personal, organization, new in period, count by status attempts total, submitted in period, average score percent (evaluated attempts in period), count by status subscriptions active, personal, organization, paid (plan price > 0) revenue successful payment totals per currency for the period, failed payment count ai LLM calls, failed calls, total cost in USD (from llm_audit) supportTickets open, in progress daily One row per day with signups, assessments created, attempts submitted, and revenue per currency. Days with no activity are filled with zeros.

docs.title: How it is computed
docs.text:
• StatsAdminService.getStats (src/stats/admin.service.ts) runs about 13 raw SQL queries in parallel with Promise.all.
  • Counts use COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE ...), so one scan gives several numbers.
  • The window is [today − (days − 1), tomorrow) in UTC.
  • The daily series uses generate_series so no day is skipped.
  • Revenue is never summed across currencies.
  • Soft-deleted users, organizations, assessments, subscriptions and tickets are excluded.
  • The average score is score / (total_questions × correct_marks), where correct_marks comes from the assessment's first section.

docs.title: Gaps
docs.text:
• No caching. Every page load runs all queries live, and the daily series uses one sub-query per day for each metric.
  • The average score assumes every section uses the same marks as the first one.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Admins write an HTML email and send it now or at a set time to every subscribed user.

docs.title: Lifecycle
docs.text:
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> SCHEDULED: admin creates, with or without scheduledAt
    SCHEDULED --> SENDING: dispatcher claims it once scheduledAt has passed
    SCHEDULED --> Cancelled: admin deletes, soft delete
    SENDING --> SENT: all pages tried, at least one delivered or no subscribers
    SENDING --> FAILED: recipient lookup failed or every recipient failed
    SENT --> [*]
    FAILED --> [*]

Cancelled is not a status value. It is a soft delete (deleted_at). A newsletter in SENDING cannot be deleted (422).

docs.title: Flow
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant Ad as Admin
    participant S as NewslettersAdminService
    participant Cr as NewsletterScheduler
    participant D as NewslettersDispatchService
    participant DB as Postgres
    participant E as EmailService

    Ad->>S: POST /v1/admin/newsletters
    S->>DB: insert SCHEDULED, scheduledAt = now if not given
    opt no scheduledAt
        S->>D: dispatchDue, not awaited
    end
    S-->>Ad: 201
    Cr->>D: dispatchDue every minute
    D->>DB: UPDATE to SENDING ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, up to 5
    loop each claimed newsletter
        loop pages of 100 subscribers
            D->>E: sendNewsletterEmail with bcc list
        end
        D->>DB: SENT or FAILED with counts
    end

Rules:

  • Who gets it: users with is_newsletter_subscribe = true, is_active = true and not soft-deleted. They are read in pages ordered by id.
  • One email per page, with all addresses in bcc. A failed page counts all its recipients as failed.
  • Claiming is safe across instances thanks to FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED. A per-instance dispatchInFlight flag stops overlapping passes.
  • Config: NEWSLETTER_DISPATCH_BATCH_SIZE (newsletters per pass, default 5), NEWSLETTER_RECIPIENT_BATCH_SIZE (default 100), NEWSLETTER_SCHEDULER_ENABLED.

See Jobs and Schedulers for the cron, and Notifications for the template.

docs.title: Endpoints
docs.text: Method and path Permission Purpose POST /v1/admin/newsletters newsletters:create Create. subject 3–200 characters, bodyHtml at least 10, optional bodyText, optional scheduledAt (ISO date). CLASS_B rate limit. POST /v1/admin/newsletters/preview newsletters:create Render a draft without saving GET /v1/admin/newsletters newsletters:read List (page and limit, optional status), newest scheduledAt first GET /v1/admin/newsletters/:id newsletters:read One newsletter with delivery counts GET /v1/admin/newsletters/:id/preview newsletters:read Render a saved newsletter DELETE /v1/admin/newsletters/:id newsletters:delete Cancel (soft delete). 422 while sending.

docs.title: Gaps
docs.text:
• A crash mid-send leaves the row in SENDING forever. Nothing resets it, and it cannot be deleted.
  • No unsubscribe. No API changes is_newsletter_subscribe (it defaults to true), and the email has no unsubscribe link.
  • No per-recipient record. A page that fails is not retried.
  • scheduledAt in the past is accepted and sent on the next tick.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: A simple help desk. Users send a question. Admins see all tickets and update their status.

docs.title: Model
docs.text:
support_tickets: user_id, topic, query (10–2,000 characters), status, timestamps and soft delete. See ERD.

  • Topics: BILLING, TECHNICAL, ACCOUNT, ASSESSMENT, FEEDBACK, OTHER.
  • Statuses: OPEN, IN_PROGRESS, RESOLVED, CLOSED.

docs.title: Lifecycle
docs.text:
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> OPEN: user creates ticket
    OPEN --> IN_PROGRESS: admin
    IN_PROGRESS --> RESOLVED: admin
    RESOLVED --> CLOSED: admin
    OPEN --> CLOSED: admin

This is the intended path. The code does not enforce it. An admin can set any status from any status.

docs.title: Endpoints
docs.text: Method and path Who Purpose POST /v1/support Any logged-in user (CLASS_B) Create a ticket with topic and query GET /v1/admin/support-tickets support_tickets:read List all tickets, newest first, page and limit (max 100) PATCH /v1/admin/support-tickets/:id support_tickets:update Set status

docs.title: Gaps
docs.text:
• Users cannot list or read their own tickets. There is only a create endpoint.
  • No replies, comments or assignee. Admins answer outside the system.
  • No email to the user or to support when a ticket is created or changes status.
  • The admin list has no filter by status or topic.
  • No transition rules (see lifecycle above).

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: A probe for load balancers, CI and deploy pipelines.

docs.title: Checks performed
docs.text:
GET /health (public, not versioned, no rate limit). HealthService.check runs three probes in parallel, each with a 2-second timeout:

Check How database SELECT 1 through TypeORM redis PING on the rate limiter's Redis client, so it matches what the limiter sees rabbitmq amqpConnection.connected (false until the link is up, because the module starts with wait: false)

docs.title: Responses
docs.text:
• All up → 200 with the usual envelope. data is { status: 'ok', uptime, checks: { database: 'up', redis: 'up', rabbitmq: 'up' } } and message is 'Service is healthy.'.
  • Any down → 503 with { success: false, message: 'One or more dependencies are unavailable.', checks, uptime }. The checks object names the dependency at fault.

A probe never throws. One dead dependency still produces a full report.

docs.title: Gaps
docs.text:
• The cache Redis client (src/config/redis/) is a separate connection and is not checked.
  • External services (SMTP, S3, LLM providers, code runners) are not checked.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: A thin wrapper around Amazon S3 (or any S3-compatible store) for files the backend needs to keep for a short time.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
StorageService (src/storage/storage.service.ts) uses @aws-sdk/client-s3 and has two methods:

  • putObject(key, buffer, contentType)
  • getObject(key) → Buffer
Env var Use AWS_REGION, AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY Required AWS_S3_BUCKET Required. The one bucket used. AWS_S3_ENDPOINT Optional. Points to MinIO or LocalStack for local development. Turns on path-style URLs.

docs.title: Current use
docs.text: Only the organization CSV invitation import uses it. The uploaded CSV is stored at org-invitations/<orgId>/<uuid>.csv. The background job then reads it back. See Organizations.

docs.title: Gaps
docs.text:
• Uploaded CSVs are never deleted. Add a bucket lifecycle rule or a delete call after import.
  • No delete, list or signed-URL methods.

docs.title: App controller
docs.text:
src/app.controller.ts has one route:

Method and path Auth Response GET /ping Public { success: true, message: 'Success.', data: 'OK' }

It only shows that the process is up and serving HTTP. It does not check any dependency. Use /health for that.

docs.text: Path What it does src/feature-flags/feature-flag.constants.ts Flag keys, defaults, isFlagOn, flagState src/feature-flags/feature-flags.service.ts enabledFor, list, get, update src/feature-flags/admin.controller.ts Feature flag admin API src/rate-limiter/policies.ts The three policies src/rate-limiter/algorithms.ts Lua token bucket src/rate-limiter/rate-limit.guard.ts Global guard src/rate-limiter/rate-limit.decorator.ts @RateLimit() src/rate-limiter/policy-resolver.ts Policy and key selection src/rate-limiter/stores.ts Redis store (fails open) src/stats/admin.service.ts All stats SQL src/newsletters/admin.service.ts and newsletters-dispatch.service.ts Newsletter CRUD and delivery src/schedulers/newsletter.scheduler.ts The minute cron src/support-tickets/ User and admin ticket endpoints src/health/ Health check src/storage/storage.service.ts S3 wrapper src/app.controller.ts /ping

docs.title: 1. Purpose
docs.text:
• Questions (src/assessments/questions/) hold the content people answer: the question bank, the three question types, and the code that saves AI-generated questions into an assessment.
  • Tags (src/assessments/tags/) are simple labels. Today they are only used to label assessment prompts in the prompt library.

How an assessment is built from questions is on Assessments. How questions are generated by AI is on AI Assessment Generation. How answers are graded is on Evaluation.

docs.title: 2. Key concepts
docs.text: Term Meaning Question bank The questions table plus one details table per type. Every question ever created or generated lives here. Snapshot A copy of a question placed in one assessment: a row in assessments_questions. It copies the text and the type-specific content as JSON (content). Question type mcq, coding or descriptive (QuestionType in src/common/enums/assessments.enums.ts). Stored as varchar, so a new type needs no Postgres enum migration. Topics Weighted labels on a question (questions.meta.topics), e.g. [{ name: "mvcc", weight: 0.6 }, ...]. Weights sum to 1. Copied onto the snapshot. Used by analytics. Checkpoint One idea a good descriptive answer must contain, with a weight. The answer key for descriptive questions. Test case An input and expected output for a coding question. Hidden cases are used for grading but never shown. Tag A label with a unique name and slug, and an isActive flag.

docs.title: 3. Data it uses
docs.text:
See the ERD for full columns. In short:

  • questions: type, question_text, meta (JSON, topics), created_by, soft delete.
  • mcq_question_details, coding_question_details, descriptive_question_details: one row per question, sharing the question's primary key (question_id). Only the table matching questions.type has a row.
  • assessments_questions: the snapshot. type, question_text, content (JSON), topics, correct_marks, incorrect_marks, order_index, section_id. Unique on (assessment_id, question_id).
  • tags, and assessment_prompt_tags (the join to assessment_prompts).
flowchart LR
    Q["questions"] --> MCQ["mcq_question_details"]
    Q --> COD["coding_question_details"]
    Q --> DES["descriptive_question_details"]
    Q -->|"copied into"| AQ["assessments_questions - snapshot"]
    AQ --> SEC["assessment_sections"]
    TAG["tags"] --> APT["assessment_prompt_tags"]
    APT --> AP["assessment_prompts"]

docs.title: 4. Question types
docs.text: The interfaces live in src/assessments/questions/interfaces/question-content.interface.ts. The snapshot's content column holds exactly one of these shapes, picked by type.

docs.title: 4.1 MCQ (McqQuestionContent)
docs.text:
Field Notes options 2–6 options, each { id, text }. id is an integer ≥ 1, unique within the question. Option text up to 500 chars. correctOptionId Must match one option's id. Exactly one correct answer. There is no multi-select type. explanation Optional, up to 5000 chars. AI-generated MCQs have none.

Question text: 10–1000 chars.

docs.title: 4.2 Coding (CodingQuestionContent)
docs.text:
Field Notes inputFormat, outputFormat, constraints Optional text, up to 5000 chars each. starterCode Object keyed by language, e.g. { python: "...", java: "...", cpp: "..." }. Each up to 20,000 chars. supportedLanguages Always the keys of starterCode. Allowed languages: python, java, cpp (CODING_LANGUAGES in src/ai/interfaces/generated-coding-question.interface.ts). timeLimitMs 100–10,000 on edit. Generated problems get 2000. memoryLimitMb 16–1024 on edit. Generated problems get 256. checkerType Only exact exists today (output compared line by line, ignoring trailing whitespace). testCases 1–50 cases of { input, expectedOutput, isHidden }.

The problem title is put at the top of questionText ("<title>\n\n<statement>"), because the content has no title field. The AI's reference solution is dropped before saving, so it can never reach a candidate. Defaults live in src/assessments/questions/coding-question.defaults.ts.

docs.title: 4.3 Descriptive (DescriptiveQuestionContent)
docs.text:
Field Notes checkpoints List of { id, description, weightage }. IDs unique. Weightages are positive integers that sum to exactly 100. maxWords Suggested answer length shown to the candidate. Not enforced when grading.

Rules in src/assessments/domain/descriptive-invariants.ts:

  • assertCheckpointWeights enforces the rules above. It runs when generated descriptive questions are saved.
  • normaliseWeightages rescales whatever weights the AI wrote to integers that sum to 100. Leftover points go to the largest remainders, and every checkpoint keeps at least 1.
  • scoreCheckpoints grades an answer: each completed checkpoint earns its share of the question's marks. An answer counts as correct at 60% or more (DESCRIPTIVE_CORRECT_THRESHOLD_PERCENT).

docs.title: 5. Question bank vs snapshots
docs.text:
Why snapshots? An assessment must not change under its participants. So when a question is placed into an assessment, its text and content are copied into assessments_questions. Later edits to the bank question do not affect assessments that already hold it.

Bank (questions + details) Snapshot (assessments_questions) Created by Admin create, admin generate, or AI section generation Manual add (POST /v1/assessments/:id/questions) or AI section generation Edited by Admins (/v1/admin/questions/:id) The assessment's manager (PUT /v1/assessments/:id/questions/:assessmentQuestionId), MCQ only, before publish Carries marks No Yes (correct_marks, incorrect_marks) Used for attempts and grading No Yes

Every AI-generated question is saved twice: once in the bank (owned by the user who asked) and once as the snapshot. Both are written in the same transaction by SectionQuestionWriter (src/assessments/questions/section-question-writer.ts):

sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant W as SectionGenerationWorker
    participant SQW as SectionQuestionWriter
    participant DB as PostgreSQL

    W->>DB: BEGIN
    W->>SQW: append(section, drafts, userId)
    SQW->>SQW: every draft must match the section type
    SQW->>DB: INSERT questions - one per draft
    SQW->>DB: INSERT type details rows - checks checkpoint weights for descriptive
    SQW->>DB: count existing snapshots in the section
    SQW->>DB: INSERT assessments_questions - section marks, next order_index
    SQW->>DB: increment assessments.curr_total_questions
    W->>DB: mark section job completed
    W->>DB: COMMIT

If anything fails, nothing from that section is saved.

docs.title: 6. Marking per question
docs.text:
• Each section has correct_marks and incorrect_marks (0–999.99). incorrect_marks is a positive number that is deducted for a wrong answer.
  • Each snapshot copies those marks when it is created. Scoring reads the snapshot's marks.
  • Manual add (POST /:id/questions) takes marks per item from the request instead.
  • Editing an assessment's marks (PATCH /v1/assessments/:id) rewrites the first section's marks and the marks on every snapshot of that assessment.
  • AI auto-mode defaults (AUTO_MODE_DEFAULT_MARKS in generation/generation.constants.ts): MCQ +1/0, coding +10/0, descriptive +5/0.
  • Descriptive answers can earn partial marks by checkpoint. MCQ is all or nothing. Coding grading is covered in Evaluation and Code Execution.

docs.title: 7.1 What tags are for
docs.text: Tags label assessment prompts so the public prompt library can be filtered (GET /v1/assessment-prompts/public?tags=...). They are linked through assessment_prompt_tags. Tags are not attached to questions or assessments today.

docs.title: 7.2 How tags are assigned
docs.text:
1. A platform admin creates tags (POST /v1/admin/tags). slug is derived from name unless given (lowercase, non-alphanumerics become -).
  2. A user creating or replacing an assessment prompt sends tagSlugs (up to 50, unique).
  3. AssessmentPromptsService.resolveTags looks the slugs up. Any unknown slug gives a 404.
  4. On PUT, removed links are soft-deleted and new links are inserted. A partial unique index keeps one live link per (prompt, tag).

docs.title: 7.3 Tag rules
docs.text:
1. name and slug must be unique. The service checks first and returns 409.
  2. Changing name regenerates the slug, unless a slug is sent.
  3. Delete is by slug and is a soft delete.
  4. isActive is a flag only. Inactive tags still show in lists unless the caller filters with is_active, and can still be assigned to prompts.

docs.title: 8. Business rules and validation
docs.text:
1. Admin create makes MCQs only. POST /v1/admin/questions always creates type = mcq. Coding and descriptive bank questions come only from AI generation.
  2. Option checks. HasUniqueOptionIds and IsCorrectOptionPresent (custom validators in dto/create-question.dto.ts) check that option IDs are unique and that correctOptionId is one of them. On partial update the pair is re-checked against the final state in the service.
  3. Edit refuses the wrong type's fields. Sending coding for an MCQ, or options for a coding question, is a 400 instead of being silently ignored.
  4. MCQ text limit is 1000, coding text limit is 10,000 (QUESTION_TEXT_MAX_LENGTH).
  5. Coding test cases need at least one visible case, and no two cases may share the same input.
  6. Starter code may only use known languages, each non-empty and up to 20,000 chars. The given languages become supportedLanguages, in canonical order.
  7. Descriptive questions cannot be edited through the admin API yet (400).
  8. Bank edits never touch snapshots. Fixing a bank question does not fix assessments that already hold it.
  9. Delete is soft. Snapshots keep pointing at the soft-deleted question.
  10. Testing environment. When NODE_ENV=testing no LLM runs: MCQ sections copy random bank MCQs, coding sections use a fixed "Sum of Two Integers" problem, descriptive sections use a fixed indexing question (coding-question.defaults.ts, descriptive-question.defaults.ts).

docs.title: 9. Endpoints summary
docs.text:
Full reference: API v1.

Method Path Permission Purpose POST /v1/admin/questions questions:create Create an MCQ in the bank POST /v1/admin/questions/generate questions:create Generate MCQs from a prompt (count 1–50) into the bank, inline GET /v1/admin/questions questions:read List with search, created_by, paging GET /v1/admin/questions/:id questions:read One question with its details PATCH /v1/admin/questions/:id questions:update Partial update (MCQ or coding) PUT /v1/admin/questions/:id/starter-code questions:update Replace coding starter code DELETE /v1/admin/questions/:id questions:delete Soft delete GET /v1/tags, /v1/tags/:id logged in List and read tags POST /v1/admin/tags tags:create Create tag GET /v1/admin/tags, /v1/admin/tags/:id tags:read Admin list and read PATCH /v1/admin/tags/:id tags:update Update tag DELETE /v1/admin/tags/:slug tags:delete Soft delete by slug

These are platform permissions, checked by @Permissions(...) (see RBAC).

The admin generate endpoint runs the LLM inside the HTTP request (no job). It is audited in llm_audit with job type GENERATE_QUESTIONS. It uses the model the admin's plan assigns. See AI Layer.

docs.title: 10. Async events
docs.text: None. Question and tag routes are synchronous. Questions created by the generation pipeline are written by the RabbitMQ section workers; see AI Assessment Generation.

docs.title: 11. Where the code lives
docs.text: Path What src/assessments/questions/admin.controller.ts, admin.service.ts Admin bank CRUD and inline generation src/assessments/questions/questions.service.ts Generators per section type, bank helpers (createBulk, findRandom) src/assessments/questions/section-question-writer.ts Saves generated drafts to bank + snapshot src/assessments/questions/interfaces/ Content, draft and meta interfaces src/assessments/questions/dto/ Request/response DTOs and option validators src/assessments/questions/coding-question.defaults.ts, descriptive-question.defaults.ts Defaults and testing stand-ins src/assessments/domain/descriptive-invariants.ts Checkpoint rules and scoring src/common/entities/question.entity.ts and *-question-details.entity.ts Bank entities src/common/entities/assessment-question.entity.ts Snapshot entity src/assessments/tags/ Tags module, public and admin controllers

docs.title: 12. Known gaps and TODOs
docs.text:
1. Tag uniqueness and soft delete clash. UQ_tags_name and UQ_tags_slug are plain unique indexes (src/common/entities/tag.entity.ts, migration 20260723000000-create-tags-table.ts). The service's duplicate check ignores soft-deleted rows. Re-creating a tag with the name of a deleted one passes the check and then hits the DB unique index.
  2. Inactive tags are not enforced. They can still be assigned to prompts and show in default lists.
  3. No user-facing bank. Only platform admins can list bank questions, yet manual assessment building needs bank question IDs.
  4. No admin create for coding or descriptive questions, and no edit for descriptive questions.
  5. Old flow saves bank rows outside the snapshot transaction. QuestionsService.generateFromPrompt saves bank questions first, and the older completeGeneration writes snapshots in a second transaction, so a failure in between leaves orphan bank rows.
  6. A stray console.log in QuestionsService.generateFromPrompt (questions.service.ts:59) bypasses the logger.

docs.title: 1. Purpose
docs.text:
RBAC means role-based access control. Users are not given rights one by one. A user holds a role, and the role grants a list of permissions.

Authentication answers "who is calling?". RBAC answers "may this caller do this action?".

TestFlow has two kinds of roles that share one permission list:

  • Platform roles, such as super_admin. They apply to the whole product and mostly guard the /v1/admin/... routes.
  • Organization roles, such as org_admin. A user holds one of these per organization, through their membership. They apply only when a request acts inside that organization. See Organizations.

docs.title: 2. Key terms
docs.text: Term Meaning Resource A kind of thing, such as questions, users or org_members. The list is the RbacResource enum in src/common/enums/identity.enums.ts. Action What you do to a resource: read, create, update or delete. (upload and export are in the enum but no resource uses them.) Permission key resource:action, for example questions:update. One row in permissions. Role A named set of permissions, for example super_admin or org_member. One row in roles. Scope platform or organization (RbacScope). It says where a role is held. Platform role Held through users_roles. Checked on normal (personal) requests. Org role Held through organization_members.role_id. Checked when the request acts in an organization. Built-in role A role seeded by the app, with organization_id = NULL. All organizations share the built-in org roles.

docs.title: 3. Data it uses
docs.text:
See the ERD for the full columns. Short version:

erDiagram
    users ||--o{ users_roles : "holds platform role"
    roles ||--o{ users_roles : "assigned via"
    roles ||--o{ role_permissions : "grants"
    permissions ||--o{ role_permissions : "granted via"
    users ||--o{ organization_members : "member of"
    roles ||--o{ organization_members : "org role"
Table Notes roles key, scope, organization_id. Built-in keys are unique among live rows with organization_id IS NULL. A custom org role would be unique per (organization_id, key), but no API creates custom org roles yet. permissions key is unique, plus an optional description. role_permissions Links a role to a permission. It has a meta jsonb column with implicitPermissions, but no code reads it. users_roles Links a user to a platform role. Soft-deletable. organization_members role_id holds the member's org role. See Organizations.

docs.title: 4.1 Built-in roles
docs.text:
These are seeded by src/seeders/role.seeder.ts.

Role key Scope What it is for super_admin platform Full platform admin. It is granted every permission key in the catalog. beta_tester platform Grants no permissions. Its only use is to switch on feature flags that target it (see Platform services). org_owner organization Owner of an organization. Exactly one per organization, set when the organization is created. org_admin organization Manages the organization, its members and its assessments. org_member organization Normal member. The role every invite gives.

super_admin and the three org roles are protected. The admin API will not rename or delete them. beta_tester is not protected.

docs.title: 4.2 The permission catalog
docs.text:
The source of truth is RBAC_RESOURCE_ACTIONS in src/identity/rbac/constants/resource-actions.constant.ts. The seeder creates one permissions row for each pair. CRUD means read, create, update and delete.

Resource Actions Used for users CRUD Admin user list and platform role changes roles CRUD Admin role routes permissions CRUD Admin role-permission routes and access check questions CRUD Admin question bank plans CRUD Admin plans features read Plan features support_tickets read, update Admin support tickets tags CRUD Admin tags assessment_prompts CRUD Admin prompts newsletters read, create, delete Admin newsletters ai_models CRUD Admin AI models llm_audits read Admin LLM audit logs organizations read, create, update Admin organization routes org_settings read, update Organization details, inside an org org_members CRUD Members and invitations, inside an org org_assessments CRUD Organization assessments, inside an org org_billing read, update Organization subscription and usage, inside an org payments, subscriptions, usage read Admin views of commerce records assessment_attempts read, update Review attempts (list, reject). Shared by platform and org roles. assessment_attempt_responses read Read the answers of an attempt. Shared by platform and org roles. assessments read Admin list of all assessments stats read Admin overview numbers feature_flags read, update Admin feature flags

An old *:* "wildcard" permission may still be in older databases. The guards do not treat it as a wildcard. SuperAdminPermissionsSeeder replaces it with explicit grants and removes it.

docs.title: 4.3 Default grants for org roles
docs.text:
These come from ORG_ROLE_DEFAULT_PERMISSIONS in the same constants file.

Permission org_owner org_admin org_member org_settings:read yes yes yes org_settings:update yes yes org_members:read yes yes yes org_members:create / update / delete yes yes org_assessments:read yes yes yes org_assessments:create yes yes yes org_assessments:update / delete yes yes org_billing:read yes yes org_billing:update yes assessment_attempts:read / update yes yes assessment_attempt_responses:read yes yes

The org seeder only adds missing grants. It never removes any. So if a platform admin changes an org role's permissions through the API, a later npm run seed keeps the change. Built-in org roles are shared, so a change applies to every organization at once.

docs.title: 4.4 Seeding order
docs.text:
npm run seed runs src/seeders/index.ts in this order:

  1. RolesSeeder: create the built-in roles if they are missing.
  2. PermissionsSeeder: create a permission row for every catalog pair.
  3. SuperAdminPermissionsSeeder: grant super_admin every catalog key and remove the legacy *:*. Runs in one transaction.
  4. OrgRolePermissionsSeeder: add the default org grants. Runs in one transaction.
  5. Then the features, plans, AI models and feature flags seeders.

After seeding, create the first admin with npm run bootstrap-admin (see Auth).

docs.title: 5. Decorators
docs.text:
Decorator File Meaning @Roles(...keys) src/identity/rbac/decorators/roles.decorator.ts The caller must hold at least one of these platform roles. @Permissions(...keys) src/identity/rbac/decorators/permissions.decorator.ts The caller must have all these permissions. Checked against platform roles on a personal request, or against the org role on an org request. @OrgPermissions(...keys) src/identity/rbac/decorators/org-permissions.decorator.ts Extra permissions checked only when the request acts in an organization. A personal request skips them. @Public() src/common/decorators/public.decorator.ts Skip authentication. See Auth. @OrgScoped(), @OrgHeaderScoped() src/organizations/decorators/ Make the request act in an organization. See Organizations.

When the handler and the controller both have the same decorator, the handler's value wins (getAllAndOverride). The two lists are not merged.

Today @Roles is used in only one place: @Roles('super_admin') on POST /v1/admin/questions/generate in src/assessments/questions/admin.controller.ts. Everything else uses permissions.

docs.title: 6. How the guards decide
docs.text:
All guards are global (APP_GUARD in src/app.module.ts) and run in this order:

JwtAuthGuard → RateLimitGuard → RolesGuard → OrgContextGuard → PermissionGuard

docs.title: 6.1 RolesGuard
docs.text:
File: src/identity/rbac/guards/roles.guard.ts.

  1. Read @Roles from the handler, or from the class if the handler has none. If it is empty, allow.
  2. If there is no request.user, deny (403).
  3. Load the user's platform role keys (AccessControlService.getUserRoleKeys).
  4. If the user holds any required role, allow. Otherwise: 403 Insufficient role.

RolesGuard runs before OrgContextGuard. It never looks at org roles.

docs.title: 6.2 PermissionGuard
docs.text:
File: src/identity/rbac/guards/permission.guard.ts.

  1. Read @Permissions (required) and @OrgPermissions (org-only). If both are empty, allow.
  2. If there is no request.user, deny (403).
  3. Look at request.org. OrgContextGuard sets it when the request acts in an organization.
  4. Build the list to check:
    • Org request (request.org is set): @Permissions plus @OrgPermissions.
    • Personal request: @Permissions only.
  5. Check each key, one at a time:
    • Org request: roleHasPermission(org.roleId, key). This is the member's org role only.
    • Personal request: userHasPermission(userId, key). This means any of the user's platform roles.
  6. The first missing key fails with 403 Missing permission: <key>.
flowchart TD
    A["Request reaches PermissionGuard"] --> B{"Any Permissions or OrgPermissions metadata?"}
    B -- no --> OK["Allow"]
    B -- yes --> C{"request.user set?"}
    C -- no --> F0["403 Forbidden"]
    C -- yes --> D{"request.org set?"}
    D -- "yes, org request" --> E["Check Permissions and OrgPermissions against the member's org role"]
    D -- "no, personal request" --> G["Check Permissions only, against all platform roles"]
    E --> H{"Every key granted?"}
    G --> H
    H -- yes --> OK
    H -- no --> F1["403 Missing permission"]

docs.title: 6.3 The two SQL checks
docs.text:
Both are in src/identity/rbac/services/access-control.service.ts, and both are a single COUNT query:

  • userHasPermission: users_roles → roles → role_permissions → permissions, filtered by user id and key.
  • roleHasPermission: role_permissions → permissions, filtered by role id and key.

There is no cache. Each key on a route costs one query, on every request. A role or permission change takes effect on the very next request.

docs.title: 7. Platform roles and org roles together
docs.text:
This is the part people most often get wrong:

  1. Inside an organization, platform roles do not count. If a route acts in an org, @Permissions is checked against the member's org role. Even a super_admin gets 403 (or 404 from OrgContextGuard if they are not a member).
  2. Outside an organization, org roles do not count. A personal request only looks at platform roles.
  3. Some keys are shared. assessment_attempts:* and assessment_attempt_responses:read are granted to super_admin (platform) and to org_owner / org_admin (org). The same route checks whichever role applies to the request.
  4. @OrgPermissions adds a check only in org mode. For example, POST /v1/assessments has @OrgHeaderScoped() and @OrgPermissions('org_assessments:create'). A personal request needs nothing extra. A request with the x-organization-id header needs that org permission.
  5. Some checks live in services, not guards. For example, editing an org assessment needs org_assessments:update unless you created it. The route checks org_assessments:read, and AssessmentsService checks the rest (ORG_ASSESSMENT_MANAGE_PERMISSIONS in src/assessments/assessments.constants.ts). See Assessments.
  6. GET /v1/orgs returns each org with the caller's role and the permission keys it grants, so the frontend can show or hide buttons. The list is empty while the membership or the org is suspended.

docs.title: 8. Admin endpoints
docs.text:
All of these are in src/identity/rbac/admin.controller.ts under /v1/admin, with the CLASS_C rate limit. They only work on built-in roles (organization_id IS NULL), of both scopes. The API reference has the full details.

Method and path Permission Purpose GET /roles roles:read List built-in roles GET /roles/:roleKey roles:read One role POST /roles roles:create Create a role. Body: { key, scope? }. scope defaults to platform. PATCH /roles/:roleKey roles:update Rename a role ({ key }) DELETE /roles/:roleKey roles:delete Soft-delete a role GET /roles/:roleKey/permissions permissions:read The keys a role grants PUT /roles/:roleKey/permissions permissions:update Replace all of a role's keys. Body: { permissions: [...] }. POST /roles/:roleKey/permissions/:permissionKey permissions:create Grant one key DELETE /roles/:roleKey/permissions/:permissionKey permissions:delete Revoke one key GET /permissions permissions:read The full catalog, sorted by key POST /access-check permissions:read { roleKey, permissionKey } returns { allowed }

Platform role assignment to users is on the user admin routes. See Auth.

docs.title: 9. Business rules and edge cases
docs.text:
1. Protected roles (super_admin, org_owner, org_admin, org_member) cannot be renamed or deleted (403).
  2. You cannot delete a role that you hold (403).
  3. You cannot change the permissions of a role that you hold, unless you are super_admin (403). So a super_admin can edit super_admin's own permissions, and could remove their own access.
  4. You cannot add or remove your own platform roles (see Auth).
  5. Role keys must be unique among live built-in roles (409). Up to 100 characters.
  6. PUT .../permissions with an unknown key fails with 404 and lists the missing keys. Nothing changes.
  7. PUT .../permissions with an empty list removes every grant from the role.
  8. Changing a built-in org role changes it for every organization.
  9. POST /roles can create a built-in role with scope organization. Org admins can then give it to members with PATCH /v1/orgs/:orgUid/members/:userId, because that route accepts any built-in org role except org_owner. A new role starts with no permissions, so a platform admin must grant some first.

docs.title: 10. Async events
docs.text: None. RBAC is fully synchronous and uses the database only.

docs.title: 11. Where the code lives
docs.text: Path What src/identity/rbac/guards/roles.guard.ts RolesGuard src/identity/rbac/guards/permission.guard.ts PermissionGuard src/identity/rbac/decorators/ @Roles, @Permissions, @OrgPermissions src/identity/rbac/services/access-control.service.ts The permission queries src/identity/rbac/services/user-roles.service.ts holdsRole, isSuperAdmin src/identity/rbac/constants/resource-actions.constant.ts Permission catalog and default org grants src/identity/rbac/admin.controller.ts, admin.service.ts Admin role routes src/common/enums/identity.enums.ts RbacResource, RbacAction, SystemRole, OrgRole, RbacScope src/seeders/role.seeder.ts, permission.seeder.ts, super-admin-permissions.seeder.ts, org-role-permissions.seeder.ts Seed data tests/unit/identity/rbac/ Unit tests

docs.title: 12. Known gaps and TODOs
docs.text:
1. PUT /roles/:roleKey/permissions is not wrapped in a transaction (src/identity/rbac/admin.service.ts, replaceRolePermissions). It deletes all grants and then inserts the new ones. If the insert fails, the role is left with no permissions.
  2. Mixed delete styles. PUT hard-deletes role_permissions rows, but DELETE .../permissions/:key soft-deletes them.
  3. Deleting a role leaves its links behind. DELETE /roles/:roleKey soft-deletes the role but not its users_roles or role_permissions rows. AccessControlService.getUserRoleKeys then reads ur.role.key. If TypeORM leaves the soft-deleted role out of the join, role is undefined and the code crashes. This affects RolesGuard (the @Roles route) for users who held the deleted role. Needs a test.
  4. No caching. Every permission check is a database query.
  5. role_permissions.meta.implicitPermissions is never read. For example, update does not imply read.
  6. No API for custom org roles. The schema supports roles with an organization_id, but nothing creates them.
  7. RbacAction.UPLOAD and EXPORT are defined but unused.
  8. @Roles('super_admin') uses a string literal instead of SystemRole.SUPER_ADMIN.

docs.title: 1. Purpose
docs.text:
Most of TestFlow works over plain HTTP. Background work (AI generation, evaluation) is followed by polling GET /v1/jobs/:id. The WebSocket layer is used only where polling would be slow or clumsy:

  • AI assistant chat. The client sends a message and gets the assistant's answer back on the same socket.
  • Running code during an attempt. Test-case results stream back one by one as they finish.
  • Push notices for background work. Today there is one: the result of a bulk organization invitation import.

The layer uses Socket.IO through NestJS's @nestjs/websockets package. All of it lives in src/events/.

docs.title: 2. Key concepts
docs.text: Term Meaning Gateway EventsGateway, the one NestJS WebSocket gateway. It accepts connections and handles incoming messages. Handshake The first request a Socket.IO client makes. The JWT is checked here, and only here. Room A named group of sockets. The server can send to a room instead of to a single socket. User room user:<userId>. Every socket a user opens joins it, so one emit reaches all of that user's tabs. requestId A client-made id (letters, digits, -, _, max 64 characters) sent with a message and echoed back in replies and errors. It lets the client match replies to requests. exception The standard Socket.IO event name NestJS uses for error frames.

docs.title: 3. Data
docs.text:
The gateway stores nothing in the database. State is kept in memory:

  • client.data.userId: the authenticated user for a socket.
  • ConnectionManager: a Map<userId, Set<socket>> of open sockets. It has isOnline(userId) and get(userId) helpers, but no other code uses them today.

AI conversations and attempts are stored by their own modules. See AI Assistant and Attempts.

docs.title: 4.1 Connection and authentication
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant C as Client
    participant G as EventsGateway
    participant E as EventService
    participant CM as ConnectionManager

    C->>G: connect to /socket.io with token
    G->>E: extractToken
    E-->>G: token from auth, query or header
    G->>E: authenticateUser
    E->>E: jwt.verify with JWT_ACCESS_SECRET
    alt token missing or invalid
        G-->>C: emit exception Invalid token
        G->>C: disconnect
    else token valid
        G->>G: client.data.userId = sub
        G->>G: join room user:userId
        G->>CM: add userId and socket
    end

The client can send the access token in one of three ways. They are checked in this order:

Order Client code Where the server reads it 1 io(url, { auth: { token } }) handshake.auth.token (recommended) 2 io(url, { query: { token } }) handshake.query.token 3 io(url, { extraHeaders: { Authorization: 'Bearer ...' } }) handshake.headers.authorization

Important details:

  • The token is the normal access token from login. It is checked once, at connect time. A socket stays open even after the token expires. The client should reconnect with a fresh token after refresh.
  • The handshake only checks the JWT signature and expiry. It does not check that the account is still active. The HTTP JwtAuthGuard does check this.
  • WsJwtGuard (src/events/guards/WsJwtGuard.guard.ts) runs on each message handler. It does not re-verify the JWT. It only checks that the handshake set client.data.userId. If not, it throws WsException('Unauthorized').
  • On disconnect, the socket is removed from ConnectionManager.

docs.title: 4.2 AI conversation message
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant C as Client
    participant G as EventsGateway
    participant R as ConversationRouterService
    participant A as ConversationAssistantService

    C->>G: ai.conversation.message with requestId, conversationId, content
    G->>G: WsJwtGuard and validation pipe
    G->>R: resolveAiConversationMessage
    R->>A: answer
    A-->>R: answer content
    R-->>G: reply
    G-->>C: ai.conversation.message with requestId and content

The reply goes back to the sending socket only, under the same event name. An LLM answer takes several seconds, so a client may have more than one message in flight. It uses requestId to match each reply.

docs.title: 4.3 Code run
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant C as Client
    participant G as EventsGateway
    participant S as CodeRunService
    participant X as Code runner

    C->>G: code.run with requestId, attemptUid, questionId, language, code, mode
    G->>S: start with a sink bound to this socket
    S->>S: check attempt, question, language, one run at a time, 5s cooldown
    S-->>C: code.run.started with total
    loop each visible test case in samples mode
        S->>X: execute
        X-->>S: output
        S-->>C: code.run.case with result
    end
    S-->>C: code.run.completed with passed and total
    Note over S,C: on runner error, code.run.failed instead

If the run is refused before it starts (bad attempt, wrong language, a run already in progress, or cooldown), the client gets an exception frame, not code.run.failed. See Code Execution for how runners work.

docs.title: 4.4 Push to a user
docs.text:
Any module can import EventsModule and call:

eventsGateway.emitToUser(userId, eventName, data)

This emits to the room user:<userId>, so every open tab of that user receives it. Today only the organizations module uses it.

docs.title: 5. Lifecycle
docs.text:
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Handshake: client connects
    Handshake --> Rejected: no token or bad token
    Rejected --> [*]: exception then disconnect
    Handshake --> Connected: token valid, joined user room
    Connected --> Connected: messages and events
    Connected --> [*]: client or server disconnect

docs.title: 6.1 Client → server messages
docs.text:
Event Payload Validation Reply ai.conversation.message { requestId, conversationId, content } requestId and conversationId: [A-Za-z0-9_-], max 64. content: string, max 4,000. ai.conversation.message to the sender code.run { requestId, attemptUid, questionId, language, code, mode, stdin? } attemptUid: UUID v4. questionId: int ≥ 1. language: one of the coding languages. mode: samples or custom. code and stdin: max 50,000 characters. code.run.* events to the sender

DTOs: src/events/dto/conversation-message.dto.ts and src/assessments/attempts/code-run/run-code.dto.ts.

docs.title: 6.2 Server → client events
docs.text:
This is the full list, found by searching every emit and emitToUser call in src/.

Event Payload Triggered by Sent to exception { status: 'error', message, errors?, requestId?, retryAfterMs? } Bad handshake token, failed guard, failed validation, or any error thrown in a handler The one socket ai.conversation.message { requestId, conversationId, userId, content, sentAt } Reply to the client's ai.conversation.message (EventsGateway.handleAiConversationMessage) The sending socket code.run.started { requestId, mode, total } CodeRunService accepted the run The sending socket code.run.case { requestId, index, input, expectedOutput, passed, status, stdout, stderr, exitCode, timeMs, memoryKb, outputTruncated } One visible test case finished (samples mode only) The sending socket code.run.completed { requestId, mode, passed?, total?, output? } (samples: passed, total. custom: output) The run finished The sending socket code.run.failed { requestId, reason, message } The runner failed mid-run (for example unavailable or busy). Results already sent still count. The sending socket org.invitations.import.settled Completed: { jobId, status: 'completed', invited, skipped, failed } (counts). Failed: { jobId, status: 'failed', reason } OrganizationInvitationImportService.run after a CSV import job finishes (src/organizations/services/organization-invitation-import.service.ts) Room user:<uploaderId>

Code-run payload types are in src/assessments/attempts/code-run/code-run-events.interface.ts. The import event name is INVITATION_IMPORT_SETTLED_EVENT in src/organizations/organizations.constants.ts. See Organizations for the import flow.

docs.title: 6.3 Error frames
docs.text:
All errors go out as the exception event. Two pieces shape them:

  • wsValidationPipe (src/events/pipes/ws-validation.pipe.ts): a ValidationPipe with whitelist, forbidNonWhitelisted and transform. Unknown fields are rejected. A failure becomes { status: 'error', message: 'Validation failed', errors: [...] }.
  • WsExceptionFilter (src/events/filters/ws-exception.filter.ts): catches everything. It:
    • maps domain errors to HTTP exceptions with the shared asHttpException mapper, then turns them into { status: 'error', message };
    • turns class-validator message arrays into message: 'Validation failed' plus errors;
    • copies retryAfterMs when present (for example the code-run cooldown);
    • adds requestId from the raw incoming frame, but only if it passes the same pattern and length rules as the DTO. This is because the frame may have failed validation.

The socket stays open after an error frame. Only a bad handshake disconnects.

docs.title: 7. Endpoints summary
docs.text: There are no REST endpoints. The Socket.IO server is mounted on the same HTTP server at path /socket.io. CORS is open to every origin (origin: '*'). Security relies on the JWT, not on origin checks.

docs.title: 8. Async events
docs.text:
The gateway does not consume RabbitMQ. A RabbitMQ consumer can push to a user through emitToUser. The invitation import consumer does this.

Background jobs for AI generation, evaluation and roadmaps do not emit socket events. Clients poll GET /v1/jobs/:id (see Jobs and Schedulers).

docs.title: 9. Scaling notes
docs.text:
• No Redis adapter. main.ts uses the default in-memory Socket.IO adapter. A room exists only inside one Node process.
  • What this means for emitToUser. With more than one app instance, the push only reaches sockets connected to the instance that emits. For the invitation import, the emitting instance is the one running the RabbitMQ consumer (CONSUMER=true), which may not be the instance holding the user's socket. Clients should treat the push as a hint and still poll the job.
  • Request and reply handlers are fine. ai.conversation.message and code.run reply on the same socket, so they work on any number of instances. A load balancer still needs sticky sessions if clients can fall back to HTTP long-polling.
  • Code-run limits are per instance. The "one run at a time" and 5-second cooldown rules are kept in memory in CodeRunService. A user connected to two instances could get around them.
  • To scale out properly, add @socket.io/redis-adapter (a new package, which needs team approval) and a custom IoAdapter in main.ts.

docs.title: 10. Where the code lives
docs.text: Path What it does src/events/events.gateway.ts Gateway: connect, disconnect, ai.conversation.message, code.run, emitToUser src/events/events.service.ts Token extraction and JWT verification for the handshake src/events/connection-manager.service.ts In-memory map of user → sockets src/events/conversation-router.service.ts Routes chat messages to the AI assistant src/events/guards/WsJwtGuard.guard.ts Per-message "is this socket authenticated" check src/events/pipes/ws-validation.pipe.ts Validation pipe for message bodies src/events/filters/ws-exception.filter.ts Turns any error into an exception frame src/events/interfaces/authenticated-socket.interface.ts AuthenticatedSocket type and userRoom() helper src/assessments/attempts/code-run/ Code-run service, DTO and event types

docs.title: 11. Known gaps and TODOs
docs.text:
• No account-status check at handshake. A deactivated user with a still-valid access token can open a socket. EventService injects UsersService but never uses it.
  • Token is never re-checked. A socket opened with a token stays authenticated until it disconnects.
  • Single-instance only. There is no Redis adapter, so emitToUser does not work across instances (see section 9).
  • Only one push event. Generation, evaluation and roadmap jobs could push completion events instead of being polled, but they do not.
  • ConnectionManager is mostly unused. It tracks sockets, but nothing reads isOnline or get.
